title: Auth, sessions, 2FA & RBAC
body:
## Context
CandleViewer is a private, self-hosted trading terminal reached only over Tailscale, operated by one owner plus a few account managers who can move real money on Bybit USDT linear perpetuals. Everything else in the product — accounts and API keys (E27), OMS and order placement (E29), trade-group fan-out (E34), admin screens (E42) — is gated by the identity, session and permission machinery built here. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 places **E09 in train R0, Sprint 03–Sprint 04, area/auth-rbac, backend modules M18 (auth/RBAC) and M19 (audit)**, 34 points, and §11.1 records the edges `E03 → E09`, `E09 → E10`, `E09 → E27`, `E09 → E42`; §11.2 puts E09 at the head of the trading critical path `E09 → E27 → E29 → E32 → E34 → E43 → E44`. Nothing that touches money can be built before this Epic lands.

The design is already specified and normative: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 (`users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`) and §3.10.1 (`audit_log`, hash-chained, append-only, `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE`); `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15 (`User`, `Session`, generated `Permission` enum); `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/auth/*`, `/users*`, `/invites/{inviteToken}`, `/admin/audit*`, and the `x-rbac.permissions` blocks that are the single canonical permission registry); `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3 and §9.5 (first-frame `auth` → `auth_ok`, in-place re-auth, mid-connection revocation); `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10 (`PasswordAuth`, `TotpAuth`) and P8 "server-side authority for RBAC, risk and scoping".

This Epic implements that specification end-to-end: Argon2id passwords with lockout, mandatory TOTP with recovery codes, rotating server-side sessions with idle lock and absolute expiry, step-up re-authentication for dangerous actions, invite-based user creation, deny-by-default RBAC enforced on every route by a single policy decision point, Tailscale-only reachability enforcement, and the append-only tamper-evident audit writer that every later Epic emits into.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Stories (domain ONB, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §1)**
- US-ONB-001 Password sign-in (Must) — E09-S01
- US-ONB-002 TOTP second factor, US-ONB-003 TOTP enrolment & recovery codes (Must) — E09-S02
- US-ONB-004 Session lifetime & idle lock, US-ONB-009 Sign-out everywhere (Must/Should) — E09-S03
- US-ONB-005 Step-up re-authentication, US-ONB-010 Owner-initiated TOTP reset (Must/Should) — E09-S04
- US-ONB-006 Invite-based user creation (Must) — E09-S05
- US-ONB-007 Guided first-run for a new manager (Should) — E09-S06
- US-ONB-008 Tailscale-only reachability enforcement (Must) — E09-T04
- SR-023 Break-glass offline owner recovery (security requirement, no user story) — E09-S11, added 2026-10-15 (#2119)

**Tasks / spike**
- E09-K01 Spike: token, session-rotation and revocation model (ADR)
- E09-T01 Postgres migration for the identity, session, MFA and RBAC tables (`21-database-schema.md` §3.1)
- E09-T02 Append-only hash-chained audit writer (M19) + `GET /admin/audit`, `POST /admin/audit/verify`
- E09-T03 RBAC policy decision point, generated permission vocabulary, deny-by-default route enforcement + WS `auth_ok`/revocation
- E09-T04 Tailscale-only reachability self-check and CIDR guard

**Screens/components consumed** (`18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.1): SCR-001 Login, SCR-002 TOTP challenge, SCR-003 TOTP enrolment, SCR-004 Forced password change, SCR-005 Session expired/re-auth modal, SCR-006 Step-up modal, SCR-017 Manager/viewer onboarding, SCR-019 Setup checklist, SCR-111/SCR-112 Profile & security settings, SCR-123 Admin invite user, SCR-149 Admin re-auth gate, SCR-154 Permission denied; CMP-200 AuthCard, CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-202 PasswordStrengthMeter, CMP-203 RequirementChecklist, CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-205 QrCode, CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList, CMP-207 BuildFooter.

**Tables**: `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`, `audit_log`.

## Out of scope
- WebAuthn/passkey enrolment (schema columns exist in `mfa_methods`; flows reserved at SCR-007..009 for a later Epic).
- Bybit API-key storage, envelope encryption and key rotation — **E27**.
- Admin user-management screens beyond invite/reset (user list, role editing UI, audit browser UI) — **E42**; this Epic ships the APIs they consume.
- Risk caps, freeze and kill-switch semantics on `user_account_access` — **E39**.
- Pen-test and hardening remediation — **E43**; live-enablement gating — **E44**.
- Android or any non-web client.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A full identity lifecycle works end to end
  Given the owner issues an invite for role manager
  When the invitee redeems it, sets a password, enrols TOTP and signs in
  Then they hold exactly the manager role, zero account bindings, and every step is in the audit log

Scenario: Deny-by-default holds across the whole surface
  Given the route inventory of 22-api-openapi.yaml
  When the RBAC conformance test enumerates every route and calls it as a viewer
  Then no route is reachable without an explicit permission declaration and unlisted routes fail the build

Scenario: A stolen session cannot escalate
  Given a valid manager session cookie replayed from another device
  When it attempts an owner-only action such as TOTP reset or key rotation
  Then the action is denied with 403, audited at high severity, and no state changes

Scenario: Audit log cannot be rewritten
  Given an operator with the application database role
  When they attempt UPDATE or DELETE on audit_log
  Then the statement is rejected and POST /admin/audit/verify still reports an intact hash chain

Scenario: The app refuses to be publicly reachable
  Given the backend is misconfigured to bind 0.0.0.0
  When it starts
  Then it comes up read-only with a blocking banner, order placement disabled, and a Prometheus gauge set to the failing state
```

## Technical notes / design
Module **M18** (`services/api/auth/`: password, totp, sessions, scopes) and **M19** (audit) per `20-architecture.md` §3.10 and its repo layout. Passwords: Argon2id, `m=65536,t=3,p=4`, per-user pepper derived from the KEK-held secret, constant-time verification, 5 failures → 15 min lockout, uniform failure messaging (no user enumeration). Sessions are server-side rows, never JWT-in-localStorage; the access token is a short-lived bearer used for the WS first-frame `auth`, the refresh token lives in an HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict/Secure cookie and rotates on every refresh, with reuse of a rotated token revoking the whole family (`auth.refresh_reuse_detected`, severity critical). RBAC is one policy decision point consulted by a FastAPI dependency on every route; the permission vocabulary is generated from `x-rbac.permissions` in the OpenAPI document by `tools/rbac/generate.py` and cross-checked against the database seed and `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.2 by the `rbac_vocabulary_single_source` contract test.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85% on `services/api/auth`), contract tests against `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS handshake schemas, integration tests on a real Postgres with the migration applied (owner-floor trigger, audit trigger, rotation family revocation), E2E Playwright for login → TOTP → workspace, lock/unlock, invite redemption and 403, abuse-case tests (privilege escalation, replay, enumeration timing), load test for login throttling, axe-core on every auth screen.

## Security notes
This is the Epic where the STRIDE model required by `30-release-roadmap.md` §7 ("STRIDE models complete for E03, E08, E09") is produced and signed off by the Security engineer. Data classification: `password_hash`, `secret_enc`, `code_hash`, refresh tokens and invite tokens are SECRET and must never be logged or returned; `ip`, `user_agent`, `email`, `tailscale_node` are PII and are redacted in structured logs. Abuse cases exercised manually before Done: privilege escalation via role tampering, step-up bypass, recovery-code brute force, refresh-token replay, audit tampering.

## Accessibility notes
Every auth surface is WCAG 2.2 AA: labelled fields with programmatic error association, `aria-live` announcement of code errors and lockouts, keyboard-only completion of enrolment including a text-equivalent TOTP secret alongside the QR, visible focus, no information by colour alone, and no time limit that cannot be extended other than the security-justified session expiry (documented as an exception per `05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Argon2id parameters are tuned so a verification stays within ~150 ms on the target host; the RBAC decision adds < 1 ms p99 per request (in-process, cached role/permission resolution with revocation checked per request); audit writes are asynchronous but durable, and never on the order-submission hot path's critical latency budget per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
Metrics: `auth_login_attempts_total{outcome}`, `auth_lockouts_total`, `auth_mfa_failures_total{reason}`, `auth_refresh_reuse_total`, `auth_sessions_active`, `rbac_denials_total{permission}`, `audit_chain_verified` gauge, `net_binding_safe` gauge. Structured logs carry `request_id`, `session_id`, `user_id` and never secrets. Grafana panel "Auth & access" plus alerts on refresh-reuse, chain-verification failure and unsafe binding.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2: all children Done, Epic-level AC verified end to end, coverage ≥85% backend, docs reconciled, axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass on auth screens, STRIDE finalised with Security sign-off, QA regression pass, demoed to the Owner, retro notes filed.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E03** (CI/CD, secrets management, migration tooling). Blocks **E10** (app shell), **E27** (accounts & key vault), **E42** (admin screens), and transitively the whole trading critical path.

## Branch
`feat/e09-auth-rbac` (children branch from and merge into `main` individually per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`).

## References
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3, §7, §11; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §1 ONB; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.1; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001..006, 016..019, 111, 112, 123, 149, 154; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-200..207; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1, §3.10.1; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3, §9.5; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15; `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

```mermaid
graph TD
  K01[E09-K01 Spike: session & token model] --> T01[E09-T01 Identity/RBAC migration]
  T01 --> T02[E09-T02 Audit writer M19]
  T01 --> S01[E09-S01 Password sign-in]
  T02 --> S01
  S01 --> S02[E09-S02 TOTP + recovery codes]
  S02 --> S03[E09-S03 Sessions, idle lock, revocation]
  S02 --> T03[E09-T03 RBAC decision point]
  S03 --> S04[E09-S04 Step-up re-auth & TOTP reset]
  T03 --> S04
  S04 --> S05[E09-S05 Invite-based user creation]
  S05 --> S06[E09-S06 First-run checklist]
  T04[E09-T04 Tailscale reachability guard] --> S01
```


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Spike: session, token rotation and revocation model (ADR)
body:
## Context
Two normative documents describe the session model at slightly different levels: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4 (server-side `sessions` rows, refresh-token hash, 12 h absolute, 30 min idle, rotation family revocation) and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1 (`Session` with `idle_expires_at`, `refresh_expires_at` 7 d, `elevated_until`). `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3 additionally requires a **bearer access token presented in the WS first frame**, refreshed in place at `expires_at - 60 s` without tearing down subscriptions, while `20-architecture.md` §5 states "no JWT in localStorage". US-ONB-004 also requires an idle lock that must *not* tear down WS subscriptions.

These constraints interact: a cookie-only design cannot feed the WS first frame; a long-lived access token defeats revocation; a short one causes refresh storms. Getting it wrong is expensive — E27, E29, E34 and E42 all build on the resulting session semantics. The Architect has asked for a timeboxed decision before E09-T01 freezes the schema.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Timebox: 3 days.** Answer, with evidence: (1) access-token format — opaque server-side handle vs signed JWT with `sid`/`jti` — given that revocation must be effective within 5 s (US-ONB-009); (2) storage split — refresh in HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict/Secure cookie `cv_refresh`, access token held in memory only and fetched via `POST /auth/refresh`; (3) access-token TTL and refresh cadence that keep WS re-auth (`23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3) at most once per 10 minutes per connection; (4) idle-lock semantics that keep the socket and subscriptions alive while blocking order entry; (5) rotation-family revocation walk over `sessions_rotation` and its cost at expected row counts; (6) step-up representation — `sessions.mfa_satisfied_at` vs `Session.elevated_until` — reconciled to one field.
- Prototype branch `spike/e09-session-model` with a throwaway FastAPI + Postgres harness measuring revocation latency and refresh throughput.
- **ADR** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording the decision and the rejected alternatives.
- A written reconciliation note listing every edit needed to `21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1 so the two agree.

## Out of scope
- Production code — this spike is explicitly not shippable; the promoted parts are re-implemented under E09-T01/S03 with full DoD.
- WebAuthn, device trust, and any second access channel beyond the web app.
- Bybit-side key or session handling (E27).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Revocation latency is measured, not assumed
  Given the prototype with N active sessions
  When a session is revoked
  Then the time until the next request and the next WS frame on that session are rejected is recorded, and the 5 s requirement of US-ONB-009 is shown met or the design is changed

Scenario: Refresh cadence does not storm the WS layer
  Given the chosen access-token TTL
  When 20 concurrent clients run for one hour in the harness
  Then the measured re-auth frame rate per connection is at most one per 10 minutes and no reconnect is triggered by refresh

Scenario: Rotated token reuse kills the family
  Given a refresh token that has already been rotated
  When it is presented again
  Then every session in its rotation family is revoked and the event is emitted as auth.refresh_reuse_detected at severity critical

Scenario: The decision is recorded even if it is to defer
  When the timebox expires
  Then an ADR exists stating the decision or an explicit deferral with what further data is needed

Scenario: The two schema documents are made to agree
  Then the note enumerates the exact field-level divergences between 21-database-schema.md 3.1.4 and 24-internal-schemas.md 15.1 and the chosen resolution for each
```

## Technical notes / design
Decision criteria agreed up front: if opaque handles meet p99 < 2 ms lookup with the per-request revocation check, they win outright over JWT (simpler revocation, no key rotation burden); JWT is chosen only if the measured lookup cost materially threatens the API latency budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. Cookie attributes are non-negotiable (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure`, `Path=/api/v1/auth`) per `04-security-program.md`.

## Test plan
Harness-level only: a load script for refresh throughput, a revocation-latency probe, and a reuse-detection assertion. No coverage gate applies to throwaway spike code; the harness is archived, not merged.

## Security notes
Threats weighed explicitly: token theft via XSS (argues against localStorage), CSRF (argues for SameSite=Strict plus an origin check), replay of rotated tokens, revocation lag, and step-up downgrade. Findings feed the E09 STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no user interface is produced. Stated explicitly rather than skipped, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §1.

## Performance notes
Record: session-lookup p50/p99, refresh endpoint throughput, rotation-family walk cost at 10k rows, and the projected WS re-auth frame rate. These numbers become the budget line for E09-S03.

## Observability
The harness emits the metric names proposed for production (`auth_sessions_active`, `auth_refresh_reuse_total`, `auth_revocation_latency_ms`) so the spike also validates that the chosen model is measurable.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2: questions answered with recorded evidence, ADR merged in `27-adrs/`, follow-up edits filed against E09-T01 and E09-S03, spike branch archived unmerged, findings presented at Sprint Review, `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E03** (CI/CD and a runnable Postgres in dev).

## Branch
`spike/e09-session-model`

## References
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3, §9.5; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`, `/auth/sessions`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-004, US-ONB-009; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/20-architecture.md
2. docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `services/api/auth/`
- `services/api/accounts/`
- `services/api/secrets/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what's listed in References.

**Commands**
- `ruff check services/api`
- `mypy --strict services/api`
- `pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `spike/e09-session-model`
- PR title: "E09-K01: Spike: session, token rotation and revocation model (ADR)"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/security @CandleViewer/backend
- Labels: type/spike, area/auth-rbac, priority/p0, security

**Done means**
- All Gherkin scenarios in this ticket pass as automated tests (or are recorded as a manual QA step with a linked follow-up automation ticket).
- Local gate green: lint, typecheck, unit tests for every touched package (AGENTS.md §4).
- Coverage threshold for the touched package is met (frontend >=80% per DoD unless the ticket states otherwise; backend --cov-fail-under=85 per AGENTS.md §4).
- PR uses the filled template, links `Closes #<issue>`, and is merged only via the merge queue.

**Do NOT**
- Production code — this spike is explicitly not shippable; the promoted parts are re-implemented under E09-T01/S03 with full DoD.
- WebAuthn, device trust, and any second access channel beyond the web app.
- Bybit-side key or session handling (E27).

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Postgres migration: identity, sessions, MFA and RBAC tables
body:
## Context
Every other ticket in E09 — and E27, E29, E39 and E42 after it — reads or writes the identity tables. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 specifies them exactly: `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`, together with the enums (`user_status`, `role_name`, `mfa_method_kind`), the check constraints, the partial unique indexes, and the **owner-floor** deferred constraint trigger `trg_owner_floor` that refuses any change leaving zero active owners. Without this migration nothing else in the Epic can start, so it is the first implementation ticket after the session-model ADR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating, verbatim against `21-database-schema.md` §3.1: enums `user_status`, `role_name`, `mfa_method_kind`; domains `citext`, `sha256_hex`; tables `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`; all listed indexes (`ux_users_email`, `ux_users_username`, `ix_users_status`, `ix_role_permissions_perm`, `ix_user_roles_role`, `ix_uaa_account`, `ix_uaa_frozen`, `ix_sessions_user_live`, `ix_sessions_expiry`, `ux_mfa_webauthn_cred`, `ix_mfa_user_active`, `ix_mfa_ch_user_open`, `ix_recovery_unused`).
- All CHECK constraints from the document, including `users_pwd_argon` (`password_hash LIKE '$argon2id$%'`), `uaa_trade_implies_view`, `sessions_expiry`, `mfa_totp_shape`, `mfa_wa_shape`, `mfa_ch_purpose`.
- `trg_owner_floor` deferred constraint trigger on `user_roles` and `users` raising SQLSTATE 23514.
- Column `COMMENT`s marking SECRET and PII columns exactly as the document does (`users.password_hash`, `users.email`, `sessions.ip`, `sessions.user_agent`, `sessions.tailscale_node`, `mfa_methods.secret_enc`, `recovery_codes.code_hash`, `mfa_challenges.nonce`).
- **Seed**: the three system roles (`owner`, `manager`, `viewer`) with `is_system = true`, and the permission rows generated from the `x-rbac.permissions` blocks of `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` with `is_dangerous` set for the step-up-requiring codes.
- Nightly cleanup job deleting `mfa_challenges` older than 24 h (retention policy, `21-database-schema.md` §3.1.5).
- Down-migration, and SQLAlchemy models/typed repository stubs under `services/api/auth/`.

## Out of scope
- `audit_log` and its chain trigger — **E09-T02**.
- `exchange_accounts`, `api_keys`, `account_profiles` — **E27**.
- Any endpoint or business logic; this ticket is schema only.
- Populating `user_account_access` rows (E27/E39 own the grant flows); the table is created here because `sessions`/RBAC scoping references it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given an empty Postgres 16 database
  When the migration is applied and then reversed and re-applied
  Then both directions succeed with no manual intervention and the final schema diff against 21-database-schema.md 3.1 is empty

Scenario: The owner floor is enforced by the database
  Given exactly one active user holds the owner role
  When a transaction removes that role or disables that user
  Then the commit fails with SQLSTATE 23514 and the row is unchanged

Scenario: Non-Argon2id password hashes are rejected at the storage layer
  When a row is inserted with a bcrypt-shaped password_hash
  Then the users_pwd_argon check constraint rejects it

Scenario: Soft-deleted users free their email and username
  Given a user is soft-deleted by setting deleted_at
  When a new user is created with the same email
  Then the insert succeeds because the unique indexes are partial on deleted_at IS NULL

Scenario: Permission seed matches the API contract
  When the seed is compared with the x-rbac.permissions blocks of 22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then the code sets are identical and any divergence fails CI
```

## Technical notes / design
Alembic revision under `services/api/migrations/versions/`, naming convention per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`. `citext` and `pgcrypto` extensions are created idempotently. The owner-floor trigger is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` so multi-statement role reshuffles inside one transaction are legal as long as the end state is valid. The permission seed is generated, not hand-written, by `tools/rbac/generate.py` (built in E09-T03) — for this ticket the generator's output is committed as a checked-in fixture and the drift check wired in T03.

## Test plan
Integration tests on a real Postgres (testcontainers): apply/rollback/re-apply; constraint tests for every CHECK; owner-floor trigger tests (remove last owner directly, via user disable, and via a transaction that removes then re-adds — the last must pass); partial-index behaviour on soft delete; a schema-snapshot test that diffs `information_schema` against a committed golden file so future drift is visible in review.

## Security notes
Labelled `security`: this migration creates the tables holding password hashes, TOTP seeds, recovery-code hashes and refresh-token hashes. No raw secret column exists anywhere — only hashes or envelope-encrypted blobs (`secret_enc` with `secret_key_ref`). Grants: the application role gets `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on these tables; the read-only role `cv_ro` gets `SELECT` but is explicitly denied on `mfa_methods.secret_enc` via a view-based access path. Reviewed by the Security engineer before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. Stated explicitly per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §1.

## Performance notes
Index coverage is verified against the query shapes E09-S01/S03 will issue: session lookup by `refresh_token_hash` (unique index), live sessions by user (`ix_sessions_user_live`), unused recovery codes (`ix_recovery_unused`), open MFA challenges (`ix_mfa_ch_user_open`). An `EXPLAIN` assertion test pins index usage for the session-lookup path so a future migration cannot silently drop it.

## Observability
Migration runs emit a structured log line with revision id and duration; a `db_schema_revision` Prometheus gauge exposes the applied head so the health screen (E42) and PRR checklist can assert environment parity.

title: Append-only hash-chained audit writer (M19) and audit query API
body:
## Context
Module **M19** is the append-only, tamper-evident audit log that every later Epic writes into: key rotation (E27), order submission and fan-out (E29/E34), rule arming (E35/E37), kill-switch (E39), admin actions (E42). `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1 specifies it precisely — `audit_log` with `prev_hash`/`entry_hash` forming a SHA-256 chain computed **by a database trigger, never by the application**, `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_log FROM cv_app, cv_ro`, a daily head-hash checkpoint written to `audit_checkpoints` and to an off-box file so tail truncation is detectable. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` exposes `GET /admin/audit`, `POST /admin/audit/verify` and `POST /admin/audit/export`.

Building this early, in the same sprint as the first auth flows, is deliberate: the auth stories themselves must emit audit entries (failed sign-in with source IP per US-ONB-001, invite reuse per US-ONB-006, high-severity TOTP reset per US-ONB-010), so the writer must exist before them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration for `audit_log` exactly per `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1: all columns, the `au_action_fmt` CHECK, indexes `ix_audit_time`, `ix_audit_actor`, `ix_audit_action`, `ix_audit_object`, `ix_audit_sev`, the `audit_chain()` trigger function and its BEFORE INSERT trigger, and the `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` grants; plus `audit_checkpoints`.
- `audit.emit(action, *, actor, object, outcome, severity, before_state, after_state, reason, request_id, env)` API in `services/api/audit/`, with a typed action registry so `action` strings are not free-form at call sites.
- **Redaction layer**: `before_state`/`after_state` diffs pass through a redactor that removes any field classified SECRET (password hashes, TOTP seeds, recovery codes, refresh tokens, invite tokens, API keys) and hashes PII where the value itself is not needed.
- Durable buffering: writes are asynchronous but survive a Postgres outage via the bounded on-disk WAL described in `20-architecture.md` §F8, replayed on recovery in original order so the chain stays monotonic.
- Endpoints `GET /admin/audit` (filter by actor, action, object, severity, time range; cursor pagination), `POST /admin/audit/verify` (walk and verify the chain, return first divergence if any), `POST /admin/audit/export` (NDJSON export with the head hash attached).
- Daily checkpoint job writing the head hash to `audit_checkpoints` and to a file outside the database volume.

## Out of scope
- The admin audit-browser UI — **E42** (this ticket ships the API it calls).
- Emitting audit events from trading, rules or key management — those Epics call `audit.emit` themselves.
- Long-term archival to Parquet/cold storage — **E16**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The chain is computed by the database
  Given an application that inserts an audit row without supplying prev_hash or entry_hash
  When the insert commits
  Then the trigger has populated both, prev_hash equals the previous row's entry_hash, and the genesis row's prev_hash is 64 zeros

Scenario: The application role cannot rewrite history
  Given the cv_app database role
  When it attempts UPDATE or DELETE on audit_log
  Then Postgres refuses with insufficient privilege and the attempt itself is logged

Scenario: Tampering is detected and located
  Given a row is altered by a superuser out of band
  When POST /admin/audit/verify runs
  Then it reports the chain as broken and returns the id of the first divergent entry

Scenario: Secrets never reach the log
  Given an audit emission whose before_state contains a password hash and a TOTP seed
  When the entry is written
  Then those fields are absent from the stored JSON and a redaction marker is present in their place

Scenario: Postgres outage does not lose events
  Given Postgres is unavailable for 60 seconds while 500 auditable actions occur
  When it returns
  Then all 500 entries appear in original order with an intact chain and no duplicates

Scenario: Non-owner cannot read the audit log
  Given a manager session
  When it calls GET /admin/audit
  Then the request is denied with 403 and the denial is itself audited
```

## Technical notes / design
The canonical serialisation hashed by `audit_chain()` is fixed in the migration (sorted keys, explicit null handling, UTC timestamps at microsecond precision) and must never change without a documented chain-break checkpoint. Inserts are serialised through a single writer task to keep the chain well-ordered under concurrency — the trigger's `SELECT ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1` would otherwise race; the writer holds an advisory lock for the duration of the insert. `verify` streams in batches so it does not load the table into memory.

## Test plan
Unit tests for the redactor (property-based over the SECRET field registry) and the action registry; integration tests for chain continuity under 1000 concurrent emissions, out-of-band tamper detection, grant enforcement, WAL replay after a simulated Postgres outage, and the checkpoint job; contract tests for the three endpoints against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; a chaos test that kills the process mid-buffer and asserts no loss and no duplication.

## Security notes
This is a core control for non-repudiation. Threats: tamper (mitigated by chain plus revoked grants plus off-box checkpoint), truncation (checkpoint), secret leakage into `before_state`/`after_state` (redactor with a fail-closed default — unknown fields in a SECRET-classified object are dropped, not passed), log injection via crafted `object_label` (stored as data, rendered escaped), and denial-of-service by flooding (bounded WAL with a drop-oldest-plus-alarm policy, never dropping silently). Security engineer review is mandatory before merge.

## Accessibility notes
No UI here; the consuming screen is E42's. The API returns machine-readable `severity` and `reason` fields so E42 can render status without relying on colour alone, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Budget: `audit.emit` returns in < 1 ms at the call site (enqueue only); sustained write throughput ≥ 2000 entries/s; `GET /admin/audit` p99 < 300 ms for a 30-day window on the indexed filters; `verify` processes ≥ 50k rows/s. Measured against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and recorded on the ticket.

## Observability
Metrics `audit_entries_written_total{action,severity}`, `audit_buffer_depth`, `audit_write_errors_total`, `audit_chain_verified` (gauge, set by the daily job), `audit_checkpoint_age_seconds`. Alerts: chain verification failure (critical), buffer depth above threshold, checkpoint older than 26 h.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2, plus: `21-database-schema.md` and `22-api-openapi.yaml` match the implementation, Security engineer sign-off comment present, perf numbers recorded, QA verification of the tamper-detection scenario recorded.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-T01**.

`feat/e09-audit-writer`

## References
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1, §2 (grants); `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/admin/audit`, `/admin/audit/verify`, `/admin/audit/export`; `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10, failure mode F8; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

title: Tailscale-only reachability self-check and CIDR guard (US-ONB-008)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-008 (Must) requires the backend to refuse connections that did not arrive over the private network, so the terminal is never publicly exposed. `20-architecture.md` §WSL hazards names the specific failure this guards against: a `0.0.0.0` binding leak via Windows `portproxy`, which would silently publish a trading terminal to the LAN. The story is unusual in that it is enforced **before authentication** and can put the whole app into read-only mode, so it is implemented as a platform Task rather than a UI Story, and it lands in Sprint 02 alongside the schema so no later auth work is ever exercised against an unsafe binding.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Boot self-check**: assert no listener is bound to `0.0.0.0` or `::`; log the bound interfaces explicitly at startup. Re-run hourly (sleep/resume on WSL can change the picture).
- **CIDR guard middleware**: requests whose source address is outside the configured Tailscale CIDR (and loopback) are rejected with **403 before authentication** and audited via `audit.emit("net.off_mesh_request", severity="warning")` with the source address. Applies to REST and to the WS upgrade.
- **Read-only degradation**: if the self-check detects a public binding, the app starts (so the operator can see why) in read-only mode — order placement disabled at the OMS boundary, a blocking banner surfaced through the `system` WS topic (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6 `system`), and the condition is non-dismissible until resolved.
- Prometheus gauge `net_binding_safe` (1/0) and the self-check result exposed on the health payload consumed by SCR-137 Admin security centre and SCR-016 first-run wizard.
- `make audit-net` check runnable in CI-on-host, per `20-architecture.md`.
- Configuration: allowed CIDR list and trusted-proxy handling documented in the deployment runbook; the source address is taken from the socket peer, never from a client-controllable header unless an explicitly configured trusted proxy is in front.

## Out of scope
- Provisioning Tailscale itself, ACLs and device approval — infrastructure (E01/E03) and the ops runbook.
- The Admin security-centre screen (SCR-137) — **E42**; this ticket provides its data.
- Per-user IP allow-listing on Bybit API keys — **E27**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Safe binding passes the self-check
  Given the backend binds only loopback and the Tailscale interface
  When it starts
  Then the self-check passes, the bound interfaces are logged, and net_binding_safe is 1

Scenario: Off-mesh request is refused before authentication
  Given a request arrives from an address outside the allowed CIDR
  When it reaches the application
  Then it is rejected with 403 without any credential being evaluated and an audit entry records the source address

Scenario: Public binding degrades the app instead of trading unsafely
  Given the process is started with a 0.0.0.0 binding
  Then the app starts read-only, order placement is refused at the OMS boundary, a blocking banner is published on the system topic and net_binding_safe is 0

Scenario: A header cannot forge an on-mesh source
  Given no trusted proxy is configured
  When an off-mesh request sets X-Forwarded-For to a Tailscale address
  Then the header is ignored, the socket peer address is used, and the request is still rejected

Scenario: Drift after resume is caught
  Given the host sleeps and resumes with a changed binding
  When the hourly re-check runs
  Then the new state is detected within the hour and the gauge and banner update accordingly
```

## Technical notes / design
The self-check enumerates listening sockets of the process (and, on WSL, cross-checks the Windows-side portproxy table when the helper is available) rather than trusting the configured bind string, because the leak mode is precisely a mismatch between configuration and reality. Read-only mode is a single process-wide flag consulted by the OMS validator (`20-architecture.md` §3.x `Validator`) so it cannot be bypassed by any route.

## Test plan
Unit tests for the CIDR matcher (IPv4/IPv6, boundaries, loopback, mapped addresses); integration tests binding a test server to `0.0.0.0` and asserting degraded start; middleware tests asserting rejection precedes authentication (a valid session from an off-mesh address is still refused); a spoofing test for the header case; a chaos test toggling the binding at runtime and asserting the hourly re-check reacts.

## Security notes
Labelled `security` and central to the deployment threat model: this is the control that keeps a money-moving application off the public internet. Fail-closed is mandatory — if the self-check cannot determine the binding state, it is treated as unsafe. The 403 response body is deliberately generic (no hint about the allowed CIDR). Audited entries carry the source address, which is PII-adjacent and is retained under the audit retention policy.

## Accessibility notes
The blocking banner it triggers is rendered by CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner / the shell (E10) and must be announced assertively, carry an icon and text (not colour alone), and be reachable in the focus order, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. This ticket supplies the machine-readable reason code and human sentence.

## Performance notes
The CIDR check is an in-memory prefix match on every request: budget < 50 µs p99, no allocation per request. The hourly self-check must not block the event loop — it runs in a thread executor with a 2 s timeout.

## Observability
`net_binding_safe` gauge, `net_off_mesh_requests_total{reason}` counter, structured log at boot listing bound interfaces, and an alert that fires immediately when the gauge goes to 0.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2: AC verified by tests, coverage met, runbook and `20-architecture.md` updated, Security engineer review recorded, demonstrated at Sprint Review by deliberately misconfiguring a staging instance.

## Dependencies

## Branch
`feat/e09-tailscale-guard`

title: Password sign-in with lockout and uniform failures (US-ONB-001)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-001 (Must): *"As a user, I want to sign in with an email/username and password over Tailscale, so that only invited people reach the terminal."* This is the first leg of the two-legged login defined in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` — `POST /auth/login` returns an `mfa_required` challenge (`mfa_token`, `methods`) rather than a session when MFA is enrolled, and `POST /auth/mfa/verify` (E09-S02) completes it. The story covers the backend credential check and SCR-001 Login end to end, including the states the screen catalogue enumerates: idle, submitting, invalid credentials, disabled account, locked, and server-unreachable.

The NFRs are security-critical and explicit in the story: Argon2id hashing, per-account **and** per-IP rate limiting (5 failures → 15 min lockout), constant-time comparison, and **no user enumeration** — the same message and the same timing whether the username is unknown, the password wrong, or the account disabled is revealed only after correct credentials.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /auth/login` per `22-api-openapi.yaml`: accepts username/email + password; returns `status=mfa_required` with an opaque `mfa_token` when an MFA method is enrolled, or a full `TokenBundle` plus the `cv_refresh` cookie when it is not (viewer without optional MFA, per `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1).
- Argon2id verification with the parameters stored per user in `users.password_algo_params` (`m=65536,t=3,p=4` default), a per-user pepper derived from the KEK-held secret, constant-time comparison, and transparent rehash-on-login when parameters change.
- Lockout: increment `users.failed_login_count`, set `users.locked_until` after 5 failures for 15 minutes; independent per-IP throttle so one attacker cannot lock every account; both counters reset on success.
- `PUT /auth/password` and **SCR-004 Forced password change** when `users.status = 'invited'` or a reset was issued — CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-202 PasswordStrengthMeter, CMP-203 RequirementChecklist.
- **SCR-001 Login** in `apps/web`: CMP-200 AuthCard, CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-005, CMP-007, CMP-027, CMP-075, CMP-207 BuildFooter; states idle / submitting / invalid / disabled / locked (with remaining time) / server-unreachable (E17's SCR-152 inline variant).
- Audit emissions via E09-T02: `auth.login_succeeded`, `auth.login_failed` (with source IP and reason, severity warning), `auth.account_locked` (severity warning), `auth.login_blocked_disabled`.

## Out of scope
- The TOTP challenge screen and code verification — **E09-S02**.
- Session lifetime, idle lock and revocation semantics — **E09-S03**.
- Invite redemption — **E09-S05**.
- Password reset by the owner and self-service recovery beyond recovery codes (owner resets are E42/E09-S04 territory).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Successful sign-in advances to the second factor
  Given I am a registered, enabled user reaching the app over Tailscale
  When I submit my correct username and password
  Then the response is status mfa_required with an mfa_token and the enrolled methods, no session cookie is set, and auth.login_succeeded is audited

Scenario: Wrong password gives no hint and is audited
  Given I am a registered user
  When I submit an incorrect password
  Then I see "Username or password is incorrect" with no indication of which was wrong
  And the attempt is audited with the source IP

Scenario: Disabled account
  Given my account has been disabled by the owner
  When I submit correct credentials
  Then I see "Account disabled - contact the owner" and no session and no mfa_token are created

Scenario: Lockout after five failures
  Given I have failed five times within the window
  When I submit even the correct password
  Then I am refused for 15 minutes, the remaining time is shown, and auth.account_locked is audited

Scenario: Unknown user is indistinguishable from a wrong password
  Given a username that does not exist
  When I submit any password
  Then the message, the HTTP status and the response time distribution match the wrong-password case within the agreed tolerance

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Given I navigate the login form with the keyboard only
  Then every control is reachable, errors are programmatically associated with their field and announced via aria-live, and focus moves to the error summary on failure
```

## Technical notes / design
Enumeration resistance is implemented by always performing an Argon2id verification — against a fixed dummy hash when the user does not exist — so the timing profile is flat; the disabled-account message is returned only when the password actually verified, which is a deliberate, documented trade-off (the user already proved knowledge of the secret). Rate limiting uses a token bucket keyed on both `user_id` and source address, held in-process (single-process deployment per `20-architecture.md` C4) with the counters additionally persisted on `users` so a restart does not clear a lockout. The `mfa_token` is single-use, bound to the source address, and expires in 5 minutes (`mfa_challenges` row with `purpose='login'`).

## Test plan
Unit: Argon2id verify/rehash, pepper handling, token-bucket edge cases, lockout arithmetic across restarts. Contract: `/auth/login` request/response against `22-api-openapi.yaml`, including the 401 shape. Integration: real Postgres, lockout persistence, audit rows written with the right severity. E2E (Playwright): all six SCR-001 states, forced password change on an invited user. Security: timing-difference test over 1000 samples for unknown vs wrong-password; enumeration attempt via response-shape diffing. a11y: axe-core on SCR-001 and SCR-004 plus a manual screen-reader pass. Load: k6 login profile asserting throttle behaviour and that Argon2id cost does not exhaust the worker pool.

## Security notes
Threats: credential stuffing (per-IP and per-account throttling, lockout), user enumeration (uniform messaging and timing), offline cracking if the database leaks (Argon2id with tuned parameters plus pepper outside the database), pepper compromise (KEK handling per `04-security-program.md`), and denial of service by locking out a known username (per-IP limiter is separate, and the owner can always be unlocked from the admin path in E42). Passwords are never logged, never echoed, and never placed in an error message or audit `before_state`. Data classification: credentials SECRET, source IP PII.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-001 per `05-accessibility-standard.md`: single `h1`, labelled inputs with `autocomplete="username"`/`"current-password"`, error summary focused on submit with `role="alert"`, lockout countdown announced politely and not by colour alone, password-reveal control labelled and keyboard operable, contrast ≥ 4.5:1, visible focus ring on every control, and CMP-202's strength meter exposing its level as text.

## Performance notes
Argon2id parameters tuned so a single verification is ~150 ms on the target host and concurrency is bounded so a burst of logins cannot starve market-data handling — verification runs in a dedicated thread pool. Endpoint p99 target < 400 ms including hashing under the k6 login profile of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
`auth_login_attempts_total{outcome}`, `auth_login_duration_seconds` histogram, `auth_lockouts_total`, `auth_argon2_pool_saturation`. Alert on a spike in failures from a single source and on any lockout of the owner account.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2: all Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests, coverage ≥85% backend / ≥80% frontend, OpenAPI matches implementation, axe-core green plus manual screen-reader pass, design-qa comparison against the SCR-001 spec, Security engineer review with the abuse cases exercised, QA sign-off, demoed at Sprint Review, feature-flag state recorded (none — auth is always on).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-T01** (tables), **E09-T02** (audit writer), **E09-T04** (off-mesh requests must already be refused before a login form is exposed). Design for SCR-001/SCR-004 must be Done per the design-ahead rule.

`feat/e09-password-signin`

title: TOTP second factor, enrolment and recovery codes (US-ONB-002/003)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-002 (Must) and US-ONB-003 (Must) together make the second factor real: an app-level TOTP independent of Bybit's, plus first-login enrolment with ten single-use recovery codes so a lost authenticator is recoverable without the owner minting passwords. `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1 makes MFA **mandatory for owner and manager** and optional for viewer. The schema exists (`mfa_methods` with envelope-encrypted `secret_enc` + `secret_key_ref`, `mfa_challenges` with `purpose`, `recovery_codes` hashed) and the endpoints are specified: `POST /auth/mfa/verify`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `POST /auth/mfa/recovery`, `DELETE /auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`.

The two stories are one deliverable because enrolment and verification share the secret handling, the replay window and the screens (SCR-002 challenge, SCR-003 enrolment, SCR-112 security settings); splitting them would ship a factor nobody can enrol or an enrolment nothing verifies.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Verification** `POST /auth/mfa/verify`: exchanges `mfa_token` + TOTP code (or a recovery code) for a session. RFC 6238, SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 s step, ±1 step skew, **replay-protected** — a code accepted within a time step cannot be reused, tracked per `(method_id, time_step)`.
- **Enrolment** `POST /auth/mfa/enroll` returning the `otpauth://` URI and a displayable text secret, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll/confirm` requiring one valid code before `mfa_methods.confirmed_at` is set; the method stays `pending` until confirmed.
- **Recovery codes**: 10 single-use codes generated at enrolment, shown exactly once with copy and download, stored only as `sha256_hex` in `recovery_codes`; consuming one signs the user in, marks `used_at`, and **forces re-enrolment of TOTP**; exhaustion returns a message directing the user to the owner (US-ONB-010 path). `POST /auth/mfa/recovery` regenerates codes, hard-deleting unused ones and auditing `auth.recovery_codes_regenerated`.
- **Secret handling**: the TOTP seed is envelope-encrypted at rest (`secret_enc`, `secret_key_ref`) using the KEK path from `04-security-program.md`; it is returned to the client exactly once during enrolment and never again — `GET` on a method never exposes it.
- **Screens**: SCR-002 Two-factor challenge (CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-200 AuthCard) with states idle / verifying / invalid / expired-challenge (returns to SCR-001) / locked after 5 tries; SCR-003 TOTP enrolment (CMP-205 QrCode, CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList, CMP-203 RequirementChecklist); SCR-112 Security settings showing enrolled methods, remaining recovery-code count and regeneration.
- Audit: `auth.mfa_verified`, `auth.mfa_failed` (reason: invalid / reused / expired), `auth.mfa_enrolled`, `auth.recovery_code_used` (severity warning), `auth.recovery_codes_exhausted` (severity error).

## Out of scope
- WebAuthn/passkeys — columns exist in `mfa_methods`, flows are reserved for SCR-007..009 in a later Epic.
- Step-up re-authentication using an already-enrolled factor — **E09-S04**.
- Owner-initiated TOTP reset — **E09-S04**.
- SMS or email factors — never in scope for this product.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Valid code creates a session
  Given I have completed the password step and enrolled TOTP
  When I enter the current 6-digit code
  Then a session is created and I land on my default workspace

Scenario: Reused code is rejected
  Given I have just used code 123456 successfully
  When I attempt to sign in again with 123456 inside the same time step
  Then the code is rejected as already used and auth.mfa_failed records reason reused

Scenario: Clock drift within one step is tolerated
  Given my authenticator is 25 seconds ahead
  When I enter the code it shows
  Then it is accepted within the plus or minus one time-step window

Scenario: First-login enrolment
  Given I sign in for the first time with a valid invite
  When I scan the QR code and confirm one valid code
  Then TOTP is enabled and 10 single-use recovery codes are displayed once

Scenario: Recovery code use forces re-enrolment
  Given I have lost my authenticator
  When I sign in using an unused recovery code
  Then I am signed in, that code is consumed, and I am forced to re-enrol TOTP before reaching the workspace

Scenario: Recovery codes exhausted
  Given all 10 recovery codes are consumed
  When I attempt recovery
  Then I am told to contact the owner and no session is created

Scenario: Codes never appear in logs
  Given any of the above flows runs with debug logging enabled
  When the logs and audit entries are searched
  Then no TOTP code, seed, otpauth URI or recovery code appears anywhere

Scenario: Screen-reader enrolment without a camera
  Given I use a screen reader and cannot scan a QR code
  Then the equivalent text secret is exposed as selectable text with a labelled copy control and the same enrolment completes by keyboard only
```

## Technical notes / design
Replay protection stores the last accepted `time_step` per method and rejects any step less than or equal to it, which also closes the ±1-window replay hole that a naive implementation leaves open. Challenge state lives in `mfa_challenges` (`purpose='login'|'enroll'|'step_up'`, `attempts` capped at 5, `expires_at` 5 min); five failed attempts abandon the challenge and return the user to SCR-001. Recovery-code verification is constant-time against the hashed set and is rate-limited identically to passwords. Codes are generated from `secrets.token_bytes` with an unambiguous alphabet (no 0/O/1/l) and are grouped for readability.

## Test plan
Unit: RFC 6238 vector tests, skew boundary tests at ±1 and ±2 steps, replay rejection, recovery-code hashing and single use, envelope encrypt/decrypt round trip. Contract: all five endpoints against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: enrolment → confirm → verify → recovery → forced re-enrolment on real Postgres with audit assertions. E2E: SCR-002 and SCR-003 including the expired-challenge and locked states, and download/copy of recovery codes. Security: log-scrape test asserting no secret material; brute-force test on the 6-digit space asserting the attempt cap holds. a11y: axe-core on SCR-002, SCR-003, SCR-112 plus a manual screen-reader pass on enrolment.

## Security notes
Threats: seed exfiltration (envelope encryption, never re-displayed, never logged), code replay (per-step tracking), brute force (5-attempt challenge cap plus per-IP throttle — the 6-digit space is small, so the cap is the control), recovery-code theft (hashed at rest, single use, shown once), and enrolment hijack (confirm requires a valid code from the same authenticated challenge). Mandatory-MFA invariant: the last remaining method cannot be deleted while `users.mfa_required` is set, enforced server-side on `DELETE /auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`, which additionally requires the `X-Reauth-Password` header per the OpenAPI contract.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-204 OtpInput must behave as a single labelled field for assistive technology (not six unlabelled boxes), accept paste of a full code, announce validation errors via `aria-live`, and never rely on a time limit the user cannot see; the 30 s expiry is surfaced as text. CMP-205 QrCode carries an `alt` description and is always accompanied by the text secret. CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList is a semantic list with a copy-all and download control, both labelled, and warns that the codes will not be shown again.

## Performance notes
TOTP verification is pure computation — p99 < 5 ms excluding the session write; envelope decryption of the seed is cached per request only, never across requests. Endpoint p99 < 150 ms.

## Observability
`auth_mfa_verifications_total{method,outcome}`, `auth_mfa_failures_total{reason}`, `auth_recovery_codes_remaining` gauge per user (exported as a low-cardinality histogram), `auth_mfa_enrollments_total`. Alerts: recovery-code exhaustion, and a burst of `reason=invalid` indicating brute force.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, with explicit Security engineer sign-off (this Story is default-on for the `security` label), design-qa against SCR-002/SCR-003, manual screen-reader pass recorded, and QA sign-off on the recovery-code lifecycle including exhaustion.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S01** (the password leg produces the `mfa_token` this Story consumes).

## Branch
`feat/e09-totp-mfa`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-002, US-ONB-003; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-002, SCR-003, SCR-112; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-200, CMP-203, CMP-204, CMP-205, CMP-206; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/auth/mfa/verify`, `/auth/mfa/enroll`, `/auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `/auth/mfa/recovery`, `/auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.5; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1; `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10 `TotpAuth`; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

title: Session lifetime, idle lock and sign-out everywhere (US-ONB-004/009)
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** Session lifetime is B16 `session` built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` via the factory (`statechart/factory.py`); idle-lock and absolute-expiry are coarse `after:` timers in `machines/B16.session.machine.json` (BENCH-6 p99 55-92 ms is acceptable here, C-04 hoists revocation onto the root so it fires from every substate). No hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime: `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/bindings/b16_session.py` is the only place idle/absolute/revocation logic lives.

US-ONB-004 (Must) and US-ONB-009 (Should) define what a session *is* in this product: 12 h absolute lifetime, a configurable 5–60 min idle lock that re-auths without tearing down the WebSocket, and server-side revocation of any session within 5 seconds. The requirement that the lock "must not tear down WS subscriptions (reconnect storms)" and that "live data keeps streaming underneath" makes this a joint auth/transport Story: it implements the in-place re-auth contract of `23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3 and the mid-connection revocation frames of §9.5 on the auth side. The token and rotation model was decided in E09-K01.

A second safety requirement sits here: on absolute expiry "any armed one-click trading is disarmed", and on sign-out-everywhere "any armed rules owned by me continue running server-side" — the rule runtime is deliberately independent of UI sessions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1`: `machines/B16.session.machine.json` (states `active` / `idle_locked` / `expired`; `after:` timers for the idle deadline and the 12h absolute lifetime; `REVOKE` arm on the root per C-04) plus `bindings/b16_session.py` (guards: `is_within_absolute_lifetime`; actions: `disarm_one_click`, `clear_ws_resubscribe_flag`; no services needed for the timer path).
- `POST /auth/refresh` with rotation: every refresh issues a new `sessions` row, marks the old `revoked_reason='rotated'`, links them in `sessions_rotation`; presenting an already-rotated refresh token revokes the **entire family** transitively and writes `auth.refresh_reuse_detected` at severity critical.
- `GET /auth/session` (introspection: identity, roles, permissions, account scope, expiry timestamps), `GET /auth/sessions` (list: device label, shell Electron/browser, first seen, last seen, source address), `POST /auth/logout` (current session), and sign-out-everywhere revoking all sessions of the user including the current one.
- **Idle lock**: `sessions.last_seen_at` drives an idle deadline (per-user configurable 5–60 min, default 15); on expiry the client shows **SCR-005** re-auth overlay, order entry is disabled server-side for that session, one-click arming is cleared, and the WS connection and all subscriptions are **preserved**. Unlock requires the password only (not TOTP) while inside the absolute lifetime.
- **Absolute expiry** at 12 h: full sign-out, WS `bye` with `token_expired` and close `4401`, armed one-click trading disarmed.
- **Revocation propagation**: a revoked session's next REST request is refused and the WS connection receives a revocation frame and closes within 5 s, per `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5.
- Frontend: SCR-005 session-expired/re-auth modal, SCR-112 Security settings session list with per-session revoke and "Sign out everywhere", state restoration to exactly the same workspace and scroll position after unlock.
- Audit: `auth.session_created`, `auth.session_refreshed`, `auth.session_revoked{reason}`, `auth.refresh_reuse_detected` (critical), `auth.idle_locked`.

## Out of scope
- Step-up elevation for dangerous actions — **E09-S04**.
- The WS transport implementation itself (framing, backpressure, revocation frame plumbing) — **E17**; this Story defines and calls the auth-side contract and tests against E17's client where available, with a stub otherwise.
- Workspace persistence mechanics — **E10**/layouts Epic; this Story only asserts restoration behaviour.
- Rule-runtime independence is asserted, not implemented (rules land in E35+).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Idle lock preserves the data feed
  Given my idle timeout is 15 minutes
  When I do not interact for 15 minutes
  Then the UI locks to a re-auth overlay, the WebSocket stays open with its subscriptions intact, and no re-snapshot is requested

Scenario: Unlock restores context
  Given the screen is locked
  When I enter my password
  Then I return to exactly the same workspace and scroll position and TOTP is not requested

Scenario: Absolute expiry disarms trading
  Given my session is older than 12 hours
  When it expires
  Then I am fully signed out, one-click trading is disarmed, and the socket closes with code 4401 and reason token_expired

Scenario: Order entry is refused while locked
  Given my session is idle-locked
  When an order submission is attempted with that session's token
  Then the server refuses it regardless of what the client believes

Scenario: Revoke one session
  Given two active sessions
  When I revoke the other one from Settings, Sessions
  Then that client is disconnected within 5 seconds and must re-authenticate, and my own session is unaffected

Scenario: Refresh-token reuse kills the family
  Given a refresh token that has already been rotated
  When it is presented again
  Then every session in its rotation family is revoked and auth.refresh_reuse_detected is audited at severity critical

Scenario: Sign out everywhere leaves server-side rules running
  Given I own an armed rule
  When I sign out everywhere
  Then all my sessions end and the rule continues to run server-side
```

## Technical notes / design
Session lifecycle state (`active`, `idle_locked`, `expired`) is published by `statechart/factory.build("B16", ...)`/`restore(...)`; the interpreter is the single source of truth read by the auth decision point (E09-T03) and by the WS gateway (`E17-T08`). `machine_hash` for B16 is locked in `machines/machine_hashes.lock`. Snapshot recipe: quiescent HMAC-enveloped blob on every `sessions` row write, restored on process start via `statechart.restore("B16", blob, clock=..., lane="platform")`. `CV-LINT-IMPORT` keeps every import of `xstate_statemachine` out of this module; only `factory.py`/`persistence.py` import it.

Revocation is checked **per request and per WS frame batch**, not only at issue, so the 5 s requirement is met without polling: a revoked session id is published on the internal bus, the gateway drops the matching connection immediately, and the per-request check is the backstop. Idle state is a property of the session row, not the browser, so closing and reopening a tab cannot reset it. The lock does not refresh tokens in the background — if the absolute lifetime elapses while locked, unlocking fails and becomes a full sign-in. One-click arming is server-side state on the session, cleared on lock and on expiry, so a stale client cannot submit with it.

## Test plan
Contract: `tests/xstate_contract/test_b16.py` asserts all B16 states/events, snapshot round-trip at every quiescence point, and the mandatory-config block (`strict_config`, `strictTargets`, `actionErrorPolicy`, `guardErrorPolicy`, `onUnhandled`) per `79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7. Unit: idle/absolute deadline arithmetic across clock changes, rotation-family walk, revocation set. Contract: `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/sessions`, `/auth/logout` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; WS `auth`/`auth_ok`/revocation frames against `23-ws-protocol.md` §13–15 schemas. Integration: reuse-detection family revocation; locked-session order refusal; restart mid-session. E2E: lock/unlock with a live subscription asserting no re-snapshot (network assertion on frame counts), revoke-other-session within 5 s, absolute expiry disarming one-click. Chaos: WS disconnect during lock, clock jump after WSL resume. a11y: axe-core on SCR-005 and SCR-112 plus a manual pass on the modal focus trap.

## Security notes
Threats: session fixation (new session id issued on every authentication and every refresh), token replay (rotation with family revocation), CSRF on refresh (SameSite=Strict cookie plus origin check), revocation lag (bus-driven immediate drop), and the idle lock being bypassed by a modified client (server-side enforcement — the client lock is cosmetic). The session list exposes IP and user-agent, which are PII shown only to the owning user and the owner role. Refresh tokens are stored only as `sha256_hex`.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-005 is a modal dialog with a proper focus trap, `aria-modal`, an accessible name, focus returned to the prior element on unlock, and an assertive announcement when the lock engages so a screen-reader user is not left typing into a dead UI. The session list is a table with row headers, an explicit "revoke" action name per row (not a bare icon), and a confirmation for "Sign out everywhere" that states the consequence in text.

## Performance notes
Per-request revocation check must add < 1 ms p99 (in-process set, invalidated by bus events). Refresh cadence per the E09-K01 decision keeps WS re-auth to at most one frame per connection per 10 minutes; the lock must generate **zero** re-subscribe traffic — asserted by counting frames in the E2E test, per the reconnect-storm concern in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
`auth_sessions_active`, `auth_session_revocations_total{reason}`, `auth_refresh_total`, `auth_refresh_reuse_total`, `auth_idle_locks_total`, `auth_revocation_latency_seconds` histogram. Alerts on any refresh-reuse detection and on revocation latency above 5 s.

title: RBAC decision point, generated permissions, deny-by-default enforcement
body:
## Context
Architecture principle **P8** states that the frontend is never trusted for account scope, risk caps or environment; `20-architecture.md` §3.10 assigns role/scope resolution to the Auth/RBAC/Audit component; `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.2 declares the `Permission` enum **generated** from the `x-rbac.permissions` blocks in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, which is the single canonical registry, cross-checked against the database seed by the contract test `rbac_vocabulary_single_source`. `30-release-roadmap.md` §12 lists "RBAC enforcement — E09" as a must-not-descope item.

This Task builds the one place that answers "may this principal do this thing to this object?" — consumed by every REST route, by the WS `auth_ok` permission payload and per-subscribe checks (`23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3, §9.5, G5), and later by the OMS validator for account scoping.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Generator** `tools/rbac/generate.py`: reads `x-rbac.permissions` from `22-api-openapi.yaml`, emits the `Permission` StrEnum consumed by `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.2 and the database seed rows for `permissions` (including `is_dangerous`, which drives step-up in E09-S04). Generated files are committed and CI fails on drift.
- **Policy decision point** in `services/api/auth/scopes.py`: `decide(principal, permission, object) -> Allow | Deny(reason)`, resolving roles via `user_roles` → `role_permissions` → `permissions`, and account scope via `user_account_access` (`can_view`, `can_trade`, `frozen`); empty `allowed_account_ids` means all, owner only.
- **Deny-by-default enforcement**: a FastAPI dependency applied globally; a route without an explicit `x-rbac.permissions` declaration (or an explicit `security: []` public marker for login/refresh/health) **fails the build**, not just the request.
- **WS integration**: `auth_ok` carries `roles`, resolved permissions and account scope; every `sub` is permission-checked per topic (`23-ws-protocol.md` §5, §6); revocation or role change publishes a live permission-change frame so a downgrade takes effect mid-connection.
- **403 semantics**: a uniform `forbidden` error body with a machine-readable `reason`, feeding **SCR-154 Permission denied**; every denial is audited (`rbac.denied`, severity warning) with the permission code.
- Role seeds: `owner` (all permissions), `manager` (trading and read within granted accounts, no `users:write`, no `keys:manage`, no `killswitch:write` beyond own scope), `viewer` (read-only across granted scope, includes audit and journal read).

## Out of scope
- Risk caps, freeze and kill-switch behaviour on `user_account_access` — **E39** (the columns are read here, the policy that sets them is not).
- Custom or user-defined roles — the three system roles are fixed in v1.
- Admin UI for granting roles and account access — **E42**.
- Rule-engine permission gates (`rules.arm_live`) — declared in the vocabulary here, enforced by E35/E37.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every route declares a permission or is explicitly public
  Given the full route inventory of the FastAPI application
  When the conformance test runs
  Then each route either declares x-rbac.permissions or is marked explicitly public, and an undeclared route fails CI

Scenario: Deny by default
  Given a newly added route whose declaration is missing
  When any principal calls it at runtime in the test harness
  Then the decision is Deny and the response is 403, never an accidental allow

Scenario: Vocabulary has one source of truth
  Given the generated enum, the OpenAPI blocks and the database seed
  When rbac_vocabulary_single_source runs
  Then the three sets are identical and any hand edit to the generated file fails the check

Scenario: A manager cannot reach another manager's account
  Given a manager granted access to account A only
  When they request data or submit an order for account B
  Then the request is denied with 403, the denial names the permission and scope, and rbac.denied is audited

Scenario: Downgrade takes effect mid-connection
  Given a connected manager whose role is reduced to viewer
  When the change commits
  Then a permission-change frame is delivered, trading topics are unsubscribed server-side, and the next order attempt on that socket is refused

Scenario: Owner floor cannot be removed through the API
  Given a single active owner
  When an attempt is made to strip that role via PUT /users/{userId}/roles
  Then the request fails and the database trigger is never relied on as the only guard
```

## Technical notes / design
The decision point is pure and synchronous over a per-request snapshot of the principal's roles, permissions and account scope, loaded once per request and invalidated by bus events on role or access change — so a decision costs a set lookup, not a query. Object-scoped decisions (account id, environment) take the object as an explicit argument; there is no ambient context, which makes the function trivially testable and keeps the OMS validator's later use honest. Endpoints touched: `POST /users`, `GET|PATCH /users/{userId}`, `PUT /users/{userId}/roles`, `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`.

## Test plan
Unit: decision matrix over (role × permission × scope × object) generated exhaustively from the seed, with golden expectations; frozen and `can_trade=false` cases. Contract: route-inventory conformance test; `rbac_vocabulary_single_source`; WS `auth_ok` payload schema. Integration: role change propagation, account-scope isolation between two managers. Security: automated privilege-escalation suite attempting every owner-only route as manager and viewer, asserting 403 and an audit row for each. Performance: decision latency benchmark.

## Security notes
This is the authorisation control for a money-moving system. Fail-closed everywhere: an unresolvable principal, an unknown permission code, or a missing declaration all yield Deny. Denials never leak whether the object exists (a manager asking about another manager's account gets the same 403 as for a non-existent account). The generator is treated as security-relevant code — changes to it require Security-engineer review, and the generated seed diff is reviewed in every PR that touches it. Feeds the E09 STRIDE model (elevation of privilege branch).

## Accessibility notes
SCR-154 Permission denied must state in text what was denied and what to do next, be announced assertively, and offer a keyboard-reachable route back; it must not rely on an icon or colour alone. This ticket supplies the `reason` code and human sentence it renders.

## Performance notes
Budget: decision p99 < 200 µs, snapshot load adds < 2 ms to the first decision of a request, zero additional queries for subsequent decisions in the same request. Measured under the API load profile in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
`rbac_denials_total{permission,role}`, `rbac_decision_duration_seconds`, `rbac_snapshot_loads_total`, and a build-time metric of declared-vs-total routes exported to the PRR checklist. Alert on a burst of denials for one principal (possible compromised session or a broken client).

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2, plus the interface-first rule: the `x-rbac.permissions` diff to `22-api-openapi.yaml` is reviewed and merged **before** implementation; Security engineer review recorded; the privilege-escalation suite is green and its report attached.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S02** (a principal must be fully authenticated before authorisation is meaningful) and **E09-T02** (denials must be auditable).

## Branch
`feat/e09-rbac-pdp`

`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` P8, §3.10; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.2; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `x-rbac.permissions`, `/users*`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` G5, §4.3, §5, §9.5; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.2, §3.1.3, §10.1; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-154; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.2.0; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12.
