title: Step-up re-authentication and owner-initiated TOTP reset (US-ONB-005/010)
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** Step-up re-auth is the step-up sub-state of B16 `session`, built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` via the factory. The per-action-class grace window and the no-grace list (`live_enablement`, `killswitch`) are guards in `machines/B16.session.machine.json`; the three-failure downgrade is a transition to a read-only child state. No hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime.

US-ONB-005 (Must): sensitive actions demand a fresh TOTP so a hijacked session cannot rotate keys or enable Live. US-ONB-010 (Should): the owner can reset a manager's second factor so a lost phone does not strand them. The two belong together because the reset is itself the archetypal step-up-protected action and shares the `mfa_challenges` (`purpose='step_up'`) plumbing and the SCR-006 modal.

The policy is precise: a 5-minute grace **per action class**, a grace that **never applies** to Live enablement or kill-switch disable, and three invalid codes abandoning the action, downgrading the session to read-only for 5 minutes and auditing at high severity. The permission registry already distinguishes dangerous actions via `permissions.is_dangerous` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.1.2), and `sessions.mfa_satisfied_at` / `Session.elevated_until` carry the freshness window — reconciled to one field by E09-K01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1`: the step-up sub-state lives inside `machines/B16.session.machine.json` (states `elevated.{action_class}` / `readonly_downgrade`); `bindings/b16_session.py` supplies the guard `grace_window_valid(action_class)` (false unconditionally for `live_enablement` and `killswitch`, per the no-grace list) and the action `record_step_up_failure` driving the 3-strike transition to `readonly_downgrade`.
- `POST /auth/step-up` per `22-api-openapi.yaml`: accepts a TOTP code for a named action class, sets the elevation window on the session, returns the window expiry so the UI can display it.
- **Server-side gate**: any route whose declared permission is `is_dangerous` requires a live elevation for its action class; the check lives in the E09-T03 decision point so no route can forget it. Action classes: `keys` (reveal-scope/rotate/revoke), `users` (invite, role change, TOTP reset), `live_enablement`, `killswitch`, `risk_caps`.
- **No-grace list**: `live_enablement` and `killswitch` disable always require a fresh code regardless of an existing window.
- **Failure policy**: three invalid codes abandon the action, mark the session read-only for 5 minutes (server-side, enforced on every write route), and audit `auth.step_up_failed` at severity `error`.
- **Owner TOTP reset**: an owner endpoint that revokes the target's `mfa_methods`, forces re-enrolment on next sign-in, revokes all their sessions, and **does not** cancel orders or flatten positions; the confirmation surface shows the target's open-position state before confirming, and the secret is never revealed to the owner.
- **Screens**: SCR-006 step-up modal and SCR-149 admin re-authentication gate (CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-043, CMP-201), showing the remaining grace window in text; SCR-003 re-enrolment forced for the reset user.
- Audit: `auth.step_up_granted`, `auth.step_up_failed` (error), `auth.session_readonly_downgrade`, `auth.mfa_reset_by_owner` (severity critical, actor and target recorded).

## Out of scope
- The key-rotation, Live-enablement and kill-switch actions themselves — **E27**, **E44**, **E39**; this Story provides the gate they declare.
- Self-service TOTP reset — deliberately impossible; recovery codes (E09-S02) are the self-service path.
- The admin user-management screen chrome — **E42**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Step-up required for a dangerous action
  Given I am signed in and open Admin, API keys
  When I attempt to reveal-scope, rotate or revoke a key
  Then I must enter a fresh TOTP code before the action proceeds

Scenario: Grace window within an action class
  Given I completed step-up 3 minutes ago for the keys action class
  When I perform a second keys action within 5 minutes
  Then no new code is required and the remaining grace window is shown in the dialog

Scenario: Grace never applies to Live enablement
  Given I completed step-up 1 minute ago for another action class
  When I attempt to enable Live trading or disable the kill-switch
  Then a fresh code is required regardless

Scenario: Three failures downgrade the session
  Given I enter an invalid code three times
  Then the action is abandoned, the session is read-only for 5 minutes, and a high-severity audit entry is written

Scenario: Owner reset does not disturb positions
  Given a manager with open positions has lost their authenticator
  When I reset their TOTP with step-up auth
  Then their sessions are revoked and re-enrolment is forced, no order is cancelled, no position is flattened, and I was shown that state before confirming

Scenario: Reset reveals nothing
  When the reset completes
  Then no TOTP secret or recovery code is returned to me, and the target enrols a fresh secret themselves

Scenario: Elevation cannot be forged by the client
  Given a client that sets an elevation flag locally
  When it calls a dangerous route without a server-side elevation
  Then the route is refused with 403 and the attempt is audited
```

## Technical notes / design
Elevation state is the B16 interpreter's own state, not a token claim or a bolted-on counter: it is revocable and cannot be replayed on another session because each session owns exactly one B16 machine instance keyed by `session_id`. `machine_hash` for B16 covers this sub-state too (one chart, one hash). Per-tick verification of the TOTP code itself stays plain code (not a statechart concern, BENCH-2).

Elevation is stored on the session row keyed by action class with its own expiry, never in a token claim, so it is revocable and cannot be replayed on another session. The read-only downgrade is the same process-wide mechanism E09-T04 uses for unsafe binding, scoped to one session. The reset flow is a single transaction: revoke methods, revoke sessions, set `users.mfa_required`, emit audit — with the position-state snapshot fetched and displayed *before* the confirmation, not after.

## Test plan
Contract: `tests/xstate_contract/test_b16.py` (shared with E09-S03) covers the elevation sub-states, the no-grace guard for `live_enablement`/`killswitch`, and the 3-failure downgrade transition. Unit: grace-window arithmetic per action class, no-grace list, failure counter and downgrade expiry. Contract: `/auth/step-up` and the reset endpoint against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: a dangerous route called with, without and just after an expired elevation; reset with open positions asserting no OMS side effects (mocked OMS with a strict no-call assertion). E2E: SCR-006 happy path, grace display, three-failure downgrade; SCR-149 gate. Security: client-forged elevation, cross-session elevation replay, brute force on the step-up code. a11y: axe-core on SCR-006 and SCR-149 plus a manual focus-trap and announcement pass.

## Security notes
This Story exists to blunt session hijacking, so its own bypasses are the threat model: elevation forged client-side (server-side only), elevation leaked across sessions (bound to `session_id`), grace abused to chain unrelated dangerous actions (per-action-class windows), reset used as an account-takeover primitive by a compromised owner session (reset itself requires fresh step-up and is audited at critical severity with actor, target and timestamp). No secret is ever transported to the owner. All step-up codes are subject to the same replay protection as login codes.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-006 and SCR-149 are modal dialogs with focus traps, accessible names describing the action being authorised (not a generic "Confirm"), the remaining grace window stated as text, error announcements via `aria-live`, and a keyboard-operable cancel that provably abandons the action. The reset confirmation states the position-impact in text, not only in an icon or colour.

## Performance notes
The elevation check rides the existing per-request principal snapshot — no extra query, < 100 µs. The step-up endpoint itself matches the TOTP verification budget (p99 < 150 ms).

## Observability
`auth_step_up_total{action_class,outcome}`, `auth_step_up_failures_total`, `auth_readonly_downgrades_total`, `auth_mfa_resets_total`. Alerts: any `auth.mfa_reset_by_owner`, and repeated step-up failures on one session.

## Definition of Done
B16 contract test green in the blocking gate (`E50-T31`). Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, with mandatory Security engineer sign-off including the manual abuse-case checks (attempt privilege escalation, attempt the withdrawal/Live toggle without elevation), design-qa on SCR-006/SCR-149, and QA sign-off on the reset-with-open-positions scenario.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S03** (elevation lives on the session) and **E09-T03** (the gate is enforced inside the decision point).

## Branch
`feat/e09-step-up-auth`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-005, US-ONB-010; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-003, SCR-006, SCR-149, SCR-154; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-043, CMP-201, CMP-204; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/auth/step-up`, `/auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`, `/users/{userId}`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.2, §3.1.4, §3.1.5; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

title: Invite-based user creation and redemption (US-ONB-006)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-006 (Must): *"As the owner, I want to invite a manager or viewer by generating a one-time link, so that I never set someone else's password."* This is the only way a user account comes into existence in CandleViewer — there is no self-registration and no owner-set password, which removes a whole class of credential-handling risk. `users.status` starts at `invited`, `users.invited_by` records provenance, and the role is fixed at invite time and cannot be self-elevated. The endpoints are `POST /users` (create the invite) and `GET|POST /invites/{inviteToken}` (inspect and redeem).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /users` (permission `users:write`, `is_dangerous` → step-up from E09-S04): creates a `users` row with `status='invited'`, assigns the chosen role in `user_roles`, zero `user_account_access` rows, and mints a **256-bit single-use invite token stored only as a hash**, valid 72 hours.
- `GET /invites/{inviteToken}`: validates without consuming, returning the invited role and expiry for the redemption screen; rejects expired, already-redeemed and unknown tokens with one uniform message.
- **Redemption wizard SCR-017** (4 steps per `14-screens-catalogue.md`): accept invite → set password (SCR-004 embedded, CMP-201/202/203) → enrol TOTP (SCR-003 embedded, from E09-S02) → orientation card; completing all steps flips `users.status` to `active`.
- **SCR-123 Admin: invite user**: form for email, username, role, with the generated link shown once and copyable, a re-issue action for expired invites, and a pending-invite list with revoke.
- Role immutability: the role is bound to the token at creation; the redemption payload cannot alter it, and an attempt to do so is a 403 plus an audit entry.
- Audit: `users.invited` (actor, target, role), `users.invite_redeemed`, `users.invite_rejected{reason}` (severity warning for reuse), `users.invite_reissued`, `users.invite_revoked`.

## Out of scope
- Granting account access and profiles to the new user — **E27**/**E39**; a new user deliberately starts with zero bindings.
- The full admin user-list and role-editing screens — **E42**.
- Email delivery of the invite: the link is displayed to the owner to transmit out of band (there is no SMTP dependency in a Tailscale-only deployment).
- The first-run checklist the invitee then sees — **E09-S06**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Invite accepted
  Given I create an invite for role manager valid for 72 hours
  When the invitee opens the link, sets a password and enrols TOTP
  Then their account becomes active with role manager and zero account bindings

Scenario: Expired invite
  Given an invite is older than 72 hours
  When it is opened
  Then it is rejected and I can re-issue a new one from Admin

Scenario: Invite reuse
  Given an invite has already been redeemed
  When the same link is opened again
  Then it is rejected and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Role cannot be self-elevated
  Given an invite issued for role viewer
  When the redemption request is tampered with to request owner
  Then the request is refused with 403, the account is still created as viewer or not at all, and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Partially completed redemption is not usable
  Given the invitee sets a password but abandons TOTP enrolment
  Then the account remains status invited, cannot sign in to the workspace, and the invite is still consumed exactly once

Scenario: Creating an invite requires step-up
  Given my step-up grace for the users action class has expired
  When I submit the invite form
  Then I am challenged for a fresh TOTP code before the invite is minted

Scenario: The link is shown once
  When the invite is created
  Then the raw token is displayed once with a copy control and is not retrievable afterwards, only re-issuable
```

## Technical notes / design
The token is `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, stored as `sha256_hex` with its expiry and consumed-at timestamp; lookup is by hash, so a database leak does not yield usable links. Redemption is a single transaction that consumes the token, writes the password hash and (via E09-S02) the confirmed TOTP method, and flips status — so an abandoned enrolment leaves the account unusable rather than half-open. Uniform rejection messaging for unknown/expired/redeemed tokens prevents probing which links ever existed.

## Test plan
Unit: token generation entropy and hashing, expiry arithmetic, single-use consumption under concurrency (two simultaneous redemptions — exactly one wins). Contract: `POST /users`, `GET|POST /invites/{inviteToken}` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: full redemption on real Postgres asserting role, zero bindings and audit rows; re-issue after expiry. E2E: SCR-123 create → SCR-017 wizard → workspace, plus expired and reused link paths. Security: role-tampering, token brute-force rate limiting, timing uniformity across rejection reasons. a11y: axe-core on SCR-017 and SCR-123 plus a manual pass on the multi-step wizard.

## Security notes
Threats: invite interception (short 72 h life, single use, hash-at-rest, out-of-band transmission), privilege escalation via the redemption payload (role read from the stored invite only), token enumeration (256-bit space plus rate limiting plus uniform errors), and invite-farming by a compromised owner session (creation requires step-up and is audited with actor and role). The raw token is never logged, never stored, and never included in an audit `after_state`.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-017 is a multi-step wizard: each step has a heading, progress is exposed as text ("Step 2 of 4"), errors are announced and focus-managed on step transitions, and the flow is completable by keyboard alone including the embedded TOTP enrolment. SCR-123's one-time link is selectable text with a labelled copy control and an explicit warning that it will not be shown again — not conveyed by styling alone.

## Performance notes
No hot path; the only cost is the Argon2id hash when the invitee sets a password, subject to the same thread-pool bound as E09-S01. Invite lookup is a single indexed query.

## Observability
`users_invites_created_total{role}`, `users_invites_redeemed_total`, `users_invites_rejected_total{reason}`, `users_invites_pending` gauge. Alert on repeated rejections from one source (token probing).

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, with Security engineer review of the token lifecycle, design-qa against SCR-017/SCR-123, manual screen-reader pass on the wizard, and QA sign-off covering expiry, reuse and abandonment.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S04** (invite creation is a step-up-gated action). Requires **E09-S02** for the embedded enrolment step and **US-ADMIN-001** groundwork delivered here as the `POST /users` endpoint; the admin screen chrome is E42.

title: Guided first-run checklist for a new manager (US-ONB-007)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-007 (Should): a newly invited manager lands in a terminal where most things are deliberately blocked — no account bindings, possibly no API key yet, and Bybit itself refuses API-key creation for 48 hours after a sub-account is created. Without an explanation this reads as a broken product. The checklist (SCR-019 setup checklist card, embedded in SCR-017/SCR-018) tells them what is green, what is pending, and why, with a **server-verified** condition behind every step — the story's NFR is explicit: "no step may be faked client-side".

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `GET` checklist endpoint returning, per step, a server-evaluated state (`ok` / `pending` / `blocked`) plus a reason and, where applicable, an unblock timestamp: **Tailscale OK** (from E09-T04's self-check), **TOTP enrolled** (`mfa_methods.confirmed_at`), **sub-account bound** (`user_account_access`), **API key status** (E27, including the Bybit 48-hour restriction with the UTC unblock time), **profile limits** (E39/E27 account profile present), **Demo session** (a demo-environment account is reachable).
- **SCR-019 Setup checklist card** (CMP-021, CMP-023, CMP-050, CMP-097): per-step state, reason text, a countdown for the 48-hour Bybit restriction, and a call to action per step that deep-links to the owning screen.
- **SCR-018 guided tour / coach marks** wiring: first-run only, dismissible, never re-shown once the checklist completes.
- Collapse behaviour: when all steps are green the card collapses to a dismissible summary and does not reappear; dismissal is persisted server-side per user so it survives device changes.
- Graceful degradation: steps whose owning Epic has not shipped yet (API key, profile limits) render as `pending` with a "coming soon in this environment" reason driven by a feature flag, not by a client-side stub.

## Out of scope
- Creating API keys, binding sub-accounts or editing profiles — the checklist links to **E27**/**E39** screens, it does not perform those actions.
- The full onboarding wizard for the owner (SCR-016) — that is the owner's first-run, covered by E27's key setup.
- Any content that constitutes trading advice or a tutorial on strategy (advice-boundary constraint, risk R9).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Checklist shown on first sign-in
  Given I sign in for the first time as an invited manager
  Then I see steps Tailscale OK, TOTP enrolled, sub-account bound, API key status, profile limits, Demo session, each with a server-evaluated state

Scenario: 48-hour Bybit restriction is surfaced with a countdown
  Given my Bybit sub-account was created less than 48 hours ago
  Then the API key step shows that Bybit blocks API key creation until a stated UTC timestamp, with a live countdown
  And Demo exploration is offered in the meantime

Scenario: Checklist completes and stays gone
  Given all steps are green
  Then the card collapses into a dismissible summary, and after dismissal it does not reappear on any device

Scenario: A step cannot be faked from the client
  Given I tamper with local state to mark the TOTP step complete
  When the page reloads
  Then the step returns to its true server-evaluated state

Scenario: A dependency is unavailable
  Given the account service is unreachable
  Then the affected steps render an error state with a retry, the rest still render, and the card never blocks the workspace

Scenario: Keyboard and screen-reader completion
  Given I use the keyboard only
  Then every step, its call to action and the dismiss control are reachable and announced with their state as text
```

## Technical notes / design
The endpoint composes read-only probes from other modules behind a small interface so that unimplemented Epics return a typed `not_available` rather than failing the whole response; each probe has its own timeout (250 ms) and the response is assembled best-effort. The dismissal flag is a per-user preference row, not local storage, satisfying "does not reappear" across devices. The 48-hour restriction timestamp comes from the exchange-account creation time recorded in E27, not from a client clock.

## Test plan
Unit: state-derivation per step including the `not_available` and error branches; countdown formatting across the DST-free UTC boundary. Contract: the checklist response schema. Integration: probes against a seeded database in each of the six step-states. E2E: first sign-in shows the card, completing TOTP flips the step without a manual reload, tamper test, dismissal persistence across a new browser profile. a11y: axe-core on SCR-019 and SCR-018 plus a manual screen-reader pass on the coach marks.

## Security notes
Low-sensitivity surface, but it must not leak: the checklist is scoped to the requesting user and never reveals other users' accounts, key states or UIDs; the API-key step reports only a status, never key material or a masked key; probes run with the caller's own permissions through the E09-T03 decision point rather than with elevated service rights.

## Accessibility notes
Each step is a list item whose state is conveyed by text and icon, never colour alone; the countdown updates politely (`aria-live="polite"`, throttled to once per minute so it does not spam a screen reader); coach marks are dismissible by Escape, trap focus only while open, restore focus on close, and are suppressed entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion` for their animated variant per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
The composed endpoint must return in p99 < 400 ms with all probes timing out independently at 250 ms; it is called once per session start and on explicit refresh, never polled, so it adds no sustained load.

## Observability
`onboarding_checklist_views_total`, `onboarding_step_state_total{step,state}` (shows where new users actually get stuck), `onboarding_checklist_dismissed_total`, `onboarding_probe_timeouts_total{step}`.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2: automated coverage of all scenarios, ≥80% frontend coverage, design-qa against SCR-019/SCR-018, axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass, QA sign-off, demoed at Sprint Review with a freshly invited test manager, feature-flag state recorded for the not-yet-shipped steps.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S05** (there must be an invited manager to onboard). Reads data owned by **E27** (accounts, keys) and **E39** (profile limits) behind feature-flagged probes, so it can ship in R0 ahead of them.

`feat/e09-first-run-checklist`

`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-007; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-017, SCR-018, SCR-019; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-017, CMP-021, CMP-023, CMP-040, CMP-050, CMP-066, CMP-097; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.1; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.3, §3.2.1; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` R14.

title: UX research: sign-in, 2FA and recovery mental models
body:
## Context
Every human entry into CandleViewer passes through the same five surfaces: SCR-001 Login, SCR-002 TOTP challenge, SCR-003 TOTP enrolment, SCR-005 session-expired re-auth and SCR-006 step-up. They are the first thing a new manager ever sees (SCR-017) and the most frequently repeated interaction the Owner has with the product after the chart itself.

Authentication in a *trading terminal* is not the same problem as authentication in a SaaS app, and that difference is the reason this research exists rather than reusing a generic pattern. `11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-004 requires an idle lock that freezes the UI **while live data keeps streaming underneath**; US-ONB-005 requires a step-up prompt that can appear in the middle of a privileged action; SCR-005 promises that "your layout and unsent ticket inputs are preserved". A trader interrupted by an auth prompt at the wrong moment either loses a trade or, worse, learns to pre-emptively defeat the mechanism. The research must establish where the tolerance line actually is for this Owner and these managers, not where a security checklist assumes it is.

The second unknown is recovery. US-ONB-003 shows ten single-use recovery codes exactly once, hashed at rest, and US-ONB-010 lets the Owner reset another user's TOTP. Recovery-code UX is famously where users fail silently: they click through, store nothing, and discover it months later when locked out. This research establishes what storage behaviour these specific users will actually perform, so D04 can design a gate that matches reality instead of a checkbox that is always ticked without reading.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions, 45 minutes: the Owner plus up to 2 prospective account managers (P1/P2 in `10-personas.md`), run against a clickable greyscale prototype and a scripted interruption harness.
- Probe set A - **entry**: first sign-in with an invite (US-ONB-006), repeat daily sign-in, sign-in on a second device, sign-in while the account is rate-limited (US-ONB-001 5-failures/15-min lockout copy).
- Probe set B - **interruption**: idle lock firing at 15 minutes with a chart and an unsent order ticket on screen (US-ONB-004, SCR-005); absolute 12-hour expiry firing mid-session; step-up (SCR-006) demanded while rotating an API key. For each: "what do you believe happened to your data?", "what do you do next?", "what would you have wanted to happen?".
- Probe set C - **recovery**: enrolment (SCR-003) with QR and text secret, the once-only recovery-code screen, lost-authenticator recovery, exhausted codes ("contact the owner").
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md`: a ranked list of friction points, verbatim quotes, the observed recovery-code storage behaviour of each participant, and 6-10 **adopted decisions** each phrased as a testable statement a wireframe can satisfy or violate.
- A specific, evidenced recommendation on three open questions: (1) default idle timeout inside the configurable 5-60 min range of US-ONB-004; (2) whether "Remember this device (30 d)" on SCR-001 and "Trust this device for 30 days" on SCR-002 are one decision or two, and how they are worded; (3) whether the step-up grace window (5 min, US-ONB-005) must be visible as a countdown or merely stated.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design: greyscale wireframes begin in E09-D02, hi-fi in E09-D03/D04/D05/D06.
- RBAC denied-state vocabulary - that is E09-D09, which has its own sessions.
- Bybit-side authentication and API-key handling (E27).
- Password policy *content* (breach-list rules are fixed by `04-security-program.md`); only its presentation is in scope.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interruption tolerance is evidenced, not assumed
  Given all three participants have experienced the idle lock with an unsent order ticket on screen
  When docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md is reviewed
  Then it states a recommended default idle timeout with the observations that justify it
  And it records what each participant believed happened to their unsent ticket

Scenario: Recovery-code storage behaviour is observed, not self-reported
  Given a participant reaches the once-only recovery-code screen
  When they proceed past it
  Then the report records what they actually did with the codes (copied, downloaded, photographed, nothing)
  And at least one adopted decision addresses the gap between the observed behaviour and the intended one

Scenario: A participant defeats the security mechanism
  Given a participant states or demonstrates a workaround (e.g. keeping a second tab active to avoid the idle lock)
  Then the workaround is recorded verbatim as a finding
  And it is raised with the Security engineer as an input to the E09 STRIDE model rather than designed around silently

Scenario: A finding contradicts a locked document
  Given a finding contradicts 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-001..006 or an NFR in 11-user-stories.md US-ONB-001..005
  Then it is filed as an explicit amendment proposal against that document
  And no wireframe is drawn against the contradicted behaviour until the amendment is accepted or rejected

Scenario: Screen-reader participant path is covered
  Given at least one session is run with a screen reader active
  Then the report records whether the OTP entry, the QR text-secret alternative and the error announcements were usable unaided
```

## Technical notes / design
The prototype is a Figma clickable flow plus a dev-only harness page that can fire the idle lock, the absolute-expiry modal and the step-up modal on command; it must not reach production code. Auth responses are stubbed - no backend is required and none of E09's engineering work blocks this ticket, which is exactly why it sits in Sprint 01.

Validity controls: the interruption scripts are fired in a different order per participant so the severity ranking is not an artefact of ordering; participants are never told in advance that an interruption is coming.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Quality control: two researchers code the transcripts independently for the friction-point ranking and reconcile; any decision supported by a single participant is marked as such in the report rather than presented as consensus.

## Security notes
No real credentials, TOTP secrets, recovery codes or API keys appear in the prototype - fixtures only, and the QR codes encode a throwaway `otpauth://` URI. Session recordings follow `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`. Any workaround a participant reveals is shared with the Security engineer under the E09 threat-model kickoff (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1).

## Accessibility notes
One of the three sessions is run with NVDA or VoiceOver active per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8, focusing on the OTP field (announced as one field, not six), the QR text alternative and the `role="alert"` error announcement on failed sign-in. Findings feed E09-D10 directly.

## Performance notes
The prototype's perceived latency is deliberately set to the documented budgets (TOTP verify <=400 ms p95 per SCR-002, step-up token issue <=400 ms p95 per SCR-006) so participants judge the real experience rather than an instant mock.

## Observability
N/A (no production code). The analytics/audit event names the screens will emit (`auth.login.attempt`, `auth.mfa.failure`, `auth.stepup.denied`) are reviewed with participants only to confirm that nothing user-identifying beyond what `21-database-schema.md` `audit_log` already stores is implied.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report merged at `docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md` with >=6 adopted, testable decisions.
- [ ] Recommended idle-timeout default, trusted-device wording and step-up-grace treatment stated with evidence.
- [ ] Findings presented at Design Review; decisions carried into the E09-D02 wireframe scope with a line-by-line trace.
- [ ] Security engineer has received any workaround findings.
- [ ] Any contradiction with `14-screens-catalogue.md` or `11-user-stories.md` filed as an amendment proposal.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket (Status Done).

## Dependencies
- **E05** design system v0 supplies the greyscale primitives the prototype is assembled from.
- No engineering dependency by design - this ticket must not wait on E09 backend work.

`design/e09-auth-research`

title: Wireframes: end-to-end auth, session and onboarding flow
body:
## Context
E09 introduces eight user-facing surfaces that are only meaningful as a *sequence*: SCR-001 Login → SCR-002 TOTP → (first time) SCR-003 enrolment → (if forced) SCR-004 password change → SCR-010 App shell, with SCR-005 and SCR-006 able to interrupt any authenticated screen at any moment, and SCR-017/SCR-019 wrapping the whole thing for an invited manager. `14-screens-catalogue.md` section 0 draws exactly this chain (`L → T → SH`) as the first flow in the document.

Drawing them individually in hi-fi first would guarantee seams: a back-button that leads nowhere, a state ("expired challenge") that returns to a screen with no matching entry message, an invited user who lands in SCR-003 with no idea they are mid-wizard. This ticket fixes the **structure and state machine** in greyscale, cheaply, so that E09-D03..D06 only have to solve visual and interaction detail inside an agreed skeleton.

The research from E09-D01 is a required input: its adopted decisions on interruption handling, trusted-device wording and recovery-code gating are what the wireframes are measured against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Greyscale wireframes in Figma (`CV / E09 Auth / Wireframes`) for every screen and every enumerated state:
  - **SCR-001 Login**: idle, submitting, generic error, rate-limited with countdown, account-disabled, server-unreachable (SCR-152 inline variant), plus the server env badge (CMP-075) and build footer (CMP-207).
  - **SCR-002 TOTP challenge**: idle, verifying, invalid code, expired challenge, locked-after-5, recovery-code entry path.
  - **SCR-003 TOTP enrolment wizard**: 3 steps (scan / confirm / recovery codes) plus the re-enrol variant triggered by US-ONB-010 owner reset and by recovery-code consumption.
  - **SCR-004 Forced password change**: policy-shown-up-front, typing, server rejection (reused password / breached password), success.
  - **SCR-005 Session expired / re-auth modal**: default, expiry-during-order-entry, "sign out instead" branch.
  - **SCR-006 Step-up modal**: code only, code + typed confirmation, remaining-grace variant, failure and 3-strike downgrade (US-ONB-005).
  - **SCR-017 Manager/viewer onboarding wizard** (4 steps) and **SCR-019 Setup checklist**, including the role-scoped task sets.
- A single **state-machine diagram** (mermaid, contributed to `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`) covering the full chain including every failure edge: wrong password, disabled account, rate limit, expired MFA challenge, recovery-code consumption forcing re-enrolment, exhausted recovery codes, idle lock, absolute expiry, step-up denial.
- A **states matrix** (screen x state x role) as a Figma page, the artefact E09-D03..D06 and E09-D11 both check against.
- An explicit annotation on every screen naming the CMP-* it is composed from (`18-traceability-matrix.md` rows for US-ONB-001..008 are the source list) and flagging any component that does not yet exist, as an input to E09-D07.
- Proposed amendments to `14-screens-catalogue.md` where the wireframes reveal a missing state, raised as a doc PR rather than an undocumented divergence.

## Out of scope
- Colour, type, iconography, elevation, motion - hi-fi work is E09-D03..D06; motion is E09-D08.
- Admin-side user management screens (SCR-120, SCR-121, SCR-123) - owned by the admin epic; this ticket only draws the *invitee's* side of the invite flow.
- The RBAC denied-state pattern (E09-D09) and the admin re-auth gate SCR-149 (drawn in E09-D06 only as the step-up variant it reuses).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every documented state is drawn
  Given the states matrix is compared against the States bullets of SCR-001..006, SCR-017 and SCR-019 in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the comparison is run at design review
  Then every enumerated state has a corresponding frame
  And any state present in the wireframes but absent from the catalogue is filed as a catalogue amendment

Scenario: No dead ends in the flow
  Given the mermaid state machine
  When each terminal node is inspected
  Then every node either reaches the app shell, reaches an explicitly designed terminal state with a recovery action, or names the human who can unblock the user

Scenario: Recovery-code exhaustion is designed, not deferred
  Given a user has consumed all ten recovery codes and has lost their authenticator
  When the wireframes are walked
  Then a frame exists showing the exact message, the owner-contact path and what the user can still see (nothing) while locked out

Scenario: Interruption preserves context visibly
  Given the SCR-005 wireframe fires over a workspace with an unsent order ticket
  Then the underlying screen is shown frozen and preserved rather than blanked
  And the frame annotates that WS subscriptions pause rather than tear down, per SCR-005

Scenario: Research decisions are traced
  Given the adopted decisions in docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md
  When the wireframe review runs
  Then each decision is marked satisfied by a named frame, or consciously rejected with a recorded reason
```

## Technical notes / design
The wireframes are assembled from E05's greyscale primitives only - no bespoke boxes - so that the CMP-* annotation is honest and the gap list handed to E09-D07 is complete.

Two structural decisions must be settled here and recorded on the matrix, because they change engineering shape and cannot be discovered in hi-fi: (1) whether SCR-003 enrolment is a standalone route (`/login/2fa/enroll`) or an embedded step inside SCR-017's wizard - the catalogue implies both, and the answer determines whether enrolment is routable and resumable; (2) whether SCR-005 (idle/expiry) and SCR-006 (step-up) share one modal chassis with variants or are two distinct organisms - this determines whether CMP-098 composes CMP-043 or stands alone.

The mermaid diagram is authored to be mergeable into `13-user-flows.md`, not as a Figma picture, so it stays reviewable in PRs.

## Test plan
Design-side verification only: (a) a walkthrough with the Architect confirming every frame's data needs map to an operation that exists in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/auth/login`, `/auth/mfa/verify`, `/auth/mfa/enroll`, `/auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `/auth/mfa/recovery`, `/auth/password`, `/auth/step-up`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/sessions`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`); (b) a keyboard-path dry run on paper - tab order annotated on every frame; (c) a QA review to confirm each state is externally observable and therefore testable.

## Security notes
The wireframes must not introduce a user-enumeration channel: the error copy for wrong-password, unknown-user and disabled-account is reviewed against US-ONB-001's NFR ("no hint about which was wrong") - the disabled-account message is the one deliberate exception the story allows and is annotated as such for the Security engineer to confirm. The rate-limit countdown must not reveal whether the account exists. No frame displays a TOTP secret or recovery code anywhere other than SCR-003 step 1/3.

## Accessibility notes
Every frame carries an annotation layer with: heading level, tab order, focus-on-entry target, focus-return target on dismissal, the `role`/`aria-live` of each error region (per SCR-001 `role="alert"`, SCR-005/SCR-006 `role="alertdialog"`), and the non-colour signalling of each state. Per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 3 no path may be mouse-only, and per WCAG 2.2.1 the idle lock must be preceded by the CMP-098 warning rather than firing silently.

## Performance notes
The wireframes annotate the budgets the hi-fi work must not break: SCR-001 first paint <=1 s cold with no chart bundle on the route (code-split), SCR-002 verify round-trip <=400 ms p95 with auto-submit on the 6th digit and no extra render pass, SCR-003 QR render <=100 ms client-side from the provisioning URI, SCR-005 modal mount <=100 ms.

## Observability
Each frame annotates the audit/analytics event it emits (`auth.login.attempt|success|failure|rate_limited`, `auth.mfa.success|failure|recovery_used`, `auth.mfa.enrolled`, `auth.mfa.recovery_generated`, `auth.password.changed`, `auth.session.expired|reauth`, `auth.stepup.granted|denied`, `onboarding.*`) so the engineering tickets inherit the list rather than inventing it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states in the matrix drawn and reviewed; matrix published in Figma and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Mermaid state machine merged into `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`.
- [ ] CMP gap list handed to E09-D07; catalogue amendments raised as doc PRs.
- [ ] Architect walkthrough complete - every data need maps to an existing `22-api-openapi.yaml` operation.
- [ ] Accessibility annotation layer complete on every frame.
- [ ] Two structural decisions (enrolment routing, modal chassis) recorded as written decisions on the ticket.

title: Hi-fi design: Login and TOTP challenge (SCR-001, SCR-002)
body:
## Context
SCR-001 and SCR-002 are the two screens every user sees every day and the only two screens a hostile visitor could ever reach. They therefore carry a double burden: they must be fast and forgettable for the Owner, and they must leak nothing to anyone else. `11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-001 fixes the security behaviour (argon2id, per-account and per-IP rate limiting at 5 failures/15 minutes, constant-time comparison, no user enumeration) and US-ONB-002 fixes the TOTP behaviour (RFC 6238, 30 s step, +/-1 step skew, replay-protected). This ticket turns the agreed wireframe skeleton into the final, buildable visual and interaction specification.

Two details make these screens more than a generic login. First, SCR-001 renders the **server's** environment badge (CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal: "server: DEMO default" / "Live-enabled") before authentication - the user must know which machine they are about to trade on before they commit a credential. Second, the 6-digit field (CMP-204 OtpInput) auto-submits on the sixth character, which means a paste, a typo and a screen-reader interaction all have to behave correctly without a visible submit press.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames, dark theme and light theme, at 1280x800 and 2560x1440, plus a 125% browser-zoom pass, for:
  - **SCR-001**: idle, focused, submitting (button busy, fields locked), generic error (`role="alert"`, focus moved to it), rate-limited with a live countdown ("Too many attempts. Try again in 14:32."), account-disabled, server-unreachable inline variant, caps-lock warning on the password field.
  - **SCR-002**: idle, per-digit fill, paste-of-6, verifying, invalid code, code-expiry countdown, expired challenge returning to SCR-001 with its entry message, locked-after-5-attempts, and the "Use a recovery code" alternate entry with its own idle/error states.
- Final composition from published library components only: CMP-200 AuthCard, CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-007 TextInput, CMP-005 Checkbox, CMP-001 Button, CMP-021 Link, CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-207 BuildFooter.
- Final **copy deck** for both screens: every label, helper, error and countdown string, reviewed against the no-enumeration rule and written at plain-English reading level.
- Interaction spec: Enter submits; tab order username → password → remember → submit; OTP auto-advance, paste-fill, Backspace-steps-back, auto-submit on the 6th digit; what happens to focus on every error.
- Redlines and token references for every spacing, colour, radius and type decision (no raw values).
- Updated `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001/SCR-002 entries so the catalogue matches the final artefact exactly (`16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.3.2).

## Out of scope
- Enrolment (E09-D04), forced password change (E09-D05), session/step-up modals (E09-D06).
- Motion curves and reduced-motion variants - specified once for the whole auth band in E09-D08.
- Any new component's full design-system entry - gaps go to E09-D07.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The screen never reveals whether an account exists
  Given the copy deck for SCR-001
  When wrong-password, unknown-username and rate-limited states are compared
  Then the visible message, the layout and the state timing are indistinguishable between unknown-username and wrong-password
  And the Security engineer has recorded that confirmation on the ticket

Scenario: The environment is unmistakable before sign-in
  Given the SCR-001 frame in both themes
  When it is viewed in greyscale and through a deuteranopia simulation
  Then a Live-enabled server is distinguishable from a Demo-default server by text and shape, not colour alone

Scenario: Six-digit entry survives a paste
  Given the SCR-002 interaction spec
  When a user pastes six digits into any cell
  Then all six cells fill, the code auto-submits once, and the spec states that no second submission can be triggered by the subsequent blur

Scenario: Lockout is honest about time
  Given the rate-limited state of SCR-001 and the locked-after-5 state of SCR-002
  Then both show a remaining time derived from a server-provided expiry, annotated as such
  And neither offers a control that appears to retry while locked

Scenario: Zoom does not break the card
  Given the 125% zoom pass at 1280x800
  Then no content is clipped or requires two-dimensional scrolling and the error region remains visible with the field it describes

Scenario: An error moves focus exactly once
  Given a failed sign-in
  Then focus moves to the alert region, the alert is announced once, and returning focus to the form does not re-announce it
```

## Technical notes / design
The route is code-split and must not pull the chart bundle (SCR-001 performance note), so the design may not depend on any engine-rendered surface, background animation or webfont that is not already in the core bundle.

The OTP field is specified as **one** control to assistive technology with six visual cells - the visual treatment must therefore survive being a single focus stop: the "current cell" indication is a rendered caret position, not six independently focusable inputs. `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-204 already binds this contract; this ticket must not contradict it.

The "Remember this device (30 d)" checkbox on SCR-001 and "Trust this device for 30 days" on SCR-002 are resolved per the E09-D01 recommendation - if they remain two controls, the frames must make clear that they mean different things, since one suppresses a password and the other suppresses a factor.

## Test plan
Design verification: axe-style manual audit of the Figma prototype annotations; contrast measurement of every text/background and every focus ring against `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 5 (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text and focus indicators) in both themes; a keyboard-only click-through of the prototype; CVD simulation (protan/deutan/tritan) of both themes. Results attached to the ticket and reused as the baseline for E09-D11 design QA.

## Security notes
No frame may display a password in plain text except behind the explicit CMP-201 reveal toggle; no frame shows a partially masked username as a hint. The build footer (CMP-207) shows version and Tailscale node name - reviewed with Security to confirm that exposing the version pre-auth is acceptable given Tailscale-only reachability (US-ONB-008), and annotated with that decision. Error copy is reviewed against the enumeration rule as an explicit sign-off line, not a general assurance.

## Accessibility notes
Target WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Specific gates: labelled inputs with `aria-describedby` for errors; error region `role="alert"` receiving focus on failure; `autocomplete="username"` / `"current-password"` / `"one-time-code"`; the OTP group carries one accessible name ("Six-digit authentication code"); the caps-lock warning is a polite live region; the countdown updates politely and never more than once per second; no focus trap on either page; the recovery-code path is reachable by keyboard from SCR-002.

## Performance notes
SCR-001 first paint <=1 s cold. The design must not require a blocking webfont load for the first paint, nor an image asset over 20 KB, nor any pre-auth network call beyond `GET /api/v1/system/build`. SCR-002 auto-submits on the sixth character with no extra render pass - the spec must not introduce an animation that delays submission.

## Observability
Frames annotate the events emitted: `auth.login.attempt`, `auth.login.success`, `auth.login.failure` (audited with source IP per US-ONB-001), `auth.login.rate_limited`, `auth.mfa.success`, `auth.mfa.failure`, `auth.mfa.recovery_used` (high severity). The annotation states explicitly that no event carries the submitted password or code.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Composed only from published library components; any gap raised to E09-D07.
- [ ] Copy deck complete and enumeration-reviewed with the Security engineer.

- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001/SCR-002 updated to match the final artefact.

title: Hi-fi design: TOTP enrolment, recovery codes and owner reset
body:
## Context
SCR-003 is the only screen in CandleViewer that shows a secret exactly once and never again. US-ONB-003 requires TOTP enrolment on first login and ten single-use recovery codes, hashed at rest, displayed once, with copy and download. US-ONB-010 lets the Owner reset another user's TOTP, which re-enters the same wizard in a re-enrol variant. US-ONB-003's third scenario - all ten codes consumed - ends outside the product entirely ("contact the owner"), and that dead end must be designed rather than discovered.

This screen is where E09-D01's most uncomfortable finding lands: users click past recovery codes without storing them. The design's job is to make the storage step genuinely load-bearing without turning it into a lie the user learns to click through. The catalogue already requires an "I saved them" gate before step 3 can be left; the hi-fi work has to make that gate *earn* its checkbox.

The QR itself has two hard constraints: the quiet zone must stay pure white in the dark theme or scanners fail (CMP-205 explicitly forbids a themed tint), and the secret must always also be available as selectable text so QR scanning is never the only path (US-ONB-003 NFR, `05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames, dark + light, 1280x800 and 2560x1440, 125% zoom pass, for:
  - **SCR-003 step 1 Scan**: QR (CMP-205) plus the manual secret in a `<code>` block with CMP-033 CopyButton, issuer/account label as it will appear in the authenticator, and the "can't scan?" path.
  - **SCR-003 step 2 Confirm**: CMP-204 OtpInput, verifying, wrong-code, expired-enrolment-challenge.
  - **SCR-003 step 3 Recovery codes**: CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList with copy / download `.txt` / print, the once-only warning, the "I saved them" gate, and the post-gate confirmation.
  - **Re-enrol variant** (existing factor present): the extra step-up confirmation, the "your old authenticator stops working" warning, and the "old recovery codes are invalidated" warning.
  - **Owner-initiated reset landing** (US-ONB-010): what the *reset user* sees on next sign-in, including who reset it and when.
  - **Recovery-code consumption path**: signing in with a recovery code, the forced re-enrolment that follows (US-ONB-003 scenario 2), and the remaining-codes count.
  - **Exhausted-codes terminal state**: the message, the owner-contact path, and what remains visible (nothing).
  - **SCR-112 Security settings** sections owned by E09: regenerate recovery codes (with the "old codes stop working" warning), re-enrol TOTP, disable TOTP behind step-up.
- Wizard chrome spec: CMP-066 Stepper behaviour, back/forward semantics, and resume-from-server-stored-step (SCR-016 performance note applies equally here - an interrupted wizard resumes from the server, not client memory).
- Copy deck for every string, including the four warnings (once-only, old-authenticator, old-codes-invalidated, exhausted).
- Updated `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-003 and the SCR-112 auth sections.

## Out of scope
- The Admin-side "force 2FA re-enrol" row action on SCR-121 - that is the admin epic's surface; this ticket designs only what the affected user experiences.
- Password change (E09-D05) even though SCR-112 hosts both.
- Motion (E09-D08) and the RBAC denied-state pattern (E09-D09).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The secret is never QR-only
  Given the SCR-003 step 1 frame in both themes
  Then the base32 secret is present as selectable text with a copy control
  And the QR carries an accessible name stating what it is rather than the secret itself

Scenario: The QR stays scannable in the dark theme
  Given the dark-theme step 1 frame
  When the QR quiet zone is measured
  Then it renders on an untinted surface at the contrast the scanner needs
  And the frame annotates that the QR never inherits the theme surface token

Scenario: The storage gate is not a reflex click
  Given a user reaches step 3
  When they attempt to continue without copying, downloading or printing
  Then the design states the exact friction applied and the evidence from E09-D01 that justifies it
  And the codes cannot be recovered after leaving the step, which is stated before the gate rather than after it

Scenario: Re-enrolment invalidates loudly
  Given a user with an existing factor enters the re-enrol variant
  Then the frame states that the previous authenticator and the previous recovery codes both stop working
  And the destructive confirmation names the consequence in words, not an icon

Scenario: Exhaustion is a designed terminal state
  Given all ten recovery codes are consumed and the authenticator is lost
  Then a frame exists showing the message, the owner-contact instruction and the absence of any self-service path

Scenario: A screen-reader user can complete enrolment unaided
  Given the annotation layer for all three steps
  Then each step announces its position, the secret is reachable as text, the OTP group is a single named control, and the recovery codes are a list that can be read item by item
```

## Technical notes / design
The QR is rendered client-side from the `otpauth://` provisioning URI returned by `POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll`; the secret does not round-trip for rendering and the design must not require a server-rendered image (SCR-003 performance note, <=100 ms render).

The recovery-code download is a plain `.txt` per the catalogue - the copy deck must specify the file's contents and header line, including which account and server the codes belong to, because a user with two environments will otherwise have two indistinguishable files.

The re-enrol variant is gated by step-up (SCR-006) rather than reimplementing a confirmation - the frames reference E09-D06's modal rather than drawing a second one.

The enrolment route's standalone-vs-embedded decision was fixed in E09-D02; these frames implement that decision and must not reopen it.

## Test plan
Contrast and CVD audit of both themes including the QR quiet zone; keyboard-only completion of all three steps plus the re-enrol variant in the prototype; screen-reader walkthrough of step 1 (text secret), step 2 (OTP) and step 3 (code list); a scanner test - the final QR spec is rendered at the specified size and contrast and scanned with at least two authenticator apps before sign-off.

## Security notes
Highest-sensitivity screen in E09. Hard rules the frames must honour and annotate: the secret and the recovery codes appear in exactly one place each and are never re-displayed; nothing here may be captured in analytics, session replay or a screenshot-based support flow; the `.txt` download and the clipboard are the only exfiltration paths and both are deliberate; the codes are hashed at rest so no screen can ever show them again, which the copy must state as fact rather than warning. The re-enrol and disable paths require a fresh step-up token (US-ONB-005), and "disable TOTP" must never be reachable without it. Reviewed jointly with the Security engineer under the E09 STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Specific gates: QR `role="img"` with a descriptive name plus the text-secret equivalent (this is the named alternative, not a nicety); the stepper exposes `aria-current="step"`; recovery codes are a semantic list, each item individually readable, with a monospace face chosen for character disambiguation (0/O, 1/l); the "I saved them" gate is a real checkbox with a label that states the consequence; all warnings are text, never colour or icon alone; no step depends on a time limit.

## Performance notes
QR render <=100 ms client-side. The design may not require a QR library larger than the budget agreed with FE, nor an animated transition between wizard steps that delays the code field's focus. Step transitions <=200 ms per SCR-017's wizard budget.

## Observability
Frames annotate `auth.mfa.enrolled`, `auth.mfa.recovery_generated`, `auth.mfa.recovery_used` (high severity), `auth.recovery_regenerated`, and the US-ONB-010 owner-reset audit entry, with an explicit note that no event payload contains the secret, the codes or their hashes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All frames and variants drawn in both themes at both resolutions plus 125% zoom.
- [ ] Scanner test passed with >=2 authenticator apps against the dark-theme spec.
- [ ] Copy deck complete including the `.txt` file contents and all four warnings.
- [ ] Security engineer review recorded on the ticket (secret/code handling, step-up gating).
- [ ] Accessibility acceptance-criteria template completed and attached; screen-reader walkthrough logged.
- [ ] Design QA checklist completed and attached.
- [ ] Data/API contract confirmed against `/auth/mfa/enroll`, `/auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `/auth/mfa/recovery`, `/auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-003 and SCR-112 auth sections updated.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done); downstream FE story moved to Ready with the Figma link.

## Dependencies
- **E09-D02** wireframes, states matrix and the enrolment-routing decision.
- **E09-D06** supplies the step-up modal the re-enrol and disable paths reuse (may run in parallel; the link must exist before sign-off).

title: Hi-fi design: forced password change & password policy surface
body:
## Context
SCR-004 is shown whenever the server sets `mustChangePassword`: a newly invited user redeeming an invite (US-ONB-006), a user whose password the Owner reset, or a password that has aged past policy. It is a screen the user cannot dismiss, which makes clarity the whole design problem - a forced screen that fails silently traps the user with no escape.

The policy is fixed and non-negotiable (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-004): at least 12 characters, not present in a known breach list, not equal to any of the previous 5, must match confirmation. Two of those four can only be evaluated by the server, which means the screen has a genuine split: client-side rules that must be visible *before* typing (CMP-203 RequirementChecklist), and server-side rejections that can only arrive after submission and must not read as a bug.

The same password surface is reused, unforced, inside SCR-112 Security settings, so the specification has to cover both a blocking page and an embedded section without forking the visual language.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames, dark + light, 1280x800 and 2560x1440, 125% zoom:
  - **SCR-004 blocking page**: entry state with the full policy listed before typing, typing with live checklist updates, strength feedback (CMP-202 PasswordStrengthMeter), confirmation-mismatch, submitting, server rejection for breached password, server rejection for reuse-of-last-5, success and onward routing.
  - **Entry-reason variants**: three distinct explanations for why the user is here (new account, owner reset, password aged out) - the user must know which one applies to them.
  - **SCR-112 embedded variant**: voluntary change with a current-password field, success confirmation, and the statement of what else it invalidates (or does not).
- Copy deck: the four policy strings, the three entry-reason explanations, both server rejections, the mismatch message, and the success message. Messages are taken verbatim from SCR-004 where the catalogue already fixes them ("Use at least 12 characters.", "This password appears in a known breach list.", "Passwords don't match.").
- Strength-meter specification: the mapping from score 0-4 to the text labels, and the rule that the meter is advisory while the checklist is normative - a strong-scoring password that fails a policy rule must not look acceptable.
- Redlines, token references, tab order and focus behaviour.
- Updated `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-004 entry.

## Out of scope
- Choosing or changing the policy itself (owned by `04-security-program.md`).
- The Owner-side "reset password" action on SCR-121 (admin epic).
- Invite redemption chrome around this step (E09-D07's wizard work).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The rules are visible before the first keystroke
  Given the SCR-004 entry frame
  Then all four policy requirements are listed as text before any input has been typed
  And none of them is discoverable only as a post-submission error

Scenario: A server-side rejection is not mistaken for a fault
  Given a user submits a password that appears in the breach list
  Then the frame shows the rejection attached to the password field with the exact catalogue copy
  And the previously entered value is retained or explicitly cleared, with the frame stating which and why

Scenario: Strength never overrides policy
  Given a password that scores Strong on the meter but repeats one of the previous five
  Then the design states that the submit outcome is failure and the checklist, not the meter, carries the authority

Scenario: The screen is not colour-dependent
  Given the checklist and the strength meter in greyscale and under CVD simulation
  Then met and unmet requirements are distinguishable by text, and strength is readable as a word

Scenario: A forced screen has no silent trap
  Given the user cannot dismiss SCR-004
  Then the frame provides a visible sign-out escape and states what happens to the session if they take it

Scenario: Live validation does not flood a screen reader
  Given a user typing a password with a screen reader active
  Then the checklist announcement is debounced and announces the changed requirement, not the whole list, on each change
```

## Technical notes / design
Policy evaluation for the client-side rules is synchronous and local (SCR-004 performance note: strength meter updates within one frame, <=16 ms), so the design may not depend on a per-keystroke network call. The breach-list and reuse checks are server-side only and arrive from `PUT /api/v1/auth/password`; the frames must therefore show a submitting state long enough to be real rather than assuming instant validation.

The strength meter's scoring source (zxcvbn-class estimator vs a simpler rule set) is an FE decision, but the design fixes the *label vocabulary* so the two cannot drift; the labels are text-first per CMP-202.

The embedded SCR-112 variant differs from the blocking page in exactly two ways - a current-password field and a dismissible surround - and the spec states that so FE builds one component with a `forced` variant rather than two screens.

## Test plan
Contrast and CVD audit both themes; keyboard-only completion including the reveal toggle; screen-reader pass over the checklist's live region with a realistic typing cadence to confirm the debounce is sufficient; a copy review with the Owner confirming the three entry-reason explanations are distinguishable to a non-technical reader.

## Security notes
The password is never echoed except behind the explicit CMP-201 reveal control, and paste must never be blocked (CMP-201 contract - password managers are a security control, not a threat). The breach-list rejection must not indicate *where* the password was breached or how many times, as that is an information leak with no user value. No frame may suggest a password hint field exists. The success state must state whether other sessions are revoked, which is a behaviour the Security engineer confirms rather than the designer assumes.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Gates: the requirement checklist is a `<ul>` whose items pair state with the words "met"/"not met" in the accessible name, wrapped in `aria-live="polite"` and debounced to 500 ms per CMP-203/CMP-202; the strength meter is a word plus a bar, never a bar alone; errors use `aria-describedby` on the field they belong to; `autocomplete="new-password"` on both entry fields; focus moves to the first failing field on server rejection.

## Performance notes
Client-side policy evaluation and strength scoring complete within one frame (<=16 ms) for a 64-character input; the design may not require a layout-shifting checklist (reserved height) since shifting content under a typing user is both a perf and a usability failure.

## Observability
Frames annotate `auth.password.changed` and the failure counterpart, with a note that neither event carries the password, its hash, or the strength score.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states and the three entry-reason variants drawn in both themes at both resolutions plus 125% zoom.
- [ ] Copy deck complete and reviewed with the Owner for plain-language clarity.
- [ ] Contrast + CVD + keyboard + screen-reader audits attached.
- [ ] Accessibility acceptance-criteria template completed and attached.
- [ ] Design QA checklist completed and attached.
- [ ] Data/API contract confirmed against `PUT /api/v1/auth/password`; session-revocation behaviour on success confirmed with the Security engineer and annotated.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-004 updated to match the artefact.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done); downstream FE story moved to Ready with the Figma link.

## Dependencies
- **E09-D02** wireframes and states matrix.
- **E05** design-system v0 (CMP-200, CMP-201, CMP-202, CMP-203 published).

## Branch

- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-201, CMP-202, CMP-203

title: Hi-fi design: idle lock, session-expiry re-auth and step-up modals
body:
## Context
SCR-005 and SCR-006 are the only E09 surfaces that appear **on top of a live trading workspace**, and that single fact makes them the riskiest designs in the epic. US-ONB-004 requires the idle lock to freeze the UI while live data keeps streaming underneath, to not tear down WS subscriptions (a reconnect storm is a real operational failure), to disable order entry while locked, and to return the user to exactly the same workspace and scroll position. US-ONB-005 requires step-up to demand a fresh TOTP for privileged actions, with a 5-minute grace that never applies to Live enablement or kill-switch disable, and a 3-strike failure that downgrades the session to read-only for 5 minutes and audits as high severity.

Get these wrong in either direction and the cost is concrete. Too aggressive: a trader is locked out mid-position and learns to defeat the timer. Too lax: a hijacked session rotates an API key. E09-D01's interruption findings are the evidence base for where that line sits.

SCR-149 (admin re-auth gate, 15-minute admin token) is the same pattern in a third dress; this ticket designs the chassis once so it is not reinvented by the admin epic.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames, dark + light, 1280x800 and 2560x1440, 125% zoom, drawn **over a realistic workspace** (chart + DOM + order ticket) rather than over an empty canvas:
  - **CMP-098 SessionTimeoutWarning**: the pre-lock warning at the agreed threshold, its extend action, and its dismissal - required by WCAG 2.2.1, so a silent auto-lock is not an option.
  - **SCR-005 idle lock / session expired**: locked state with live data visibly continuing underneath, password re-auth entry, verifying, wrong password, absolute-expiry variant (full sign-out, armed one-click trading disarmed per US-ONB-004), "sign out instead" branch, and the expiry-during-order-entry case where a draft ticket is retained but unarmed.
  - **SCR-006 step-up modal**: code-only, code + typed confirmation (the exact target restated verbatim), valid-grace variant with a remaining-TTL indicator sourced from a server expiry, failure 1 and 2, the 3rd failure and the resulting read-only downgrade banner, and the no-grace-allowed variant for Live enablement and kill-switch disable.
  - **SCR-149 admin re-auth gate** as a declared variant of the same chassis (password + TOTP, 15-minute unlock, the "why am I seeing this" explanation).
- A written **interruption policy** covering: what is frozen vs what keeps moving, whether alerts and toasts can still fire behind the lock, what happens to an in-flight order at the moment of lock, and what the user sees on return. This is a design decision with engineering and risk consequences and must be signed off by the Architect and the Owner, not only the CDO.
- Copy deck for all three surfaces including the read-only downgrade banner and the grace explanation.
- Updated `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-005, SCR-006 and the SCR-149 cross-reference.

## Out of scope
- The risk/kill-switch surfaces that *call* step-up (E39) - only the modal and its contract are designed here.
- Admin route guarding beyond the SCR-149 gate's own visual (admin epic).
- The RBAC read-only vocabulary reused by the downgrade banner - defined in E09-D09, referenced here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The workspace is frozen, not destroyed
  Given the SCR-005 locked frame over a live workspace
  Then the underlying chart and ladder are visibly present and visibly not interactive
  And the frame annotates that WS subscriptions are paused rather than torn down

Scenario: Order entry cannot survive the lock
  Given an armed one-click ticket at the moment the absolute session lifetime expires
  Then the frame shows the ticket disarmed and states that arming is not restored automatically on return

Scenario: Step-up names what it is authorising
  Given the step-up modal is raised for rotating an API key on account sub_002
  Then the exact action and target are restated verbatim in the dialog and in its accessible description
  And the Confirm control is disabled until both the code and the typed confirmation are valid

Scenario: Grace is honest and bounded
  Given a step-up token issued 3 minutes ago
  When a second action of the same class is attempted
  Then the remaining validity is shown from a server-provided expiry, never a client clock
  And a Live-enablement or kill-switch-disable action shows no grace at all, as a separate frame

Scenario: Three failures downgrade visibly
  Given three consecutive invalid step-up codes
  Then the action is abandoned, a read-only downgrade banner with its expiry is drawn, and the frame annotates the high-severity audit event

Scenario: A warning always precedes the lock
  Given the idle timer is about to elapse
  Then CMP-098 appears at the agreed threshold with a keyboard-operable extend action
  And no frame in this set shows the lock appearing without that warning

Scenario: Focus is trapped and returned
  Given SCR-005 or SCR-006 is open
  Then focus is trapped inside the dialog, Escape does not dismiss SCR-005, and on resolution focus returns to the control that triggered the action
```

## Technical notes / design
SCR-005 and SCR-006 share one chassis with variants; the E09-D02 decision on whether that chassis is CMP-043 Dialog + CMP-098 or a distinct organism is implemented here and must not be reopened. The typed-confirmation pattern is CMP-044 ConfirmDialog `variant="typed"` and is reused verbatim rather than re-drawn.

The remaining-TTL indicator is rendered from the server expiry returned by `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up` (SCR-006 performance note); the design must tolerate a clock that disagrees with the client by showing time-remaining rather than an absolute local time.

The lock overlay must not repaint the workspace beneath it - a full-screen blur or a heavy backdrop filter over a running WebGL chart is a measurable frame-rate cost and is explicitly forbidden unless E09-D08's motion measurement clears it.

## Test plan
Prototype walkthrough of all three surfaces over a live-looking workspace; contrast and CVD audit including the overlay scrim over both a dark chart and a light chart; keyboard-only pass verifying trap, Escape semantics and focus return; screen-reader pass verifying `role="alertdialog"`, the accessible description naming the action, and assertive announcement of failures; a timing review with QA confirming every state in the interruption policy is observable and therefore testable.

## Security notes
The step-up modal is the last gate before key rotation, Live enablement and kill-switch changes, so its design is reviewed by the Security engineer as part of the E09 STRIDE model. Rules: the dialog must never be dismissible by clicking the scrim; the typed confirmation is case-sensitive and compared exactly; the action being authorised is server-supplied text, never client-composed, so the dialog cannot be made to lie about its target; the read-only downgrade after three failures is a server-enforced state that the UI reflects, and the frame must not imply the user can clear it client-side; no frame displays the step-up token.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, with WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable) as a hard gate: the CMP-098 warning before the idle lock is mandatory and must offer extension. SCR-005 and SCR-006 are `role="alertdialog"` with focus starting on the code/password field; Escape does not dismiss SCR-005; failures announce via `aria-live="assertive"`; the reason for step-up is text, never an icon; the remaining-TTL indicator is announced politely at meaningful intervals rather than every second.

## Performance notes
SCR-005 mounts <=100 ms; step-up token issue <=400 ms p95. The overlay may not trigger a full re-composite of the WebGL surfaces beneath it - the design specifies a cheap scrim and states the forbidden alternatives (backdrop blur over the chart canvas). Paused-not-torn-down subscriptions mean no reconnect storm on resume, which the annotation states as a design requirement, not an implementation detail.

## Observability
Frames annotate `auth.session.expired`, `auth.session.reauth`, `auth.stepup.granted`, `auth.stepup.denied` (with the target action key), and the high-severity 3-strike downgrade event. The annotation states that the audit record carries the action key and target, never the submitted code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All frames and variants drawn over a realistic workspace in both themes at both resolutions plus 125% zoom.
- [ ] Written interruption policy signed off by the Architect and the Owner as well as the CDO.
- [ ] Security engineer review recorded (step-up gating, non-dismissibility, server-supplied action text).

- [ ] Accessibility acceptance-criteria template completed and attached.

- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-005, SCR-006 updated; SCR-149 annotated as a variant of this chassis.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done); downstream FE stories moved to Ready with the Figma link.

- **E09-D01** interruption findings (idle default, grace visibility).
