title: Design-system contribution: auth component band CMP-200..206 + CMP-097/098
body:
## Context
`15-component-catalogue.md` band 8 exists precisely because the auth surfaces composed components that no other band covered: CMP-200 AuthCard, CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-202 PasswordStrengthMeter, CMP-203 RequirementChecklist, CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-205 QrCode, CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList, plus CMP-207 BuildFooter, and the onboarding/session pair CMP-097 OnboardingChecklist and CMP-098 SessionTimeoutWarning. Each is listed in the catalogue with a purpose, props sketch, a11y contract, token list, Storybook set and test requirements - but listed is not the same as **published**.

This ticket promotes them from screen-specific drawings inside E09-D03..D06 into published, variant-complete library components with the same status as the atoms in band 1. That matters beyond tidiness: the design-system Definition of Done (`16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.3.1) requires every screen to be composed **only** from published-library components, so until this ticket lands, every auth screen is technically non-conformant, and any later screen that needs an OTP field (step-up, admin re-auth, a future confirmation) will fork a copy.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Published Figma library components, dark + light, all density modes the brief defines, for:
  - **CMP-200 AuthCard** - variants: Default, WithError, Busy, WithFooter.
  - **CMP-201 PasswordField** - Default, Revealed, CapsLockOn, WithError; paste never suppressed.
  - **CMP-202 PasswordStrengthMeter** - Weak, Fair, Strong, WithFeedback; text-first.
  - **CMP-203 RequirementChecklist** - NoneMet, PartiallyMet, AllMet.
  - **CMP-204 OtpInput** - Empty, PartiallyFilled, Complete, Error, Disabled; one control to assistive tech.
  - **CMP-205 QrCode** - Default, LargeSize; untinted quiet zone in both themes.
  - **CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList** - Default plus the consumed/remaining representation.
  - **CMP-207 BuildFooter** - Default plus the long-node-name overflow case.
  - **CMP-097 OnboardingChecklist** - Default, PartiallyComplete, plus role-disabled items with a visible reason.
  - **CMP-098 SessionTimeoutWarning** - Default plus the extend-in-progress state.
- For each: a **props/API table** matching the catalogue entry exactly, a written a11y contract, the token list (no raw values anywhere), the Storybook story list the FE component must ship, and the states that are *forbidden* (e.g. CMP-205 with a themed quiet zone).
- Reconciliation pass: every divergence discovered between the catalogue's existing entries and what E09-D03..D06 actually needed is either folded into the component or raised as a catalogue amendment PR - no silent drift.
- A **composition map** showing which screen uses which component in which variant, so E09-D11 design QA and the FE handoff have a checklist rather than an inspection.
- Any component E09-D03..D06 needed that has no CMP-* id at all is proposed with a new id in the reserved band gap, with a written justification against `15-component-catalogue.md` section 8's consolidation reasoning.

## Out of scope
- Building the React components (FE story in E09 engineering scope).
- Tokens themselves - owned by E05; this ticket consumes them and reports any gap.
- Chart-engine primitives (CMP-180..199) and trading components.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every auth screen composes only published components
  Given the composition map and the E09-D03..D06 artefacts
  When each frame is inspected
  Then every element resolves to a published library component instance
  And any remaining local component is listed with a dated plan to publish or remove it

Scenario: A component contract cannot be violated silently
  Given CMP-205 QrCode
  When a consumer applies a themed surface to the quiet zone
  Then the published component does not permit it and the forbidden state is documented

Scenario: OTP entry is one control everywhere it appears
  Given CMP-204 is used by SCR-002, SCR-003 and SCR-006
  Then all three consume the same published variant set
  And the accessible name is supplied by the consumer while the internal cell structure is never exposed as six inputs

Scenario: Catalogue and library agree
  Given 15-component-catalogue.md entries CMP-097, CMP-098, CMP-200..207
  When compared against the published components
  Then props, a11y contract, tokens and Storybook lists match exactly
  And any difference has been merged as a catalogue amendment PR before sign-off

Scenario: A new component is justified, not assumed
  Given a surface that needs a component with no existing CMP id
  Then a new id in the reserved gap is proposed with a written justification
  And the alternative of extending an existing component is explicitly considered and rejected in writing
```

## Technical notes / design
The library structure and naming follow `16-design-system-brief.md` section 10; the token-to-code path is Style Dictionary per section 11, so every value in these components must be a token reference or the handoff will produce hard-coded CSS.

CMP-201's "never suppresses paste" and CMP-204's "supports paste of the whole code" are contracts, not preferences - password managers and OTP autofill are security controls. They are recorded as forbidden-state documentation so a later well-meaning change cannot remove them.

CMP-202 and CMP-203 are deliberately separate components even though they always appear together, because the checklist is normative and the meter is advisory; merging them would blur that distinction, and the catalogue's section 8 reasoning applies.

## Test plan
Per component: axe audit of the Storybook-equivalent prototype states, contrast measurement in both themes, keyboard interaction pass (especially CMP-204 arrow/backspace/paste and CMP-201 reveal toggle), and a CVD simulation. A cross-screen consistency pass confirms no two screens use a different variant for the same purpose. Results attached and reused as the E09-D11 baseline.

## Security notes
CMP-205 and CMP-206 handle secret material. Their published documentation states: the QR's accessible name must never contain the secret; the recovery-code list must not be screenshot-friendly by default in any analytics or session-replay integration; neither component may log its props. CMP-201 documents that suppressing paste is forbidden. These statements live with the component so a consumer cannot reintroduce the risk.

## Accessibility notes
Each component ships its a11y contract verbatim from `15-component-catalogue.md`: CMP-200's `<main>` + `<h1>` + focused `role="alert"`; CMP-201's real `<button aria-pressed>` reveal and polite caps-lock region; CMP-202's text-plus-bar with 500 ms debounce; CMP-203's met/not-met accessible names in a polite list; CMP-204's single labelled control with `inputmode="numeric"` and `autocomplete="one-time-code"`; CMP-205's `role="img"` plus mandatory text secret; CMP-098's `role="alertdialog"` at a fixed threshold satisfying WCAG 2.2.1; CMP-097's `aria-checked` read-only list semantics with visible reasons for role-disabled items.

## Performance notes
Components must be usable on a code-split pre-auth route with no chart bundle: no component in this band may depend on the engine, a heavy animation library, or a webfont beyond the core set. CMP-205's QR generation budget (<=100 ms) is recorded on the component so the FE library choice is bounded.

## Observability
None of these components emits telemetry itself; the composition map records which screen-level event each component participates in, so instrumentation stays at the screen level and a component cannot start reporting on its own.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten components published in the library with every listed variant in both themes.
- [ ] Props/API tables, a11y contracts, token lists, Storybook lists and forbidden states documented per component.
- [ ] Composition map published and linked from E09-D11 and the handoff pack.
- [ ] All divergences reconciled; catalogue amendment PRs merged.
- [ ] Axe + contrast + keyboard + CVD audits attached per component.
- [ ] Design-system team review recorded in addition to CDO sign-off.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done).

## Dependencies
- **E09-D03..D06** - these define the real variant requirements; publishing before them would guess.
- **E05** design-system v0 tokens and the library structure.

## Branch
`design/e09-auth-component-band`

## References
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` band 8 (CMP-200..207), CMP-097, CMP-098, section 8
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` sections 10, 11, 12, 13
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-ONB-001..008 component columns
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 11

title: Motion & transition spec for auth, lock and step-up surfaces
body:
## Context
Motion in the auth band has an unusual constraint: three of its surfaces appear **over a running WebGL workspace**. A modal that fades in with a backdrop blur over a 60 fps footprint chart is not a cosmetic choice - it is a per-frame compositing cost on the most performance-sensitive surface in the product, and `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets do not stop applying because a dialog opened.

The second constraint is comprehension. SCR-005's whole promise is that the workspace is *preserved*, not destroyed; the transition into the lock is what communicates that. A hard cut reads as a page navigation and undermines the promise the copy makes. Conversely SCR-006's failure states must feel immediate - an animated shake or a slow error reveal on a step-up code entry wastes a trader's seconds during a key rotation.

`16-design-system-brief.md` sections 2.6 and 7 define the motion token vocabulary; this ticket applies it to the auth band and measures the result rather than asserting it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A motion specification covering every transition in the band, each expressed in tokens (duration, easing, property) rather than raw values:
  - Route transitions SCR-001 → SCR-002 → SCR-003/SCR-010, including the backward transition on an expired challenge.
  - SCR-003 wizard step transitions (<=200 ms budget) and the focus handoff to the next step's first control.
  - CMP-098 warning appearance and its extend-dismissal.
  - SCR-005 lock-in and unlock-out over a live workspace, including the scrim's arrival and the preservation cue.
  - SCR-006 step-up open/close, the grace-TTL indicator's update cadence, and the failure feedback.
  - Error-region appearance on SCR-001/002/004 (must not delay the announcement).
  - Loading/busy affordances: button spinner, field lock, and the verifying state.
- A **reduced-motion variant** for every one of the above, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 7: what becomes instant, what remains (opacity-only), and what is removed entirely.
- A **forbidden-techniques list** with reasons: backdrop blur or filter over the chart canvas, animating layout properties, any transition that delays focus placement, any animation on the OTP auto-submit path, looping/attention-seeking motion on an error.
- A measured **cost budget**: each transition profiled in a prototype over a representative running chart, with the recorded frame cost attached to the ticket. Any transition that drops a frame at 1440p is redesigned, not shipped with a note.
- Contribution of any new motion token the band needs back into `16-design-system-brief.md` section 2.6 rather than inventing a local value.

## Out of scope
- Chart-engine animation (pan/zoom easing) - E11/E12.
- Motion for admin or trading surfaces beyond the step-up chassis they reuse.
- Sound or haptics - not used in this product.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No transition costs the workspace a frame
  Given the SCR-005 lock-in transition profiled over a running chart at 2560x1440
  When the frame cost is measured
  Then no frame exceeds the budget in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md
  And the measurement is attached to the ticket rather than asserted

Scenario: Reduced motion is complete, not partial
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  When every transition in the spec is walked
  Then each has a defined reduced variant and none retains a movement or scale animation
  And no information is conveyed only by the motion that was removed

Scenario: Motion never delays a security interaction
  Given the step-up modal opens
  Then focus reaches the code field at or before the end of the opening transition
  And the failure feedback is visible within one frame of the server response

Scenario: A forbidden technique is caught
  Given a proposed transition uses a backdrop filter over the chart canvas
  Then the spec rejects it by name and states the measured reason

Scenario: Preservation is communicated
  Given the idle lock engages over a workspace with an unsent order ticket
  Then the transition visually preserves the underlying layout rather than replacing it
  And a user shown the transition without copy can still tell the workspace was not discarded
```

## Technical notes / design
All transitions are specified as compositor-friendly properties only (opacity and transform); animating width, height, top or box-shadow is on the forbidden list because it forces layout over a canvas-heavy page.

The measurement prototype runs the real E05 primitives over a stand-in animated canvas at the target resolutions; it does not need the real engine, but it must not use a static screenshot as the backdrop, which would hide exactly the cost being measured.

Where a transition and an accessibility requirement conflict - for example an entrance animation on a `role="alert"` region delaying its announcement - the accessibility requirement wins and the motion is removed rather than shortened.

## Test plan
Profiled prototype runs at 1280x800 and 2560x1440 with the backdrop animating, recording frame cost per transition; a reduced-motion pass confirming every variant; a screen-reader pass confirming that no announcement is delayed by an entrance transition; a review with the chart-engine lead confirming the scrim approach is compatible with how the WebGL surfaces composite.

## Security notes
Motion must not become a covert channel or a confusion vector: the step-up modal may not animate in a way that allows a click intended for the underlying page to land on Confirm (no transition during which the dialog is interactive but not yet fully visible), and the modal must be fully opaque to input from the moment it can receive it.

## Accessibility notes
`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 7 is binding: every animation has a reduced-motion variant; nothing flashes more than three times per second; no animation is required to understand a state; focus movement is never animated in a way that a screen reader or a magnifier user cannot follow. The CMP-098 warning's appearance must not be so subtle that it is missed, which is an explicit review point rather than a default.

## Performance notes
This is the ticket's centre of gravity. Budgets: SCR-005 mount <=100 ms including its transition; SCR-003 step transitions <=200 ms; no transition may cause a dropped frame on the underlying workspace at 2560x1440; the total added JS/CSS animation weight on the pre-auth route must not break SCR-001's <=1 s cold first paint.

## Observability
No runtime telemetry is added by motion. The spec records which transitions are considered performance-sensitive so that, if the FE performance budget check (E46) later flags the auth routes, there is a documented list to inspect first.

title: Design the RBAC permission-denied pattern (owner/manager/viewer)
body:
## Context
E09 introduces three roles - Owner, Manager, Viewer - enforced server-side with deny-by-default on every route. RBAC has no screen of its own, which is exactly why it needs a design ticket: it is a **cross-cutting visual grammar** that every subsequent epic will inherit, and if it is not fixed now, forty screens will each invent their own way of saying no.

`14-screens-catalogue.md` section 0 already fixes the policy and it is unusually specific: *controls the user may not use are rendered disabled with a reason tooltip, not hidden - except whole admin areas, which are hidden from navigation and hard-404 for non-owners; the server returns 403 plus an audit entry regardless of UI state*. That single sentence contains three different treatments (disabled-with-reason, hidden-and-404, server-rejected-anyway) and a rule about which applies when. Turning it into a pattern designers and engineers can apply without re-deciding is this ticket's job.

The decision is not purely aesthetic. Showing a disabled control teaches a manager what the product can do and why they cannot do it, which is good for onboarding (SCR-017 explicitly promises a "what you cannot do" section drawn honestly) but leaks the shape of the owner's capabilities. Hiding everything is safer but produces a product that feels broken. The Owner and the Security engineer both have a stake in where that line falls.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A written and drawn **RBAC presentation pattern** with a decision rule: for any control, which of the four treatments applies -
  1. **Enabled** (permitted);
  2. **Disabled with a visible reason** (permitted for the role in principle but blocked by state, or not permitted but useful to show);
  3. **Hidden** (whole areas the role has no business knowing about - the `/admin/*` band);
  4. **Server-denied** (the 403 landing state when UI and server disagree, e.g. a grant revoked mid-session).
- Hi-fi frames, dark + light, for each treatment, drawn on real host surfaces rather than in the abstract: a disabled order-submit for a Viewer, a disabled admin action for a Manager, the navigation as a Manager sees it (admin absent), the hard-404 a Manager gets by typing `/admin`, and the 403 state when a permission disappears while the user is looking at the screen.
- The **reason vocabulary**: a fixed, small set of plain-English reason strings ("Viewers can't place orders", "Only the owner can change this", "Your role doesn't include this account") with a rule that every disabled control must supply one - no reasonless disabled controls anywhere in the product.
- The **role-change-mid-session** design: what a user sees when their role or account grants change while they are signed in, including whether the UI degrades in place or forces a reload.
- A short research component: 2 sessions with prospective Managers/Viewers confirming that the disabled-with-reason treatment reads as "not for you" rather than "broken", and that the hidden admin area does not read as a missing feature.
- Contribution of the pattern into `15-component-catalogue.md` (the `disabledReason` propagation contract already referenced by CMP-085-class wrappers) and into `14-screens-catalogue.md` section 0 as normative text every later screen cites.

## Out of scope
- The RBAC policy itself (roles, permissions, the `roles` / `role_permissions` tables) - engineering scope in E09.
- Admin screens' own designs (admin epic) beyond how they are hidden from non-owners.
- Per-account scoping UI in the account switcher (E27) - this ticket supplies the grammar it will use.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every treatment has a decision rule, not a preference
  Given the pattern document
  When a designer must decide how to present a control the current role cannot use
  Then the document yields exactly one treatment for that case without further interpretation
  And the admin-area exception is stated as the one case where hiding is mandatory

Scenario: No disabled control is silent
  Given any frame in this ticket showing a disabled control
  Then a reason is available as text to both sighted and screen-reader users
  And the reason is not conveyed by a hover-only tooltip

Scenario: A revoked permission is handled mid-session
  Given a Manager loses access to an account while a position panel is open
  Then a frame shows what they see, what happens to any in-flight action, and how they learn why
  And the design states that the server denies regardless of what the UI showed

Scenario: A hidden area is genuinely hidden
  Given a Manager navigates directly to /admin
  Then the frame shows a hard 404 that does not confirm the route exists
  And no navigation element, search result or empty state elsewhere reveals the admin area's existence

Scenario: The treatment reads correctly to real users
  Given the two research sessions
  Then the report records whether participants interpreted disabled-with-reason as a permission boundary rather than a defect
  And any misinterpretation drives a change to the treatment or the vocabulary

Scenario: The pattern survives a role it was not designed for
  Given a future role between Manager and Owner is hypothesised
  When the decision rule is applied
  Then it yields a treatment without requiring the pattern to be rewritten
```

## Technical notes / design
The disabled-with-reason treatment relies on `disabledReason` being propagated to the wrapped atom's native prop rather than an overlay - `15-component-catalogue.md` already binds this for CMP-001-class atoms, and the pattern must reuse it so that reasons are exposed through real semantics rather than a non-semantic layer that assistive tech cannot reach.

The hard-404 for `/admin/*` is a router behaviour, not a design flourish; the frame specifies that the 404 is indistinguishable from a genuinely nonexistent route, which is a deliberate anti-enumeration choice that the Security engineer signs off.

The 403 landing state must distinguish "you never had this" from "this was taken away just now", because the user actions differ (ask the owner vs re-sync), and the design names which server signal drives which message.

## Test plan
A pattern-application dry run: three controls from other epics (an order submit, a rule-arming action, a recorder setting) are presented to two designers who independently apply the decision rule and must reach the same treatment. Disagreement means the rule is underspecified and is refined before sign-off. Plus contrast/CVD audits of the disabled treatment (disabled text is the most commonly failed contrast case in any design system) and a screen-reader pass confirming reasons are announced.

## Security notes
This pattern is a deliberate, bounded information disclosure and is reviewed as such in the E09 STRIDE model. Rules: disabled controls may name the capability but never the data behind it (a Viewer may see that order entry exists, never an account's balance); the admin area is hidden and hard-404'd with no timing or message difference from a nonexistent route; reason strings are a fixed vocabulary so a future screen cannot leak specifics by writing its own; the UI treatment is never a security control - the server denies with 403 and an audit entry regardless, which the pattern states in bold so no engineer treats a disabled button as enforcement.

## Accessibility notes
Disabled controls must still be discoverable and their reasons readable: reasons are rendered as text associated with the control (`aria-describedby`), never hover-only tooltips; per `05-accessibility-standard.md` the disabled state is signalled by more than reduced opacity, and the disabled text still meets the contrast floor for meaningful non-interactive text; the role-scoped checklist items in CMP-097 use `aria-disabled` with a visible reason rather than removal.

## Performance notes
The pattern must not require a per-control permission fetch: permissions arrive once with the session (`GET /api/v1/auth/session`) and are evaluated client-side for presentation only. The design states this so no screen introduces a permission round-trip per rendered control.

## Observability
The 403 landing state and the mid-session revocation both correspond to audited server events; the frames annotate that a UI-side denial emits nothing (there is nothing to audit) while every server denial is audited with actor, role, action and target per `21-database-schema.md` `audit_log`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Pattern document published with the four treatments and a deterministic decision rule.
- [ ] Frames drawn for every treatment on real host surfaces, both themes.
- [ ] Reason vocabulary fixed and published.
- [ ] Two research sessions run; findings recorded and acted on.
- [ ] Two-designer dry run reached the same treatment for all three test controls.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off on the disclosure boundary and the admin hard-404.
- [ ] Contrast/CVD and screen-reader audits attached.
- [ ] Normative text merged into `14-screens-catalogue.md` section 0 and `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done).

## Dependencies
- **E09-D02** wireframes (the role variants in the states matrix).
- **E05** design-system v0 (disabled-state tokens, `disabledReason` propagation).

## Branch
`design/e09-rbac-denied-pattern`

## References

- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-085-class `disabledReason` contract, CMP-097

title: Accessibility design review & screen-reader script for the auth band
body:
## Context
The auth band is the one part of CandleViewer where an accessibility failure is not a degraded experience but a total lockout: a user who cannot complete TOTP entry cannot use the product at all, and there is no alternative route in. `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 11.7 makes an accessibility role sign-off a **named mandatory gate** on every design ticket, and `16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.3.3 restates it as a precondition for Status Done.

This ticket is that gate, executed once across the whole band rather than five disconnected checks, because the band's hardest a11y problems are *sequence* problems that no single-screen review catches: focus continuity from SCR-001 to SCR-002 to SCR-003; whether an error announced on one screen is re-announced after a route change; whether the idle lock's focus trap returns focus to the right control when it resolves over a workspace the user was in the middle of.

It also produces the artefact QA will actually run: a screen-reader test script specific to these flows, so the manual pass required by `03-testing-strategy.md` and the Epic DoD is a repeatable procedure rather than an improvised session.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **full accessibility design review** of E09-D03..D06 and E09-D09 against `05-accessibility-standard.md`, producing a completed acceptance-criteria template (section 10) per screen, with each finding classified blocker / major / minor and assigned back to the owning design ticket.
- Review dimensions, each checked explicitly rather than assumed: keyboard operability and visible focus on every path (section 3); colour-independence of every state including disabled and error (section 4); contrast in the dark theme for text, focus rings and disabled text (section 5); reduced motion (section 7, cross-checked with E09-D08); timing (WCAG 2.2.1 - the CMP-098 warning before the idle lock); no keyboard trap except the deliberate, resolvable modal traps; target sizes; and the OTP field's single-control exposure.
- A **focus-continuity map** across the whole band: for every transition (route change, wizard step, modal open, modal close, error appearance, success), where focus is before and after, and what is announced.
- A **screen-reader test script** covering NVDA + Chrome and VoiceOver + Safari per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8, with expected announcements written out verbatim for: sign-in failure, rate-limited state, OTP entry and auto-submit, enrolment secret as text, recovery-code list, password requirement changes, idle-lock warning and lock, step-up with its named action, and an RBAC-disabled control's reason. Handed to QA as the basis for the manual pass.
- A list of **CI-checkable assertions** (axe rules, focus assertions) derived from the review, handed to the QA/SDET tickets so the automated gate (`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9) covers what matters here rather than generic rules only.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the findings - they return to E09-D03..D06/D09 as change requests under `16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.5.
- Implementation-level a11y testing of built code (QA tickets in E09 engineering scope).
- Non-auth screens.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every screen has a completed template
  Given SCR-001..006 and the RBAC pattern
  When the review closes
  Then each has a completed 05-accessibility-standard.md section 10 acceptance-criteria template attached
  And no template contains an unexplained N/A

Scenario: A blocker stops sign-off
  Given a finding classified as a blocker
  Then the owning design ticket cannot reach Status Done until it is resolved and re-reviewed
  And the dependency is recorded on that ticket rather than tracked informally

Scenario: Focus continuity has no gaps
  Given the focus-continuity map
  When every transition in the band is walked
  Then each has a defined focus destination and a defined announcement
  And no transition leaves focus on the document body

Scenario: The timing requirement is met, not waived
  Given the idle lock
  Then a warning with an extend action precedes it at a defined threshold
  And the review records this as satisfying WCAG 2.2.1 rather than accepting an exception

Scenario: The script is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given the screen-reader test script
  When a QA engineer who was not involved in the design runs it
  Then every step has an expected announcement they can pass or fail without interpretation

Scenario: A lockout risk is identified
  Given any path where a user with a disability could be unable to complete authentication
  Then it is recorded as a blocker regardless of how rare it is judged to be
```

## Technical notes / design
The review runs against the Figma prototypes plus their annotation layers, not against built code - which is the point of design-ahead: a focus-order defect costs minutes here and days after implementation.

The OTP field receives disproportionate attention because it is the single most likely lockout point: it must be one labelled control, it must accept paste and `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, its auto-submit must not fire twice, and its error must be announced without stealing focus from the field the user is correcting.

Where the standard and a design decision conflict, the standard wins and the design changes; any proposed exception requires the explicit "essential exception" logging that `16-design-system-brief.md` section 12 demands, signed by both the CDO and the accessibility lead.

## Test plan
The review is itself the test. Method: two passes - a structured checklist pass against the standard, and an unstructured exploratory pass by a reviewer who has not seen the designs, whose confusions are recorded as findings. Automated contrast measurement of every text/background and focus-ring pair in both themes. CVD simulation (protan, deutan, tritan) of every state. The resulting script is dry-run once end-to-end before being handed to QA.

## Security notes
The accessible alternatives must not weaken the security properties: the QR's text secret is an equivalent path, not a downgrade, and must be protected identically; announcements must never read out a password, a TOTP code or a recovery code; the screen-reader script itself uses fixture credentials only and is safe to store in the repo.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility work; the target is WCAG 2.2 AA with no outstanding blockers across the band. The deliverables become the baseline for the Epic-level DoD requirement ("axe-core CI green plus at least one manual screen-reader pass") and for E09-D11's design QA.

## Performance notes
The review confirms that no accessibility affordance introduces a performance cost that violates the band's budgets - specifically that live regions are debounced (CMP-202/CMP-203 at 500 ms) rather than announcing per keystroke, and that the countdown regions on SCR-001's rate-limit and SCR-006's grace update at a cadence that neither floods a screen reader nor forces a re-render per second.

## Observability
The CI-checkable assertion list is handed to the QA/SDET tickets so that axe-core failures on these routes are attributable to a named requirement rather than a generic rule id.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Completed acceptance-criteria template attached per screen, no unexplained N/A.
- [ ] Focus-continuity map published covering every transition in the band.
- [ ] Screen-reader test script published (NVDA+Chrome, VoiceOver+Safari) with verbatim expected announcements, dry-run once, handed to QA.
- [ ] CI-checkable assertion list handed to the QA/SDET tickets.
- [ ] All blockers resolved and re-reviewed; majors either resolved or logged as essential exceptions with CDO + accessibility-lead signature.
- [ ] Contrast and CVD measurement results attached for both themes.
- [ ] Accessibility lead sign-off and CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done).

title: Design QA of the built auth, session and RBAC surfaces
body:
## Context
Design QA is the closing half of the design-ahead loop: design runs two sprints ahead, engineering builds, and then someone verifies that what shipped is what was signed off. Without it, the catalogue documents slowly become fiction and `16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.5's arbitration rule ("the catalogue documents are the arbitration source when Figma and shipped code disagree") has nothing to arbitrate against.

The auth band is the first band to complete this loop, so this ticket also establishes the *procedure* every later epic's design QA will copy: what is checked, how a defect is classified, who decides whether a divergence is a bug or an accepted change, and what happens to the catalogue when the answer is "accepted change".

It sits in Sprint 04 because that is when E09's frontend stories land; it is deliberately not a sprint-01-style design ticket, and its sprint placement is driven by the build, not by the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **design QA pass** per `16-design-system-brief.md` section 12 against the implemented SCR-001, SCR-002, SCR-003, SCR-004, SCR-005, SCR-006, the RBAC pattern's manifestations, and the CMP-097/098/200-207 components as built, covering:
  - Token fidelity: every colour, space, radius, type and elevation value resolves to a token, with no hard-coded values (checked in the running app via computed styles, not by eye).
  - State completeness: every state in the E09-D02 states matrix is reachable in the built app and matches its frame.
  - Copy fidelity: every string matches the signed-off copy decks character for character, including the error messages that carry security meaning.
  - Component fidelity: every surface uses the published component and variant recorded in E09-D07's composition map, with no local forks.
  - Theme and density: dark and light, both resolutions, 125% zoom.
  - Interaction fidelity: tab order, focus destinations, auto-submit, paste behaviour, Escape semantics, focus return - checked against E09-D10's focus-continuity map.
  - Motion fidelity: transitions match E09-D08's spec, reduced-motion variants present, no forbidden technique in use.
- A **defect log** with each finding classified: *implementation defect* (code must change), *accepted divergence* (design changes, catalogue updated under section 13.5 change control), or *specification gap* (neither was defined - design ticket reopened). Every entry names an owner and a ticket.
- Updates to `14-screens-catalogue.md` and `15-component-catalogue.md` for every accepted divergence, so the documents describe shipped behaviour rather than the original proposal - a requirement the Epic DoD states explicitly.
- A short **written procedure** generalising this pass into a reusable design-QA checklist for later epics.

## Out of scope
- Functional QA (correctness of auth, rate limiting, token rotation) - engineering QA tickets.
- Penetration testing (E43) and load testing.
- Fixing the defects - they are raised as tickets against the implementing stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every signed-off state is verified in the running app
  Given the E09-D02 states matrix
  When design QA runs against the built application
  Then every state has been reached and compared, or is recorded as unreachable with the reason
  And an unreachable state is a defect unless the design explicitly removed it

Scenario: A hard-coded value is caught
  Given a shipped surface whose computed style does not resolve to a token
  Then it is logged as an implementation defect with the element, the value and the expected token

Scenario: Security-bearing copy is exact
  Given the sign-in failure, rate-limited and account-disabled messages
  When compared to the signed-off copy deck
  Then they match exactly
  And any deviation is treated as a blocker, not a cosmetic defect, because the wording carries the no-enumeration property

Scenario: A divergence is decided, not tolerated
  Given a difference between the built surface and the signed-off design
  Then it is classified as defect, accepted divergence or specification gap before the pass closes
  And no difference is left unclassified

Scenario: An accepted divergence updates the documents
  Given a divergence is accepted
  Then 14-screens-catalogue.md and/or 15-component-catalogue.md are updated in the same sprint
  And the change is recorded against the originating design ticket under section 13.5 change control

Scenario: A component fork is detected
  Given the composition map from E09-D07
  When the built surfaces are inspected
  Then any surface using a local component instead of the published one is logged as a defect
```

## Technical notes / design
The pass runs against a deployed build on the target browsers, not against Storybook alone - several of the band's requirements (focus return over a live workspace, the lock's behaviour with subscriptions paused, the RBAC 403 landing) only exist in the integrated app.

Token fidelity is checked mechanically where possible: computed styles are compared against the Style Dictionary output (`16-design-system-brief.md` section 11) rather than judged visually, which catches the near-miss values a human eye approves.

The defect log lives with the ticket and its entries are real tickets, not a spreadsheet the sprint forgets.

## Test plan
Structured pass in this order: (1) mechanical token diff; (2) state matrix walk in dark, then light, then 125% zoom; (3) copy diff against the decks; (4) composition-map component audit; (5) focus-continuity walk from E09-D10's map; (6) motion pass including reduced motion; (7) an axe run on each route to confirm the CI gate is actually covering these surfaces. Each step's result is recorded pass/fail with evidence.

## Security notes
The copy diff is a security check, not a proofreading exercise: the no-enumeration property of SCR-001's error messages lives entirely in their wording and timing, so a reworded message is a security regression. The pass also verifies that the built app does not display a TOTP secret or recovery code anywhere outside SCR-003, that the admin area is genuinely absent from a Manager's navigation and hard-404s, and that no auth screen logs a credential to the console. Findings in this class are escalated to the Security engineer immediately rather than queued in the log.

## Accessibility notes
Design QA re-runs the E09-D10 screen-reader script against the built app as its accessibility component, and confirms the axe-core CI gate is green on every auth route. Any regression against the focus-continuity map is a blocker. This pass is one of the two evidences (automated + manual) the Epic DoD requires for a11y.

## Performance notes
The pass records measured values against the band's budgets on the real build: SCR-001 cold first paint <=1 s, SCR-002 verify round-trip <=400 ms p95, SCR-003 QR render <=100 ms, SCR-005 mount <=100 ms, step-up token issue <=400 ms p95, and no dropped frame on the workspace when the lock engages. A missed budget is a defect with an owner, not an observation.

## Observability
Verifies that the audit/analytics events annotated on the designs are actually emitted with the expected keys (`auth.login.*`, `auth.mfa.*`, `auth.password.changed`, `auth.session.*`, `auth.stepup.*`, `onboarding.*`) and that none carries a credential - a check that is cheap here and expensive after release.

- [ ] All seven pass steps executed with recorded evidence.
- [ ] Defect log complete, every entry classified and ticketed with an owner.
- [ ] Catalogue documents updated for every accepted divergence.
- [ ] Security-class findings escalated and resolved or accepted with Security-engineer sign-off.
- [ ] E09-D10 screen-reader script re-run against the build; axe-core green on every auth route.
- [ ] Performance budgets measured and recorded.
- [ ] Reusable design-QA procedure written for later epics.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done).

`design/e09-auth-design-qa`

title: Engineering handoff pack for the auth, session and RBAC band
body:
## Context
`16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.3.7 defines the literal unblocking action of the design-ahead rule: a design ticket is Done only when its downstream engineering tickets are updated with a link to the final artefact and moved Backlog → Ready. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 enforces the other side - a Story with UI surface cannot enter Ready without a linked, Done design artefact that has been Done for ≥2 sprints.

That handshake needs a single artefact to point at. Five separate Figma files, a research report, a motion spec, a pattern document and a component band are not a handoff; they are a scavenger hunt, and the predictable result is a frontend engineer reconstructing a decision from a picture. This ticket assembles the pack that makes the E09 frontend stories genuinely Ready in Sprint 04, two sprints after the designs are signed off.

It is also where design commits to the **contract** side of the handoff: every data field a screen renders is traced to an operation in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, so no screen ships assuming data the backend does not return - the specific failure `16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.3.5 exists to prevent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A single handoff document at `docs/design/handoff/e09-auth.md` assembling and linking:
  - Final Figma artefacts per screen with the exact frame links, plus the E09-D02 states matrix and E09-D07 composition map.
  - Redlines and token references, exported from the library rather than hand-written.
  - The complete copy deck for the band in one table (screen, state, string, notes), flagging the strings whose exact wording is security-bearing.
  - The focus-continuity map (E09-D10) and the per-screen accessibility acceptance criteria.
  - The motion spec and reduced-motion variants (E09-D08) with the forbidden-techniques list.
  - The RBAC presentation pattern and reason vocabulary (E09-D09).
  - Asset exports: icons used, the QR sizing spec, and the `.txt` recovery-code file format.
- A **data-contract table**: every field rendered on SCR-001..006, SCR-017 and SCR-019 mapped to the operation that supplies it (`POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/mfa/verify`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `POST /auth/mfa/recovery`, `DELETE /auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`, `PUT /auth/password`, `POST /auth/step-up`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `GET /auth/session`, `GET /auth/sessions`, `POST /auth/logout`, `GET /api/v1/system/build`, `GET /api/v1/onboarding/checklist`, `GET /api/v1/me/sessions`), with any field that has no source raised as an OpenAPI change request **before** the story starts, never during it.
- An **error-mapping table**: every server error condition (invalid credentials, disabled account, rate limited, invalid/replayed TOTP, expired challenge, invalid recovery code, exhausted recovery codes, reused/breached password, step-up denied, 403 from RBAC) mapped to the exact UI state and string.
- A **10-minute walkthrough session** with the frontend engineers who will build the band, recorded, with questions and answers appended to the document - the point of contact where ambiguity surfaces cheaply.
- Update of each downstream E09 frontend story: Figma link attached, catalogue entry linked, moved Backlog → Ready.

## Out of scope
- Writing the frontend code or its tests.
- Backend contract changes themselves - this ticket raises them, E09 engineering makes them.
- Screens outside the band.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every rendered field has a source
  Given the data-contract table
  When each field on SCR-001..006, SCR-017 and SCR-019 is checked
  Then it names the operation in 22-api-openapi.yaml that supplies it
  And any field with no source has an open OpenAPI change request linked before the story is moved to Ready

Scenario: Every server error has exactly one UI state
  Given the error-mapping table
  When each listed server condition is looked up
  Then it maps to one state and one string
  And no condition maps to a generic fallback without that being an explicit, justified decision

Scenario: The pack is sufficient without its author
  Given a frontend engineer who did not attend any design review
  When they read docs/design/handoff/e09-auth.md
  Then they can identify every screen, state, component, variant, string, focus behaviour and data source without asking a designer
  And any question they do ask is appended to the document as a permanent answer

Scenario: The design-ahead gate is satisfied honestly
  Given an E09 frontend story about to move to Ready in Sprint 04
  Then its linked design artefact is Status Done and has been Done for at least two sprints
  And if it has not, an explicit Architect or CDO waiver with a reason is recorded rather than the rule being quietly ignored

Scenario: A late design change is controlled
  Given a signed-off design changes after the pack is published
  Then the change goes through section 13.5 change control, the pack is re-issued, and any in-progress engineering work is flagged for re-sync

Scenario: Security-bearing strings are marked
  Given the copy deck in the pack
  Then every string whose exact wording carries a security property is flagged as such
  And the flag states what breaks if it is reworded
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack is a markdown document in the repo with links out to Figma, not a Figma page - it must survive a Figma outage, be reviewable in a PR, and be diffable when it changes. Tokens are referenced by name and resolved through the Style Dictionary pipeline (`16-design-system-brief.md` section 11) so the engineer never copies a hex value.

The data-contract table is the highest-value part and is built by reading `22-api-openapi.yaml` directly rather than from memory of what was discussed; discrepancies found during this exercise are the whole reason the exercise exists and are expected, not a sign of failure.

The walkthrough is deliberately short and deliberately recorded: the recording plus the appended Q&A is what a second engineer joining in Sprint 04 reads instead of re-running the meeting.

## Test plan
The "sufficient without its author" scenario is tested literally: an engineer not involved in the design reads the pack cold and attempts to describe one full flow (invite → password → enrolment → first sign-in) including every state and data source. Gaps found become pack revisions before sign-off.

## Security notes
The pack flags which strings and behaviours carry security properties so a later change cannot silently remove them: SCR-001's identical failure messaging (no enumeration), the admin hard-404's indistinguishability, the once-only display of recovery codes, the unconditional step-up on Live enablement and kill-switch disable, and the rule that a disabled control is never enforcement. The pack contains no real secrets, tokens or credentials - fixtures only - and is reviewed by the Security engineer before publication.

## Accessibility notes
The accessibility acceptance criteria travel *inside* the pack rather than as a separate document, so an engineer implementing a screen has the per-screen criteria, the focus-continuity map and the screen-reader expectations in the same place as the redlines. The pack states that these criteria are part of the story's Definition of Done, not advisory notes.

## Performance notes
The pack restates the band's budgets next to the screens they constrain (SCR-001 <=1 s cold first paint with no chart bundle, SCR-002 <=400 ms p95 verify, SCR-003 <=100 ms QR render, SCR-005 <=100 ms mount, step-up <=400 ms p95) and names the design decisions that exist to protect them, so an engineer knows which choices are not free to change.

## Observability
The pack lists the audit and analytics events each screen must emit with their exact keys and payload shape, sourced from the design annotations and reconciled against `21-database-schema.md` `audit_log`, so instrumentation is implemented from a specification rather than added retrospectively.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/design/handoff/e09-auth.md` merged, assembling all artefacts with working links.
- [ ] Data-contract table complete; every unsourced field has a linked OpenAPI change request.
- [ ] Error-mapping table complete for every listed server condition.
- [ ] Copy deck included with security-bearing strings flagged and Security-engineer reviewed.
- [ ] Walkthrough held and recorded; Q&A appended.
- [ ] Cold-read test passed by an uninvolved engineer; gaps fixed.
- [ ] Every downstream E09 frontend story updated with the Figma and catalogue links and moved Backlog → Ready.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done).

## Dependencies
- **E09-D03, E09-D04, E09-D05, E09-D06** - the signed-off screen artefacts.
- **E09-D07** - the published component band and composition map.
- **E09-D08, E09-D09, E09-D10** contribute sections; the pack is re-issued if they land after publication.

`design/e09-auth-handoff-pack`

- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` sections 3.1, 3.2

body:
## Context
E09 ships the controls that every later epic assumes: password sign-in, mandatory TOTP, opaque server-side sessions, step-up re-authentication, deny-by-default RBAC and a tamper-evident audit log. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 and §8 make a recorded black-box QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story here, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 requires a written test plan per feature plus a white-box review checklist. Nothing in that plan exists yet: the story tickets each state *what* to build, but there is no single artefact a QA engineer can execute end-to-end against a staging build to say "authentication behaves as specified".

This ticket produces that artefact — a black-box test plan organised by story group, traced to `US-ONB-001..010` and to the security requirements `SR-010..SR-029`, `SR-050`, `SR-051` in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.3–6.4. It is deliberately black-box: written against the screens (`SCR-001..006`, `SCR-017`, `SCR-019`, `SCR-111`, `SCR-112`, `SCR-123`, `SCR-154`) and the public REST/WS contract, with no knowledge of internal helpers, so it stays valid if the implementation is refactored.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e09-auth-rbac-test-plan.md` with five executable sections, one per story group:
  1. **Sign-in & second factor** (US-ONB-001, US-ONB-002) — `SCR-001`, `SCR-002`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/mfa/verify`, `POST /auth/mfa/recovery`.
  2. **Enrolment, recovery codes & forced password change** (US-ONB-003) — `SCR-003`, `SCR-004`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `PUT /auth/password`.
  3. **Session lifetime, idle lock & step-up** (US-ONB-004, US-ONB-005) — `SCR-005`, `SCR-006`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `POST /auth/step-up`, `GET /auth/session`.
  4. **Sessions list, sign-out everywhere & TOTP reset** (US-ONB-009, US-ONB-010) — `SCR-111`, `SCR-112`, `GET /auth/sessions`, `POST /auth/logout`, `DELETE /auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`.
  5. **Invite, onboarding & permission denial** (US-ONB-006, US-ONB-007, US-ONB-008) — `SCR-017`, `SCR-019`, `SCR-123`, `SCR-154`, `GET /invites/{inviteToken}`, `GET|POST /users`, `GET /onboarding/checklist`, `POST /onboarding/complete`.
- Per case: id (`E09-TC-<group><nn>`), preconditions (seeded fixture user + role), steps, expected result, the `US-ONB-*` / `SR-*` id it verifies, the child ticket it covers, and whether it is automated (`E09-Q02`/`E09-Q03`) or manual-only.
- A **test data & fixture appendix**: seeded owner, manager-with-grants, manager-without-grants, viewer, disabled user, invited-but-not-onboarded user; a deterministic TOTP secret so codes can be generated in test; a frozen-clock helper for skew/expiry cases.
- A **traceability table** US-ONB-001..010 × test cases × automation status, mirroring `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` conventions, proving no story is untested.
- **Negative/abuse-adjacent cases owned by QA** (the deeper ones live in `E09-X02`): unknown-user vs wrong-password indistinguishability, TOTP replay, recovery-code reuse, expired MFA challenge, session cookie stripped/edited, role change mid-session.
- Defect-reporting conventions for this epic: severity mapping per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3, with anything that grants access without a completed factor filed as `priority/p0-critical` by definition.

## Out of scope
- Writing the Playwright automation itself (`E09-Q02`) and the RBAC matrix pack (`E09-Q03`).
- Accessibility auditing (`E09-Q04`), performance/chaos (`E09-Q05`), exploratory charters (`E09-Q06`).
- Security-owned artefacts: STRIDE model (`E09-X01`), abuse cases (`E09-X02`), SAST/DAST rules (`E09-X03`).
- Admin user-management beyond `SCR-123` invite (E42) and key-vault flows (E27).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every ONB story is covered by at least one executable case
  Given the test plan is merged at qa/plans/e09-auth-rbac-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against US-ONB-001..010
  Then every story id maps to at least one test case with steps and an expected result
  And every case names the SR-* requirement or child ticket it verifies

Scenario: A plan case is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer with only a staging URL and the seeded fixture set
  When they execute group 3 (session lifetime, idle lock, step-up) without asking the author a question
  Then every step resolves to an unambiguous observable outcome
  And any step that needs a clock or TOTP helper names the exact helper and its invocation

Scenario: Failure case - indistinguishable login errors
  Given a request for an unknown user and a request with a wrong password for a known user
  When both are executed per case E09-TC-A07
  Then the plan requires body, status code and response-time band to be compared
  And a measurable difference is recorded as a P1 defect against SR-014

Scenario: Edge case - role change while a session is live
  Given a manager is signed in and viewing an account-scoped screen
  When the owner revokes the manager's grant per case E09-TC-D05
  Then the plan requires the next request to return 403, the WS connection to receive a revoked frame, and the session id to have rotated
  And no cached client state is accepted as evidence of continued access

Scenario: Plan stays honest when a case cannot be automated
  Given a case that depends on a 7-day absolute session lifetime
  When the plan marks it manual-only
  Then it records the time-travel technique to be used and a follow-up ticket reference to automate it later
```

## Technical notes / design
Write the plan against the contract, not the code: every expectation must be phrased in terms of an HTTP status/body from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, a WS frame from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4/§9.5, a visible screen state from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, or an `audit_log` row. Where `14-screens-catalogue.md` enumerates states (e.g. `SCR-002`: idle · verifying · invalid code · expired challenge · locked after 5 tries), each state gets its own case — state coverage is the structural backbone of the plan.

Fixtures are seeded through the same migrations/seed path used by CI (`E09-T01`), never by hand-editing Postgres, so the plan is runnable on an ephemeral docker-compose environment and on staging identically. The deterministic TOTP secret lives in the test fixture set only and is documented as such; it must never appear in a non-test seed.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan, so its own verification is a dry run: execute the full plan once against the Sprint 03 staging build, record pass/fail per case, and file defects found. A plan that passes 100% on first execution is treated as suspicious — at least the negative cases must have been genuinely attempted, evidenced by screenshots/HAR snippets attached to the run record.

## Security notes
The plan itself contains security-relevant expectations (SR-014 uniform errors, SR-021 TOTP replay, SR-022 recovery-code single use, SR-013 rotation). It must not contain real secrets: only fixture credentials, clearly labelled. Any defect that implies an authentication bypass, privilege escalation or credential disclosure is routed to the Security engineer the same day and is a release blocker for R0.

## Accessibility notes
Each manual case notes whether it must also be executable keyboard-only; the deep a11y audit is `E09-Q04`, but a case whose steps are impossible without a mouse is itself a defect against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 and is filed as such.

## Performance notes
Cases record wall-clock observations where the screen catalogue states a budget (`SCR-002` TOTP verify ≤400 ms p95, `SCR-006` step-up issue ≤400 ms p95, `GET /auth/session` ≤100 ms p95) as smoke-level sanity only; the measured budget run is `E09-Q05`.

## Observability
Every case that should produce an audit action (`auth.login`, `auth.login_failed`, `auth.mfa_enroll`, `auth.mfa_reset`, `auth.password_change`, `roles.grant`, `roles.revoke`) includes "verify the audit row exists with the expected actor, action and target" as an explicit step — audit completeness is a tested behaviour, not an assumption.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `qa/plans/e09-auth-rbac-test-plan.md` merged and linked from every E09 story ticket.
- [ ] Traceability table covers US-ONB-001..010 with no gaps; reviewed by the QA lead and the Security engineer.
- [ ] One full dry-run execution recorded with a pass/fail table and attached evidence; defects filed with `priority/*`.
- [ ] Automation ownership assigned per case (`E09-Q02`, `E09-Q03`, or manual-only with a follow-up ticket).
- [ ] No live Bybit dependency and no wall-clock `sleep` in any case; frozen-clock helper documented.
- [ ] QA lead sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-S01` — the auth/users REST surface must exist to write concrete expectations against.
- `blocked_by: E09-S01` — the login/TOTP screens define the observable states the black-box cases assert.
- Feeds `E09-Q02` (automation), `E09-Q03` (RBAC pack), `E09-Q06` (sign-off), and the R0 release test report (`03-testing-strategy.md` §13).

## Branch
`chore/e09-qa-test-plan`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §1 ONB (US-ONB-001..010)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §1 (SCR-001..006, SCR-017, SCR-019), SCR-111/112/123/154
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (tags `auth`, `users`), `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4, §9.5
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.6, §6.3–6.4 (SR-010..SR-029, SR-050, SR-051)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11, §13; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, §8

title: Playwright E2E suite for login, TOTP, idle lock, step-up and onboarding
body:
## Context
R0 exit criterion 7 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4) requires end-to-end authentication to be demonstrable, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` puts E2E (Playwright, web + Electron) at the top of the pyramid for exactly these user journeys. The E9 stories each ship unit and component tests, but nothing yet walks a real browser from a cold start through password → TOTP → app shell, or proves that an idle session actually locks and recovers.

This ticket implements the automatable portion of the `E09-Q01` plan as a Playwright suite that runs in CI against the ephemeral docker-compose environment, and on staging nightly. It is the regression net every later epic relies on: once E27 (key vault), E39 (kill switch) and E42 (admin) start adding step-up-gated actions, a broken step-up must fail here first, not in production.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright spec files under `tests/e2e/auth/`:
  - `login.spec.ts` — happy path US-ONB-001/002 (`SCR-001` → `SCR-002` → app shell), wrong password, wrong TOTP, expired MFA challenge, locked-after-5-tries state, recovery-code sign-in.
  - `enrolment.spec.ts` — US-ONB-003: first-login forced enrolment (`SCR-003`), QR + selectable secret both present, recovery codes shown exactly once, forced password change (`SCR-004`).
  - `session.spec.ts` — US-ONB-004/009: idle lock modal (`SCR-005`), refresh/resume, absolute-lifetime expiry via clock control, sessions list (`SCR-111`), sign-out everywhere revoking a second browser context.
  - `stepup.spec.ts` — US-ONB-005: step-up modal (`SCR-006`) demanded on a gated action, 5-minute validity, expiry re-prompt, cancel path returns to a safe state.
  - `onboarding.spec.ts` — US-ONB-006/007: invite link (`GET /invites/{inviteToken}`), `SCR-017` wizard including embedded `SCR-004`/`SCR-003`, skip → `SCR-019` checklist persistence, invalid/expired invite.
  - `denied.spec.ts` — `SCR-154` permission-denied page reached by direct URL as a viewer, with no data leakage in the page or network responses.
- A **TOTP helper** (`tests/e2e/support/totp.ts`) generating RFC 6238 codes from the fixture secret, plus a **clock helper** driving server-side time for idle/absolute-lifetime cases without `sleep`.
- **Multi-context fixtures**: two browser contexts for the same user to prove sign-out-everywhere and mid-session revocation.
- **Electron shell run**: the `login` and `session` specs also execute against the Electron build (per `03-testing-strategy.md` E2E scope), tagged `@electron`, so cookie/`SameSite` behaviour is verified in the shipping shell.
- CI wiring: a `e2e-auth` job on every PR touching `area/auth-rbac`, plus inclusion in the nightly full-suite run; traces/videos retained on failure.
- Each spec title carries its `E09-TC-*` id from `E09-Q01` so the traceability table can be generated from test names.

## Out of scope
- RBAC allow/deny enumeration across all routes/topics (`E09-Q03` — contract-level, not E2E).
- axe-core assertions beyond a smoke check (`E09-Q04` owns the audit).
- Load, chaos and clock-skew-at-scale (`E09-Q05`).
- Any test that talks to live or demo Bybit — auth needs no exchange.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cold start to app shell
  Given a seeded owner with TOTP enrolled and an empty browser context
  When the suite signs in with the fixture password and a generated TOTP code
  Then the app shell renders, GET /auth/session returns identity and permissions
  And the session cookie value after MFA differs from the value after the password step

Scenario: Idle lock and resume
  Given an authenticated session and a controlled server clock
  When idle time is advanced past the idle timeout
  Then the re-auth modal SCR-005 appears over preserved application state
  And after a successful re-auth the user returns to the same route without data loss

Scenario: Failure case - sign-out everywhere kills the other context
  Given the same user authenticated in two browser contexts
  When sign-out everywhere is invoked from context A
  Then context B's next request is rejected and it is routed to SCR-001
  And context B's WebSocket receives a revoked frame and closes with 4401

Scenario: Edge case - expired step-up must re-prompt, never silently pass
  Given a step-up was completed and the clock is advanced past its validity window
  When the user retries the gated action
  Then the step-up modal is shown again and the action does not execute
  And no request carrying the stale step-up marker succeeds

Scenario: Suite is deterministic
  Given the auth E2E suite runs 10 consecutive times in CI
  Then the flake rate is below 1% and no test uses a wall-clock sleep
```

## Technical notes / design
Use Playwright's `storageState` only for tests that are *not* about authentication; every auth test starts from a cold context so cookie attributes are actually exercised. Assert cookie flags directly (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, host-only) via `context.cookies()` rather than trusting the UI, per SR-012.

Clock control is server-side (a test-only endpoint or an injectable clock enabled by an env flag that is asserted absent in production builds) — not `page.clock()` alone, because idle/absolute lifetime are server-evaluated. The test-only surface must itself be covered by a test proving it is disabled when the flag is off.

Selectors use role/name queries (`getByRole`) so the suite doubles as a weak a11y oracle: if a control cannot be found by accessible name, that is a defect, not a reason to switch to a CSS selector.

## Test plan
Self-verifying. Additionally: run the suite against a deliberately broken build (rotation disabled) on a scratch branch and confirm `login.spec.ts` fails — a suite that passes against a known-broken implementation is worthless. Record that mutation check in the ticket.

## Security notes
Fixture credentials only; the TOTP fixture secret is stored in the test fixture module and is excluded from any non-test seed. Traces and videos may contain cookie values, so failure artefacts are retained in CI only, with the standard retention, and never attached to public issues. Tests assert that no token, password or recovery code appears in `page` network response bodies logged by the suite.

## Accessibility notes
Every spec drives the UI keyboard-only for at least one path (tab order through `SCR-001`, OTP entry on `SCR-002`, modal focus trap and Escape behaviour on `SCR-005`/`SCR-006`), enforcing `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 and §9's keyboard-E2E gate.

## Performance notes
The suite must complete within the PR-job budget; parallelise by spec file with isolated seeded users so no test serialises on a shared account lockout counter. Argon2id's deliberate ≥100 ms cost (SR-011) is expected and must not be "fixed" by weakening parameters in the test environment — instead use fewer, targeted password verifications.

## Observability
On failure the suite attaches the relevant `audit_log` slice and the backend request ids seen by the browser, so a red E2E run is debuggable without re-running locally.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six spec files merged under `tests/e2e/auth/` and green in CI on web and (for the two tagged specs) Electron.
- [ ] Every automatable `E09-TC-*` case from `E09-Q01` is implemented or explicitly deferred with a follow-up ticket id recorded in the plan.
- [ ] Flake rate <1% across 10 consecutive CI runs; no `sleep`-based waits.
- [ ] Mutation check recorded (suite fails against a deliberately broken auth build).
- [ ] `e2e-auth` job wired as a required check for `area/auth-rbac` PRs.
- [ ] QA lead sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-Q01` — the plan defines the cases and their ids.
- `blocked_by: E09-S03` — idle lock and step-up UI must exist.
- `blocked_by: E09-S05` — invited onboarding and the setup checklist must exist.
- Consumes E03's CI pipeline and ephemeral environment; feeds `E09-Q06` sign-off and the R0 release test report.

## Branch
`chore/e09-e2e-auth-suite`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §6 (E2E), §9, §11
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §1 ONB; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001..006, SCR-017, SCR-019, SCR-111, SCR-154
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-012, SR-013, SR-021, SR-022, SR-024, SR-025
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5 (revoked/bye, close code 4401)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3, §9


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §6 (E2E), §9, §11
2. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §1 ONB; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001..006, SCR-017, SCR-019, SCR-111, SCR-154
3. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-012, SR-013, SR-021, SR-022, SR-024, SR-025
4. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5 (revoked/bye, close code 4401)
5. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3, §9

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `services/api/auth/`
- `services/api/accounts/`
- `services/api/secrets/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Commands**
- `ruff check services/api`

- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`

- Every automatable `E09-TC-*` case from `E09-Q01` is implemented or explicitly deferred with a follow-up ticket id recorded in the plan.

title: RBAC allow/deny matrix regression pack across every route and WS topic
body:
## Context
`SR-018` is unusually prescriptive: *"A test MUST enumerate all registered routes and topics and assert, for each role, the expected allow/deny outcome; adding a route without updating the matrix fails CI."* It exists because `SR-017`'s deny-by-default router only guarantees that a capability was *declared*, not that the *right* capability was declared — threat **U3** ("role check missing on a new endpoint", Critical) and **D1** ("admin screen hidden in the UI but its API remains callable by a Manager", Critical) both land here.

This ticket builds that enumeration as a durable regression pack rather than a one-off test: a machine-readable expectation matrix, a runner that discovers every registered REST route and WS topic at import time, and a CI gate that fails on drift in either direction (a new route with no matrix entry, or a matrix entry for a route that no longer exists).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` — the expectation matrix: one row per (route or WS topic) × role ∈ {Owner, Manager-with-grant, Manager-without-grant, Viewer, unauthenticated}, with the expected outcome (`allow`, `403`, `401`, `sub_ok`, `account_scope_denied`) and the `permission` string from the 36-string vocabulary.
- `tests/contract/rbac/test_route_matrix.py` — discovers routes from the FastAPI app and topics from the WS topic registry (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6), asserts the matrix is total (no undeclared route, no orphan row) and then executes each cell against a live test app with a real session per role.
- **Two-layer assertion** per `SR-050`: for account-scoped routes the pack asserts both the API-boundary capability check *and* the domain-layer grant check, by calling with a valid capability but a non-granted `account_id` and requiring a 403 with nothing mutated.
- **Scope-at-construction assertion** per `SR-051`: list endpoints called by a manager with one grant must not return rows for other accounts; the pack asserts the returned set, and (where a test hook exists) that the SQL carried an `account_id IN (...)` predicate rather than post-filtering.
- **Self-service vs administrative separation** per `SR-026`: assert that self-service routes reject a target-user parameter entirely (400/422, not a silent ignore), and that administrative mutation routes are owner-only and require step-up (`SR-025`).
- **WS parity**: for every private topic, subscribing over a socket authenticated as a non-entitled role yields the specified failure, and an in-flight subscription receives `revoked` when the grant is withdrawn mid-connection.
- **Vocabulary single-source check**: assert `x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, the DB seed and the Python enum agree (complements the `rbac_vocabulary_single_source` test owned by `E09-T03` — this pack consumes it and fails loudly if it is missing).
- CI gate `rbac-matrix` as a required check on `main`.

## Out of scope
- Implementing `authorize()`/the route registry (`E09-T03`) or the WS handshake (`E09-S03`).
- Penetration testing and hand-crafted abuse cases (`E09-X02`, E43).
- Non-auth business assertions about what the endpoints return beyond scope leakage.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Matrix is total over the live route and topic registries
  Given the FastAPI app and the WS topic registry are imported
  When the matrix runner enumerates routes and topics
  Then every discovered route and topic has a matrix row for all five actor profiles
  And every matrix row corresponds to a route or topic that still exists

Scenario: Adding a route without a matrix entry fails CI
  Given a scratch branch adds a new authenticated route with a declared capability
  When the rbac-matrix job runs
  Then the job fails naming the undeclared route
  And the failure message states exactly which matrix rows must be added

Scenario: Failure case - manager reaches another account's data
  Given a manager granted account A only
  When the pack calls an account-scoped route with account_id = B
  Then the response is 403, no row is created or modified, and an audit row records the denial
  And a list endpoint called without an account filter returns rows for A only

Scenario: Edge case - grant revoked mid-subscription
  Given a manager is subscribed to a private topic for account A over an open socket
  When the owner revokes the grant
  Then the socket receives a revoked frame for that topic within the specified window
  And a subsequent resubscribe attempt is denied

Scenario: Edge case - self-service route offered a target user id
  Given an authenticated manager
  When the pack posts a user_id parameter to a self-service profile or password route
  Then the request is rejected as invalid rather than silently applied to the caller
```

## Technical notes / design
Discovery must be reflective, not hand-maintained: read `app.routes` and the WS topic registry so the matrix cannot silently miss a surface. The five actor profiles are seeded once per session and reused; each cell runs with a fresh authenticated session to avoid cross-test contamination from session rotation.

Mutating cells (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) run inside a transaction rolled back after assertion, or against a per-test schema, so "nothing was mutated" is verifiable rather than assumed. Where a route legitimately has no safe mutating call, the matrix marks it `allow-shape-only` and asserts the authorisation decision via the audit row plus a 4xx/2xx distinction, with the reason recorded in the row — silent exclusions are not permitted.

Run time matters: the pack will grow to hundreds of cells as later epics add routes, so cells are parameterised and parallelised by route group, and the runner prints a per-group timing summary to keep the gate under the PR budget.

## Test plan
Mutation-test the gate itself: on a scratch branch, (a) remove a capability declaration — start-up must fail (`SR-017`); (b) widen a capability from owner-only to manager — the matrix must fail; (c) change a list endpoint to post-filter instead of scope-at-construction — the leakage assertion must fail. All three recorded as evidence.

## Security notes
This pack is the primary automated mitigation for U3, U4, D1 and D5 in `04-security-program.md` §5.6/§5.8 and for O1/O7 in §5.7. Its failures are security defects: any red cell is triaged with the Security engineer and cannot be waived by a QA-only decision. The matrix file is code-owned by Security so a widening edit requires their review.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend contract-level pack with no UI surface. The UI's obligation to *hide* unauthorised affordances is verified in `E09-Q02`/`E09-Q04`; hiding is cosmetic and never the control (`04-security-program.md` §8).

## Performance notes
Target: full pack under 3 minutes in CI at R0 size. Sessions are created once per role and reused across read-only cells; Argon2id verification is invoked at most once per role per run.

## Observability
The runner emits a JUnit report plus a rendered matrix artefact (HTML table, green/red per cell) attached to the CI run, which becomes an input to the R0 release test report and to the pen-test brief for E43.

- [ ] WS topic parity including mid-connection revocation covered.
- [ ] Three mutation checks recorded as evidence.

- [ ] Rendered matrix artefact published on every run.
