title: Accessibility audit of the auth, onboarding and settings surfaces
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 makes "axe-core zero violations on the auth routes" an R0 quality gate, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 removes any "internal tool" exemption — the owner/admin screens live in the same RBAC-gated web app and are held to WCAG 2.2 AA like everything else. The auth surfaces are also the hardest a11y problem in the product's early screens: one-time codes, QR codes, timed lockouts, focus-stealing modals over live application state, and error messages that must be announced without leaking which factor failed.

The automated axe gate runs per PR (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §9) and `E09-Q02` drives keyboard-only paths, but neither is an audit. This ticket is the epic-level audit: a manual screen-reader pass on every E09 screen across the §8.1 coverage matrix, plus the structured checks (contrast, zoom/reflow, reduced motion, focus order) that tooling cannot judge.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Audit of screens**: `SCR-001` Login, `SCR-002` TOTP challenge, `SCR-003` TOTP enrolment, `SCR-004` Forced password change, `SCR-005` Session-expired/re-auth modal, `SCR-006` Step-up modal, `SCR-017` Manager/viewer onboarding, `SCR-019` Setup checklist card, `SCR-111` Profile settings (sessions section), `SCR-112` Security settings, `SCR-123` Admin invite user, `SCR-154` Permission denied.
- **Components** `CMP-200` AuthCard, `CMP-201` PasswordField, `CMP-202` PasswordStrengthMeter, `CMP-203` RequirementChecklist, `CMP-204` OtpInput, `CMP-205` QrCode, `CMP-206` RecoveryCodeList, `CMP-207` BuildFooter — audited in Storybook as well as in situ, with the "keyboard interaction" and "accessible name/role" tables required by `05-accessibility-standard.md` §11.6 verified as present and accurate.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** per the §8.1 matrix: NVDA on Windows/Chromium (P0 gate, matching Electron's Chromium), plus the second and third configurations named in the matrix, each executing the §8.2 protocol on every screen above.
- **Structured checks**: focus order and visible focus on every interactive control; modal focus trap + Escape semantics on `SCR-005`/`SCR-006`; error regions announced via `role="alert"` and receiving focus; `aria-live` on OTP entry and password-policy feedback; QR always accompanied by selectable secret text (`SCR-003`); no colour-only status anywhere; contrast ≥4.5:1 body / 3:1 non-text in dark, light and high-contrast themes; 200% zoom and 320 px-width reflow; reduced-motion variant of every transition.
- **Report** `docs/qa/a11y/e09-auth-a11y-audit.md`: per-screen findings table (issue, WCAG SC, severity, evidence, owner), a remediation list filed as bugs with `priority/*`, and a re-test record after fixes.
- **CI reinforcement**: confirm the axe-core Playwright checks cover all twelve routes (adding any missing route to the a11y spec), so the audit's findings are guarded by automation going forward.

## Out of scope
- Designing the fixes (`E09-D06`/`E09-D07` own design-side a11y and design QA); this ticket finds and verifies, it does not redesign.
- Chart-engine/canvas accessibility (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6) — no canvas surface in E09.
- Screens outside E09 (app shell `SCR-010` belongs to E10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Zero serious or critical automated violations on the auth routes
  Given the axe-core Playwright spec covering all twelve E09 routes
  When it runs in CI on the Sprint 04 build
  Then it reports zero new serious or critical violations
  And every moderate or minor violation has a filed backlog ticket with a burn-down target

Scenario: A screen-reader user can complete enrolment without sighted help
  Given NVDA on Windows Chromium and a user who must enrol TOTP at first login
  When the auditor completes SCR-003 using the screen reader only
  Then the secret is reachable as selectable text, its purpose is announced, and the recovery codes are readable and copyable
  And the one-time nature of the recovery-code display is announced before the user can navigate away

Scenario: Failure case - an error that is shown but not announced
  Given an invalid TOTP code is submitted on SCR-002
  When the screen-reader pass is executed
  Then the error must be announced and focus moved to the error region
  And if it is not, a bug is filed against WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 with the recording attached

Scenario: Edge case - modal over live state at 200% zoom
  Given the re-auth modal SCR-005 appears over a populated route at 200% zoom and 320 px width
  Then all modal content reflows without horizontal scrolling and without clipped controls
  And focus is trapped inside the modal, with Escape behaving per the screen catalogue's stated semantics

Scenario: Edge case - reduced motion
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  When any E09 transition or the lockout countdown animates
  Then motion is removed or reduced per 05-accessibility-standard.md section 7 and no information is conveyed by motion alone
```

## Technical notes / design
Run the audit against the staging build, not Storybook alone — several findings (focus restoration after re-auth, announcement ordering when a modal interrupts a live region) only appear in a real route. Use the §8.2 protocol verbatim so results are comparable with other epics' audits.

Countdown timers (lockout on `SCR-001`/`SCR-002`) need special care: an `aria-live="polite"` region ticking every second is a screen-reader denial-of-service. The expected pattern is a politely-announced coarse update (e.g. at 60/30/10 s) plus an on-demand accessible value; verify which pattern shipped and file a bug if the implementation chatters.

## Test plan
The audit is the test. Its own verification is the re-test record: every filed bug is re-checked after the fix, both by the automated axe spec and by a targeted manual pass, and the report is updated with the closing evidence.

## Security notes
Accessibility must not weaken the security posture: verify that the accessible representation of an error does not disclose more than the visual one (SR-014 uniform login errors apply to announcements too), that the recovery-code list is not copied into an offscreen element that persists after navigation, and that no secret is exposed through an `aria-label` or a Storybook fixture committed to the repo.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility work; conformance target WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1. Findings are classified by success criterion, not by subjective severity alone, so the report is auditable.

## Performance notes
Check that live-region updates do not cause layout thrash on the OTP field (one reflow per keystroke is acceptable; a full-card re-render is not) — a perf observation recorded in the report rather than a separate budget.

## Observability
None beyond CI artefacts: axe HTML reports and screen-reader session recordings are attached to the ticket and referenced from the R0 release test report.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/qa/a11y/e09-auth-a11y-audit.md` merged with per-screen findings and evidence.
- [ ] axe-core CI spec covers all twelve E09 routes; zero serious/critical violations.
- [ ] Manual screen-reader passes executed on all three §8.1 configurations, with recordings attached.
- [ ] Every finding fixed or filed with `priority/*`; all fixed findings re-tested and recorded.
- [ ] Component keyboard-interaction and accessible-name tables verified for CMP-200..207.
- [ ] Accessibility role (or the sprint's frontend a11y champion) sign-off comment posted; QA lead sign-off.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-S02` — enrolment and forced password-change screens must exist.
- `blocked_by: E09-S05` — onboarding, checklist and invite screens must exist.
- Related: `E09-D06` (design-side a11y review) and `E09-D07` (design QA) — findings are cross-linked so design and build fixes are not duplicated.

`chore/e09-a11y-audit`

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001..006, SCR-017, SCR-019, SCR-111, SCR-112, SCR-123, SCR-154

title: Auth perf profile and chaos: k6 load, clock skew, Postgres restart
body:
## Context
Authentication has an unusual performance shape: `SR-011` deliberately makes password verification *slow* (Argon2id ≥100 ms on the reference host), which is why `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` excludes it from API latency budget #13 — while `GET /auth/session` sits on the app bootstrap path and must be fast, because every page load waits on it. Getting this wrong in either direction is costly: weaken Argon2id to pass a budget and you break a security requirement; leave the session lookup uncached and every screen in the product inherits the latency.

Auth is also a chaos target. Sessions live in Postgres; TOTP depends on wall-clock agreement; the WS gateway must revoke in-flight connections. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §9 requires chaos scenarios per epic, re-run every release. This ticket writes the k6 profile and the chaos harness for E09 and records the numbers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **k6 script** `perf/k6/auth.js` with four scenarios against a staging backend on recorded fixtures (never live Bybit, never live accounts):
  1. `login_burst` — 5 concurrent users (the §10.3 capacity basis) performing password + TOTP sign-in, reporting p50/p95/p99 separately for the Argon2id step and the rest of the request.
  2. `session_bootstrap` — sustained `GET /auth/session` at app-load rates, asserting ≤100 ms p95 with the in-process session cache warm and reporting the cold-cache figure separately.
  3. `stepup_burst` — `POST /auth/step-up` under concurrency, asserting ≤400 ms p95 (`SCR-006`).
  4. `mfa_verify` — `POST /auth/mfa/verify`, asserting ≤400 ms p95 (`SCR-002`).
- **Rate-limit and lockout behaviour under load** (`SR-015`, `SR-016`): confirm throttling engages per account *and* per source address, that a throttled attacker cannot degrade a legitimate user's sign-in, and that lockout after 10 consecutive failures is enforced without a race under concurrency.
- **Chaos scenarios** in `tests/chaos/auth/`:
  - **Postgres restart mid-session** — existing sessions survive (or fail closed with a clean re-auth prompt, never a partial-auth state); no 500 storm; the app recovers without a manual step.
  - **Clock skew** — host clock moved ±1 and ±3 time steps: ±1 accepted per `SR-021`, ±3 rejected, and a skew beyond tolerance raises a system event rather than silently failing users.
  - **WS gateway restart with live authenticated sockets** — clients reconnect and re-authenticate, and no socket resumes with pre-restart authorisation state.
  - **Revocation storm** — the owner revokes grants for all managers at once; every open socket receives `revoked`/`bye` within the specified window and no stale subscription survives.
  - **Session-store pressure** — many concurrent sessions per user (`SR-019` listing) with expiry sweeping running, verifying the sweeper does not block authentication.
- **Results record** `docs/qa/perf/e09-auth-perf-report.md`: measured numbers against each budget, the reference-host spec, the Argon2id parameters in force, and a pass/fail verdict per budget.

## Out of scope
- WS market-data fan-out load (E17's k6 profile) — only the auth handshake and revocation paths are in scope here.
- Tuning Argon2id parameters (`E09-K01` calibration owns that); this ticket verifies the tuned values hold under concurrency.
- Full-capacity composite scenario (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §10.3) — run at R1+.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Session bootstrap stays off the critical path
  Given the k6 session_bootstrap scenario at realistic app-load concurrency
  When the run completes
  Then GET /auth/session p95 is at or below 100 ms with a warm session cache
  And the cold-cache p95 is reported separately rather than averaged away

Scenario: Argon2id cost is preserved, not optimised away
  Given the login_burst scenario
  When per-step timings are reported
  Then the password-verification step costs at least 100 ms on the reference host
  And the run fails if the configured Argon2id parameters are below m=64MiB, t=3, p=4

Scenario: Failure case - lockout race under concurrency
  Given 20 concurrent wrong-password attempts against one account
  When the attempts complete
  Then the account is locked after the specified threshold with no more than the allowed number of verifications performed
  And no attempt succeeds after the lock, and the owner alert fires exactly once

Scenario: Chaos - Postgres restarts mid-session
  Given authenticated users with open sessions and sockets
  When Postgres is restarted
  Then no user ends in a partially authenticated state
  And either sessions resume cleanly or every affected user is prompted to re-authenticate, with the outcome recorded

Scenario: Chaos - clock skew beyond tolerance
  Given the host clock is moved 3 time steps ahead of the authenticator
  When a user submits a valid TOTP code
  Then the code is rejected, the user sees the specified message, and a system event is raised naming clock skew
  And the event is visible in metrics so the operator can diagnose it without reading logs
```

## Technical notes / design
Run on the reference host defined in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §10.2 and record the spec in the report; an Argon2id number without a host spec is meaningless. Report the login path as two measurements (hash verification vs everything else) so the security-mandated cost is never confused with a regression elsewhere.

Chaos scenarios use the docker-compose test environment with deliberate fault injection (container restart, `libfaketime`/clock offset, forced socket close). Each scenario asserts a *fail-closed* outcome: the acceptable results are "works correctly" or "denies access with a clean recoverable prompt", never "grants access in a degraded state".

The revocation-storm scenario is the one most likely to expose a design gap; if revocation is found to be O(n) per socket in a way that misses the window, file the finding against `E09-S03` rather than relaxing the assertion.

## Test plan
Self-verifying, plus a negative control: run `session_bootstrap` against a build with the session cache disabled and confirm the budget assertion fails, proving the gate has teeth. Record that control in the report.

## Security notes
Load scripts use fixture accounts and a fixture TOTP secret only; the rate-limit scenario is an intentional, authorised, staging-only abuse test and must never be pointed at a production or live-enabled environment — the script refuses to run unless the target's environment flag is `dev` or `staging`. No credentials are written to k6 output or CI logs.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — headless load and fault-injection work with no UI surface. Any user-visible degradation observed during chaos (e.g. a lockout countdown that stops announcing) is filed against `E09-Q04`.

## Performance notes
Budgets verified here: `GET /auth/session` ≤100 ms p95; `POST /auth/mfa/verify` ≤400 ms p95; `POST /auth/step-up` ≤400 ms p95; REST read/write budgets per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` #13 for the non-Argon2id portion; Argon2id ≥100 ms as a *floor*, not a ceiling.

## Observability
The run asserts that the expected metrics exist and move: `cv_auth_login_total{outcome}`, `cv_auth_lockouts_total`, `cv_sessions_active`, `cv_authz_denied_total{permission}`. A scenario that produces the right HTTP behaviour but no metric movement is a failure — R0 must ship with auth observable, per the epic's observability contract.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `perf/k6/auth.js` and `tests/chaos/auth/` merged and runnable in CI (`@chaos` job) and on staging.
- [ ] `docs/qa/perf/e09-auth-perf-report.md` merged with measured numbers, reference-host spec and per-budget verdicts.
- [ ] All five chaos scenarios executed with recorded outcomes; every failure filed with `priority/*`.
- [ ] Negative control recorded (cache-disabled run fails the budget assertion).
- [ ] Metric-movement assertions in place; no credential appears in any artefact.
- [ ] QA lead and Architect sign-off comments posted.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-S01` — the REST auth surface must exist to load.
- `blocked_by: E09-S03` — WS handshake and revocation paths are chaos targets.
- Consumes `E09-K01`'s Argon2id calibration output; feeds `E09-Q06`, the R0 release test report and `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Branch
`chore/e09-auth-perf-chaos`

## References

title: Exploratory charters, epic regression pack and QA sign-off for E09
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an **epic-level** regression and exploratory pass before E09 can be Done — explicitly "not just child-ticket QA". `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 names admin/RBAC boundary probing as a mandatory exploratory charter area. Scripted tests only find what someone already imagined; auth failures in practice come from interaction effects between features that were each individually correct: a password change during an active step-up, an invite accepted while the inviter's role is being revoked, a disabled user with a live socket.

This ticket runs the time-boxed exploratory charters, assembles the durable E09 regression pack from the four preceding QA tickets, and produces the formal QA sign-off that gates the epic.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Four exploratory charters** (60–120 min each, charter format: mission, areas, oracles, debrief — `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2), notes committed under `docs/qa/charters/`:
  1. **Auth state-machine boundaries** — interrupt every transition: close the tab mid-MFA, submit a stale MFA challenge, change password during an active step-up, use a recovery code while a TOTP challenge is pending, re-enrol TOTP with an old authenticator still configured.
  2. **RBAC boundary probing** — a viewer and a grantless manager attempt every admin/owner affordance by deep link, by browser back/forward after a role downgrade, by replaying a captured request, and by opening a WS subscription for another account.
  3. **Session identity and concurrency** — the same user in three contexts with sign-out-everywhere, role change and disable happening concurrently; verify no context retains authority and no context is falsely evicted.
  4. **Onboarding and lockout** — invite links reused, expired, opened by the wrong person, opened twice simultaneously; lockout countdown across a page refresh and a clock change; break-glass documentation followed literally by someone who has never run it.
- **Epic regression pack** `qa/plans/e09-regression-pack.md` + a CI-runnable tag: the subset of `E09-Q02`/`E09-Q03` automation plus the manual cases from `E09-Q01` that must be re-run before every release gate, sized to complete in a single QA day.
- **Cross-ticket rollup**: verify coverage thresholds (≥85% auth/RBAC/audit backend packages, ≥80% auth frontend slice), confirm no open P0/P1 bugs in E09 scope, and check that each story's Gherkin AC has a named automated test or a recorded manual execution.
- **QA sign-off record** on the epic ticket: pass/fail per story group, charter debriefs, deferred P2/P3 defects with owner acknowledgement, and the white-box review checklist (`03-testing-strategy.md` §11.4) completion statement.
- **Release test report contribution** for R0: coverage snapshot, E2E results, chaos outcomes, perf budget compliance, a11y sweep summary, open-bug list by severity.

## Out of scope
- Writing new automation (owned by `E09-Q02`/`E09-Q03`) — this ticket may file follow-ups but does not implement suites.
- Security-owned deliverables: STRIDE (`E09-X01`), abuse cases (`E09-X02`), the security review and break-glass drill (`E09-X04`).
- Design QA (`E09-D07`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All four charters executed with debriefs
  Given the Sprint 04 staging build
  When each charter is run within its time box
  Then a debrief note exists naming what was probed, what was not, and every anomaly observed
  And every anomaly is either filed as a bug or explicitly dismissed with a reason

Scenario: Epic rollup is green before sign-off
  Given the coverage reports and the E09 bug list
  When the rollup is checked
  Then backend auth/RBAC/audit packages are at or above 85% and the auth frontend slice at or above 80%
  And no P0 or P1 bug against E09 scope is open

Scenario: Failure case - an acceptance criterion with no evidence
  Given a story whose Gherkin scenario maps to no automated test and no recorded manual execution
  When the rollup check runs
  Then sign-off is withheld and the gap is filed against that story
  And the epic cannot move to Done until the gap is closed or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition

Scenario: Edge case - concurrent role change during an active session
  Given a manager mid-way through a step-up-gated action
  When the owner revokes the manager's role at that instant
  Then the action is refused, the session reflects the new role on the next request, and the audit log shows both events in order
  And no partially applied effect remains

Scenario: Regression pack is re-runnable by a different person
  Given a QA engineer who did not build the pack
  When they execute qa/plans/e09-regression-pack.md against a fresh staging deploy
  Then the pack completes within one QA day with an unambiguous pass/fail per item
```

## Technical notes / design
Charters are deliberately unscripted; the value is in the oracles. Define them up front per charter — e.g. "any screen reachable that the role's permission set does not include", "any state where a user is authenticated but the audit log has no corresponding login row", "any error that differs between an unknown user and a wrong password". An anomaly that matches an oracle is a bug even if no written case covers it.

Run charters against staging with the fixture user set from `E09-Q01`, and keep a session recording so a surprising finding can be reconstructed. Where a charter finds something that scripted tests should have caught, file a *second* ticket to extend the automation — the charter's lasting output is better coverage, not just a bug.

## Test plan
Meta-level: the regression pack is validated by a cold execution (a QA engineer who did not write it runs it end-to-end) and the timing is recorded; if it exceeds one QA day it is trimmed to the highest-risk items, with the trimmed items noted as "release-gate only".

## Security notes
Charter 2 (RBAC boundary probing) overlaps the Security engineer's abuse cases (`E09-X02`); findings are cross-posted and the Security engineer co-reviews charter 2's debrief. Anything suggesting authentication bypass, privilege escalation or audit-log gaps is escalated the same day and blocks R0 regardless of QA's own severity judgement (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).

## Accessibility notes
Each charter includes at least one keyboard-only segment per `03-testing-strategy.md` §10; a screen that cannot be exercised keyboard-only during exploration is filed against `E09-Q04` rather than worked around.

## Performance notes
Charters note any subjectively slow interaction (>1 s to a visible response outside the Argon2id path) as an observation for `E09-Q05` to measure; exploration does not produce budget numbers itself.

## Observability
During every charter the auditor keeps the audit log and the auth metrics visible; "the action happened but produced no audit row or metric movement" is a first-class oracle, since audit completeness is an R0 requirement and a repudiation control (threat U7).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Four charter debriefs committed under `docs/qa/charters/` and attached to the epic.
- [ ] `qa/plans/e09-regression-pack.md` merged, cold-executed by a second person, completing within one QA day.
- [ ] Coverage rollup verified; no open P0/P1 in E09 scope; every story AC traced to evidence.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted on E09 with pass/fail per story group and deferred-defect acknowledgements.
- [ ] R0 release-test-report section drafted and handed to the PRR owner.
- [ ] Follow-up automation tickets filed for every charter finding that scripted tests should have caught.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-Q02, E09-Q03, E09-Q04, E09-Q05` — the pack and sign-off roll up all four.
- Coordinates with `E09-X04` (security review + break-glass drill) so charter 2 and the abuse-case review are not duplicated.
- Gates the epic's DoD (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2) and feeds `07-release-and-prr.md`'s R0 PRR.

`chore/e09-qa-signoff`

- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1–11.4, §13

title: STRIDE threat model for authentication, sessions, 2FA, RBAC and audit
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 requires a STRIDE model per epic, re-reviewed when the epic enters design, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes the kickoff a DoR item that is default-on for any epic touching auth. §5.6 "Area 6 — Authentication & RBAC (A-03, A-04)" already lists threats **U1–U10**, but that table was written at programme level against an intended design; E09 now has a concrete design (ADR-0010: Argon2id + mandatory TOTP, opaque server-side sessions in Postgres, one central `authorize()`/`ScopeResolver`, hash-chained append-only audit) with concrete data flows, and the model must be re-derived against what is actually being built.

This epic is also where three assets with the highest classification in the programme live: **A-03 credentials (SECRET)**, **A-04 session/refresh tokens (SECRET)**, and the audit log that every other epic's non-repudiation depends on. A modelling miss here is not contained to E09 — E27 (key vault), E39 (kill switch), E42 (admin) and E44 (live enablement) all inherit its controls.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Data-flow diagram** (mermaid, committed with the model) with trust boundaries drawn explicitly: browser ↔ Tailscale ↔ API gateway; gateway ↔ **M18 Auth/RBAC**; M18 ↔ Postgres (`users`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`); M18 ↔ **M19 Audit** (`audit_log`, `audit_checkpoints`); WS gateway ↔ M18 for the `auth` → `auth_ok` handshake and mid-connection revocation; the offline break-glass CLI ↔ host filesystem + KEK; the invite flow's out-of-band link delivery.
- **STRIDE analysis per element and per flow**, in the `04-security-program.md` §5 table format (`T` id, category, threat, likelihood, impact, risk, mitigating SR ids, residual risk), re-deriving and extending U1–U10 with at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** — credential stuffing (U1); phishing a manager's password (U2); session-token theft via XSS or logs (U5); session fixation if rotation is missed on any transition (U6); TOTP code replay within the skew window; an invite token guessed or replayed; the WS `auth` frame replayed onto a second socket.
  - **Tampering** — direct `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on `audit_log`; a forged `account_id` in a request body; role/permission seed drift between the OpenAPI `x-rbac` vocabulary, the DB seed and the Python enum; an Alembic migration that silently widens a grant; client-side manipulation of the step-up marker.
  - **Repudiation** — an authenticated action with no audit row; a shared login making attribution impossible (U7); audit chain gaps across a restart or a migration; clock manipulation making audit ordering untrustworthy.
  - **Information disclosure** — user enumeration via differing error bodies, status codes or timing (U8); a token in a URL, log line, metric label, error message or Sentry-style report; recovery codes persisted in the DOM or in browser history; `users.email`, `sessions.ip`, `audit_log.actor_ip` as PII in exports; a 403 that reveals the existence of a resource; Viewer-visible `build`/`git_sha` metadata.
  - **Denial of service** — lockout weaponised against a legitimate user (an attacker locking the owner out deliberately); Argon2id's ≥100 ms cost used as an amplification vector; session-table growth; owner total lockout on a lost TOTP device (U10).
  - **Elevation of privilege** — a new endpoint shipped without a capability declaration (U3, Critical); self-service role escalation (U4); an admin API callable despite a hidden UI (D1); shared handlers exposing owner-only mutation through a self-service route (D5); a stale permission snapshot in a live session surviving a role change; account-scope bypass (O1) and cross-manager data leakage (O7) as they apply to the auth layer's `ScopeResolver`.
- **Control mapping**: every threat maps to at least one of SR-010..SR-029, SR-050, SR-051, SR-055, SR-112, SR-122 — or to a **new** requirement proposed back into `04-security-program.md`, or to an accepted risk with a dated Owner signature.
- **Verification mapping**: every mitigation names the test that proves it (`E09-Q03` matrix cell, `E09-Q02` E2E spec, a unit test, or `E09-X03`'s SAST/DAST rule). A mitigation with no named verification is itself a finding.
- **Residual-risk register update**: `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` entries added/retired.
- Model committed at `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`, reviewed with the Architect and the epic owner in a scheduled session.

## Out of scope
- Implementing controls (the E09 `T*`/`S*` tickets) or writing the detection rules (`E09-X03`).
- Abuse-case execution (`E09-X02`) and the review/drill (`E09-X04`).
- API-key vault threats (E27's own model) and OMS/fan-out threats (§5.7/§5.9, later epics) except where they consume E09's `authorize()`.
- External pen-testing (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and flow is analysed
  Given the committed data-flow diagram
  When the STRIDE tables are checked against it
  Then every element and every cross-boundary flow has at least one row per applicable STRIDE category or a recorded "not applicable" reason
  And no element appears in the diagram without a corresponding analysis section

Scenario: Every threat has a mitigation and a named verification
  Given the completed threat table
  When each row is inspected
  Then it names a mitigating SR id (existing or newly proposed) and the specific test that verifies it
  And any row without a verification is filed as a finding with an owner and a due date

Scenario: Failure case - a Critical threat with no control
  Given threat U3, a route shipped without a capability declaration
  When the model checks the mitigation
  Then it must demonstrate that application start-up fails on an undeclared route, not merely that a review would catch it
  And if the implementation does not fail closed, the model records a Critical finding blocking R0

Scenario: Edge case - owner total lockout
  Given the owner loses the TOTP device and all recovery codes
  When the model analyses U10
  Then the break-glass path is modelled as its own trust boundary, including who can reach the host filesystem and the KEK
  And the residual risk of that path being abused is stated explicitly, not assumed away

Scenario: Model is reviewed, not just written
  Given the model document is complete
  When the review session is held
  Then the Architect and the epic owner have recorded comments
  And the risk register reflects any new or retired risk
```

## Technical notes / design
Model the design in ADR-0010 as built, not as idealised. Two areas deserve disproportionate attention because they are where this design differs from a generic web app:

1. **The single `authorize()` chokepoint** is a strength (one place to get right) and a concentration risk (one place to get wrong). Model what happens if it is bypassed, if it is called with a default-permissive argument, and if a route's declared capability is correct but its *scope* argument is not — the second-layer domain check (SR-050) exists precisely for that case and must be modelled as a distinct control, not a duplicate.
2. **The audit hash chain** is computed by a Postgres trigger with `UPDATE`/`DELETE` revoked. Model the trust placed in the database role: who can alter the trigger, who can `ALTER TABLE`, what a compromised migration could do, and how the nightly chain verifier detects each case. A chain that only detects row edits but not trigger replacement is a finding.

Use the same table shape as §5 so the model can be folded into the programme document without reformatting, and keep threat ids stable (`U*` for area 6) so cross-references from other epics keep resolving.

## Test plan
The model is a document, but it is falsifiable: for each of the top five risks, write a one-line "how we would know this control failed" statement and confirm that detection exists (a test, a metric, or an alert). Where detection does not exist, file it. The model's own review checklist is the `04-security-program.md` §5 completeness criteria.

## Security notes
The document itself is sensitive: it enumerates weaknesses in the authentication system. It lives in the private repo under `docs/security/`, is code-owned by the Security engineer, and must contain no live secrets, no host addresses and no KEK material — only references to where those live.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — a document with no UI surface. Where a control has an accessibility consequence (e.g. an anti-enumeration message that must still be announced to a screen reader), the model notes it and routes it to `E09-Q04` rather than choosing a less accessible control silently.

## Performance notes
Where a control has a performance cost, the model states it and points at the budget: Argon2id ≥100 ms (excluded from budget #13), the session-cache invalidation required to keep `GET /auth/session` ≤100 ms p95 while still revoking promptly, and the cost of writing an audit row on every authenticated mutation.

## Observability
The model specifies the minimum detections for area 6: `cv_auth_login_total{outcome}`, `cv_auth_lockouts_total`, `cv_authz_denied_total{permission}`, `cv_audit_chain_verified`, `cv_network_binding_ok`, plus the alert conditions (lockout burst, chain-verification failure, binding self-check failure) that must exist before R0 ships.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md` merged with diagram, STRIDE tables, control mapping and verification mapping.
- [ ] Every threat mapped to an SR id, a new proposed requirement, or a dated Owner-signed accepted risk.
- [ ] Every mitigation names a verifying test; gaps filed as tickets with owners.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated for new/retired risks.
- [ ] Review session held with the Architect and epic owner; comments recorded.
- [ ] Security-engineer sign-off comment posted; findings routed to `E09-X02`/`E09-X03`/`E09-X04`.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-D01` — the UX research on auth, first-run and lockout flows defines the real user paths (including lockout perception and recovery-code handling) the model must cover.
- Informs `E09-T04` (PDP), `E09-T02` (audit chain), `E09-T04` (binding self-check), `E09-X02`, `E09-X03`, `E09-X04`.
- Consumed by E27, E39, E42, E43, E44, which inherit these controls.

title: Abuse cases and adversarial testing of auth, session and RBAC boundaries
body:
## Context
`E09-X01` says what could go wrong; this ticket tries it. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires, for anything touching keys, withdrawal or RBAC, "a manual abuse-case check performed (e.g. attempt privilege escalation, attempt withdrawal toggle)" before Done — a real attempt, not a code reading. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12 assigns exploratory *security* charters against auth/RBAC boundary conditions, and R0 must ship with those results recorded, because E43's external pen-test is scheduled far later (before R4 Live enablement) and R0 cannot wait for it.

The controls under test are the ones the rest of the product assumes: rotation on every authentication transition (SR-013), uniform login errors (SR-014), TOTP replay rejection (SR-021), single-use recovery codes (SR-022), deny-by-default routing (SR-017), two-layer authorisation (SR-050/SR-051), step-up gating (SR-025) and audit tamper-evidence.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case catalogue** `docs/security/abuse-cases/e09-auth.md`, each case written from the attacker's goal: precondition, attacker capability assumed, steps, expected defence, observed result, verdict, and the control id it exercises.
- **Executed cases**, at minimum:
  - *Credential attacks* — offline-style guessing against a captured hash (confirm Argon2id parameters actually in force in the DB, not just in config); online stuffing against the rate limiter (SR-015) from one and from many source addresses; deliberate lockout of another user as a denial-of-service (SR-016) and the resulting owner alert.
  - *Enumeration* — compare status, body and response-time distributions for unknown user / wrong password / wrong TOTP / locked account / disabled user across hundreds of samples; a statistically detectable difference is a finding (SR-014, U8).
  - *Session attacks* — fixation (reuse a pre-login session id after login and after MFA — must fail, SR-013); theft simulation (replay a captured cookie from a different address/user agent; record whether it is accepted and whether it is detectable); cookie-flag downgrade attempts; refresh-token reuse triggering family revocation; CSRF against every state-changing route with and without the double-submit token (TB-4).
  - *MFA attacks* — TOTP replay inside the skew window (SR-021); brute force of the 6-digit code against the rate limiter; recovery-code reuse and reuse-after-regeneration (SR-022); racing two concurrent MFA verifications for the same challenge; completing MFA for a challenge issued to a different user.
  - *Authorisation attacks* — every admin/owner route called as Manager and as Viewer (D1); `account_id` tampering in body, query and path (O1); a list endpoint probed for other accounts' rows (O7); self-service route given a `user_id` (D5, SR-026); self-elevation attempts (U4, SR-055); the step-up marker replayed, extended, or transplanted to another user/action (SR-025); a role change applied while the victim session is live, then the old session used.
  - *WS attacks* — subscribing to a private topic before `auth_ok`; replaying a captured `auth` frame on a second socket; holding a socket open across a grant revocation; topic-name injection attempting to escape the registry.
  - *Audit attacks* — attempt `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on `audit_log` as the application role; attempt to blank a row via a crafted migration on a scratch branch; confirm the nightly chain verifier detects each; attempt to perform an audited action in a way that produces no row.
  - *Invite/onboarding attacks* — invite-token guessing and enumeration; reuse after acceptance; acceptance by a different identity; an expired invite still granting a session; a `Viewer`-default violation (SR-027) by an invite that arrives pre-elevated.
- **Automation of the durable subset** into `tests/security/auth/` so the cases become permanent regressions (the rest stay manual with a re-run cadence stated per case).
- **Findings** filed with STRIDE category, severity, reproduction and suggested fix; each mapped back to an `E09-X01` threat id.

## Out of scope
- Building the detection rules (`E09-X03`) or running the formal review/break-glass drill (`E09-X04`).
- Attacks on the API-key vault (E27) or the order path (E32/E34) beyond how they consume `authorize()` and step-up.
- External/black-box pen-testing (E43) — this is internal, white-box-informed adversarial testing.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every X01 threat with an executable attack has an attempted case
  Given the E09-X01 threat table
  When the abuse-case catalogue is cross-checked
  Then every threat that can be attempted against a running system has a case with an observed result
  And threats that cannot be attempted record why (e.g. requires physical host access, covered by the break-glass drill)

Scenario: Session fixation is defeated
  Given a session id captured before authentication
  When it is presented after a successful password step and again after MFA
  Then it is rejected in both cases and the audit log records the attempt
  And the id issued after MFA differs from the id issued after the password step

Scenario: Failure case - a successful privilege escalation
  Given any case that results in a Manager or Viewer performing an owner-only action
  When the result is recorded
  Then it is filed as a P0 critical finding, R0 is blocked, and the Owner is notified the same day
  And a regression test reproducing the escalation is added before the fix is merged

Scenario: Edge case - timing-based user enumeration
  Given 500 login attempts split between an unknown user and a known user with a wrong password
  When the response-time distributions are compared
  Then they are statistically indistinguishable at the agreed threshold
  And any measurable separation is filed against SR-014 with the sample data attached

Scenario: Edge case - audit row cannot be altered by the application role
  Given the application's database role
  When it attempts UPDATE and DELETE on audit_log and then attempts to drop the chain trigger
  Then all attempts are refused, and any that succeed are a Critical finding
  And the nightly chain verifier is shown to detect a row modified out-of-band by a superuser
```

## Technical notes / design
Run exclusively against the ephemeral CI environment and staging, never against a live-enabled environment; the harness refuses to start unless the target reports environment `dev`/`staging`. Attacks that generate sustained load (stuffing, code brute force) are rate-limited by the harness itself so the exercise measures the *defence*, not the test runner's ability to saturate a laptop.

Timing analysis needs statistical discipline: fixed sample size agreed up front, warm-up discarded, comparison by distribution (e.g. Mann-Whitney) rather than by mean, and the same host for both arms. A naive mean comparison will either miss a real leak or manufacture a false one.

Where a case exposes a design gap rather than a bug — e.g. cookie replay from another address is accepted because the design deliberately does not bind sessions to IP — record it as a *design decision to confirm* with the Architect and the Owner, with the residual risk written down, rather than silently filing a bug against an intended behaviour.

## Test plan
Each case is its own test. The ticket's verification is twofold: (a) the durable subset runs green in CI as regressions; (b) a mutation check — deliberately disable rotation, recovery-code consumption and the `audit_log` revocations on a scratch branch and confirm the corresponding cases *fail*, proving the catalogue detects the very problems it claims to cover.

## Security notes
This is authorised adversarial testing of our own system, conducted by the Security engineer with the epic owner's knowledge, on non-production environments only. Captured artefacts (cookies, hashes, timing samples) are treated as SECRET, kept in CI-retained artefacts and the private security folder, and destroyed after the findings are closed. No finding is published outside the private repo before it is fixed.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — protocol-level adversarial testing with no UI deliverable. Where a proposed mitigation would harm usability or accessibility (e.g. a CAPTCHA-style control), it is routed through `E09-D01`/`E09-Q04` before adoption rather than imposed unilaterally.

## Performance notes
The stuffing and code-brute-force cases double as a check that the rate limiter degrades gracefully: a defended endpoint must reject cheaply, without each rejection costing a full Argon2id verification — otherwise the defence is itself an amplification vector (an X01 DoS threat).

## Observability
Every case records whether the attack was *visible*: which metric moved (`cv_auth_login_total{outcome="failed"}`, `cv_auth_lockouts_total`, `cv_authz_denied_total`), which audit action was written, and whether an alert would have fired. An attack that is defended but invisible is filed as an observability finding — silent defence is how repeated attempts go unnoticed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/security/abuse-cases/e09-auth.md` merged with every case's observed result and verdict.
- [ ] Durable subset automated under `tests/security/auth/` and green in CI.
- [ ] Every finding filed with STRIDE category, severity, repro and owner; P0/P1 findings fixed before R0.
- [ ] Mutation check recorded (disabled controls cause the corresponding cases to fail).
- [ ] Timing-analysis sample data attached; SR-014 verdict recorded.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated; Security-engineer sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-X01` — the threat model defines what to attempt.
- `blocked_by: E09-S01, E09-S03` — the REST surface and WS handshake must exist to attack.
- Overlaps `E09-Q06` charter 2 (RBAC boundary probing) — findings cross-posted, charter co-reviewed.
- Feeds `E09-X03` (turn findings into rules), `E09-X04` (review), E43 (pen-test scoping).

title: SAST/DAST rules, secret scanning and CI security gates for the auth surface
body:
## Context
Generic SAST catches generic bugs. The failure modes that matter in E09 are project-specific and invisible to an off-the-shelf rule set: a route handler that reads `account_id` from the request instead of from the resolved scope, a log statement that interpolates a session token, a self-service route that accepts a `user_id`, a new endpoint registered without a capability, a step-up-gated action that forgot its decorator. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12 and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §11 mandate SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA, secrets scanning and DAST (ZAP baseline per PR, full active scan weekly and before each release gate, "targeting the RBAC-gated admin surface... specifically").

This ticket turns the E09 threat model and abuse-case findings into **enforcing automation**: custom Semgrep rules, a tuned ZAP configuration for the authenticated surface, secret-scanning patterns for our token shapes, and the CI wiring that makes all of it merge-blocking.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Custom Semgrep rules** under `security/semgrep/auth/`, each shipped with a positive and a negative fixture:
  - `no-raw-account-id` — a handler using a request-supplied `account_id` without passing it through the `ScopeResolver` intersection (SR-051).
  - `no-adhoc-authz` — any permission/role comparison outside the single `authorize()` implementation (SR-017, ADR-0010 invariant 1).
  - `no-target-user-on-self-service` — a self-service route signature accepting a user identifier (SR-026, D5).
  - `stepup-required` — a route in the SR-025 action list lacking the step-up dependency.
  - `no-secret-logging` — logging/f-string interpolation of password, token, session id, TOTP code, recovery code or invite token variables (SR-122).
  - `no-jwt-in-browser-storage` — frontend rule forbidding token persistence in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` (ADR-0010: opaque server-side sessions only).
  - `cookie-flags` — session cookie construction missing `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` or host-only scope (SR-012).
  - `argon2-params` — an Argon2id configuration below `m=64MiB, t=3, p=4` (SR-011).
  - `audit-write-required` — a mutating handler in the audited-action list with no audit call.
- **Bandit/CodeQL tuning** for the auth packages: suppress documented false positives with justifications in-file (never blanket-ignore a rule), and confirm the crypto/randomness rules are active where recovery codes and session tokens are generated (128/256-bit CSPRNG, SR-012/SR-022).
- **Secret scanning** (gitleaks) patterns for our own token shapes — session token, refresh token, invite token, recovery code, TOTP secret — plus a pre-commit hook and a history scan of the repo to date.
- **ZAP configuration** `security/zap/auth-context.yaml`: an authenticated context (script-based login + TOTP using the fixture user), the session-management and CSRF-token configuration so ZAP stays authenticated, an exclusion list for genuinely destructive endpoints with reasons, and an active-scan policy tuned to the auth/admin surface. Baseline scan on every PR to `main`; full active scan weekly and before each release gate.
- **SCA**: pip-audit/npm audit/Dependabot coverage confirmed for the auth dependency set (Argon2 binding, TOTP library, cookie/session middleware), with alerting on the crypto-relevant packages specifically.
- **CI wiring**: a `security-auth` job aggregating the above, merge-blocking on new high/critical findings, with a documented triage path for accepted risks.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the code the rules find (routed to the owning `T*`/`S*` ticket).
- The threat model (`E09-X01`) and abuse-case execution (`E09-X02`).
- Container and infrastructure scanning (Trivy, owned by E03/E04) except confirming the auth service image is in scope.
- Pen-testing (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every custom rule is proven on a vulnerable fixture
  Given each rule in security/semgrep/auth/
  When the rule runs against its positive fixture and its negative fixture
  Then it fires on the positive and stays silent on the negative
  And the CI job fails if any rule lacks either fixture

Scenario: A regression is caught before merge
  Given a scratch branch that logs a session token and adds a route with an ad hoc role check
  When the security-auth job runs
  Then it fails, naming both findings with file and line
  And the failure message points to the SR id each rule enforces

Scenario: Failure case - ZAP loses its session mid-scan
  Given the authenticated ZAP context
  When the active scan runs against the auth and admin surface
  Then ZAP remains authenticated for the whole scan, verified by a logged-in indicator check
  And a scan that silently drops to unauthenticated is treated as a failed scan, not a clean one

Scenario: Edge case - suppressions are justified and expiring
  Given a false positive suppressed in-file
  When the job inspects suppressions
  Then each carries a reason, an owner and a review date
  And an undated or unowned blanket suppression fails the job

Scenario: Edge case - secret scanning catches our own token shapes
  Given a commit containing a plausible session token and a recovery code
  When gitleaks runs in the pre-commit hook and in CI
  Then both are detected and the commit is blocked
  And the repo history scan reports no pre-existing matches, or each match is documented and rotated
```

## Technical notes / design
Rules must be written against the *shapes the codebase actually uses*, which means writing them after `E09-T04` lands the PDP and route registry — a rule written speculatively will either miss everything or drown the team in noise. Noise is the real failure mode: each rule is measured against the full repo before landing, and a rule producing more than a handful of findings that are all false is reworked, not merged with a blanket suppression.

The `no-adhoc-authz` and `stepup-required` rules need an allowlist (the `authorize()` implementation itself; routes legitimately outside SR-025). The allowlist is a data file, code-owned by Security, so widening it requires their review — the same pattern as the RBAC matrix in `E09-Q03`.

ZAP's authenticated context is the fiddly part: the login script must complete password + TOTP (using the fixture secret) and refresh when the session rotates, since rotation on every authentication transition (SR-013) will otherwise log the scanner out. Verify with an explicit logged-in/logged-out indicator regex, and fail the job when the indicator is lost.

## Test plan
Unit-style fixture tests per Semgrep rule (positive/negative). An end-to-end check: a deliberately vulnerable branch containing one violation of each rule must produce exactly the expected finding set — no misses, no extras. ZAP is validated by pointing it at the same vulnerable branch and confirming it reports the injected authenticated-surface issue.

## Security notes
The fixture credentials and the fixture TOTP secret used by ZAP are test-only and stored as CI secrets, never in the repo; the gitleaks patterns are written so they would catch those values if they ever were committed. Scan reports may contain request/response bodies with tokens, so artefacts are retained privately in CI with the standard retention and never attached to public issues.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — CI tooling with no UI surface.

## Performance notes
The PR-time portion (Semgrep + gitleaks + ZAP baseline) must stay within the PR job budget; the expensive full active scan runs weekly and pre-gate. Rule performance is measured — a rule that adds disproportionate scan time is rewritten or moved to the scheduled job.

## Observability
Findings are published as a CI check summary with counts by severity and rule, trended over time so a rising false-positive rate is visible and can be fixed rather than tolerated. Gate failures link directly to the SR id and the E09-X01 threat they defend.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All nine custom Semgrep rules merged, each with positive and negative fixtures, and each demonstrated failing on a deliberately vulnerable fixture then passing on `main`.
- [ ] Bandit/CodeQL tuning applied with justified, dated, owned suppressions only.
- [ ] gitleaks patterns + pre-commit hook in place; full history scan clean or documented with rotation evidence.
- [ ] ZAP authenticated context works end-to-end through password + TOTP + session rotation; baseline wired per PR, full scan scheduled weekly and pre-gate.
- [ ] SCA coverage confirmed for the auth dependency set.
- [ ] `security-auth` job merge-blocking on new high/critical findings, with a documented triage path.
- [ ] Security-engineer sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E09-X01` — the threat model determines which rules are worth writing.
- `blocked_by: E09-T04` — rules are written against the real PDP/route-registry shapes.
- Consumes E03's CI pipeline; consumed by `E09-X04` and by every later epic adding auth-adjacent code.

## Branch
`chore/e09-security-gates`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.3 (SR-011, SR-012, SR-017, SR-022, SR-025, SR-026), §6.4 (SR-050, SR-051), SR-112, SR-122, §11
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0010-auth-and-rbac.md`
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7 (required checks)
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1–15.2

1. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.3 (SR-011, SR-012, SR-017, SR-022, SR-025, SR-026), §6.4 (SR-050, SR-051), SR-112, SR-122, §11

title: Security review, break-glass drill and Owner sign-off for E09
body:
## Context
E09's DoD (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2) requires a finalised STRIDE model with findings triaged and a Security-engineer sign-off; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 makes that sign-off an R0 quality gate. Two E09 controls cannot be proven by automated tests at all and must be *rehearsed*: **SR-023**, the documented break-glass path for total Owner lockout (an offline CLI runnable only with filesystem access to the host and the KEK), and **SR-029**, immediate termination of a disabled user's sessions and pending actions. A break-glass procedure that has never been executed is a procedure that does not work.

This ticket is the closing security gate for the epic: a white-box review of the implemented controls, the two drills, triage of everything `E09-X02` and `E09-X03` surfaced, and the recorded sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box control review** against the threat model, walking the implementation with the epic owner: the single `authorize()` chokepoint and its two-layer enforcement (SR-050/SR-051); session lifecycle and rotation points (SR-013 — login, TOTP completion, step-up, password change, role change, each verified in code and in behaviour); Argon2id parameters and transparent hash upgrade (SR-011); TOTP skew and replay cache (SR-021); recovery-code generation, hashing, single-use and regeneration semantics (SR-022); session timeouts and the 12-hour trading-capability freshness rule (SR-024); step-up scope and validity (SR-025); `Viewer`-by-default user creation (SR-027); password policy and other-session invalidation on change (SR-028); the audit chain trigger, revoked grants and the nightly verifier; the Tailscale-only binding self-check and its fail-closed read-only behaviour (US-ONB-008).
- **Break-glass drill (SR-023)**: executed on a staging host by a person following only the written runbook, with the Owner's TOTP device treated as lost and recovery codes unavailable. Record: elapsed time, every point where the runbook was ambiguous, whether the CLI refuses to run without filesystem access and the KEK, that an audit event was written, and that the UI loudly surfaces the event afterwards. Runbook corrections are merged as part of this ticket.
- **Disable-user drill (SR-029)**: disable a user with a live session, an open WS subscription and pending activity; verify sessions terminate immediately, the socket receives `revoked`/`bye`, pending rule-engine actions are cancelled, and the recorded decision about positions exists. Record elapsed time from action to full effect.
- **Findings triage**: every finding from `E09-X01`, `E09-X02`, `E09-X03` and `E09-Q03`/`E09-Q06` is fixed, ticketed with an owner and a date, or accepted with a dated Owner signature and a residual-risk statement.
- **Sign-off record** `docs/security/reviews/e09-auth-review.md`: control-by-control verdict, drill reports, the triage table, residual risks, and the explicit statement that R0's security gate for area 6 is met.
- **Risk register and pen-test brief**: `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated; a scoping note handed to E43 listing the controls that most warrant external testing before R4 Live enablement.

## Out of scope
- Building or fixing controls (routed to the owning tickets) — this ticket verifies and signs off.
- External pen-testing (E43) and live-enablement gating (E44).
- E27's key-vault review, which reuses this epic's step-up and audit plumbing but has its own model and sign-off.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every control has a recorded verdict
  Given the control list derived from SR-010..SR-029, SR-050, SR-051 and the E09 threat model
  When the review document is complete
  Then each control has pass, fail-with-ticket, or accepted-risk-with-Owner-signature
  And no control is left without a verdict

Scenario: Break-glass works for someone who has never run it
  Given a staging host and an engineer who did not write the runbook
  When they follow SR-023 with the Owner's TOTP device treated as lost
  Then the Owner's TOTP is reset, an audit event is written, and the UI surfaces the event loudly afterwards
  And every ambiguity encountered is corrected in the runbook before this ticket closes

Scenario: Failure case - break-glass CLI reachable without the intended preconditions
  Given the CLI is invoked without filesystem access to the host or without the KEK
  When it runs
  Then it refuses and writes an attempt record
  And if it proceeds, that is a Critical finding blocking R0

Scenario: Edge case - disabling a user with a live socket
  Given a manager with an active session, an open private subscription and pending rule-engine actions
  When the owner disables the user
  Then sessions terminate immediately, the socket receives revoked/bye, pending actions are cancelled
  And the recorded decision about their positions exists in the audit log

Scenario: Epic security gate is explicit
  Given all findings are triaged
  When the sign-off is recorded
  Then it names the reviewer, the date, the open accepted risks and their Owner signatures
  And E09 cannot be marked Done without this record
```

## Technical notes / design
The review is white-box and conversational: read the code with the implementer rather than from a report, because the interesting failures here are omissions (a rotation point not called, an audited action with no audit write) which are invisible in a diff-by-diff review. Use the control list as the agenda so nothing is skipped when time runs short.

Run the break-glass drill unrehearsed and time-boxed, with a scribe. The common outcome is not "it failed" but "it took three times longer than expected because step 4 assumed knowledge" — that is the finding worth capturing, and it is only capturable if the operator is genuinely unfamiliar.

For accepted risks, insist on an expiry: an accepted risk without a review date becomes permanent by accident. Each carries a date by which it is re-examined, and those dates are mirrored into `32-risk-register.md`.

## Test plan
The drills are the tests, executed once with recorded evidence. In addition, verify that each drill has a lighter automated counterpart where possible (an integration test for disable-user propagation; a test asserting the break-glass CLI refuses without its preconditions) so the next regression is caught without a full drill.

## Security notes
The drill touches the most sensitive path in the system. It is performed on staging only, with a staging KEK; the production KEK is never used in a drill. The review document names weaknesses and therefore stays in the private repo under `docs/security/`, code-owned by Security. Any finding rated Critical is reported to the Owner the same day and blocks R0.

## Accessibility notes
The post-break-glass UI notification must meet the same WCAG 2.2 AA bar as the rest of the product — it is a security-critical announcement, so verify it is perceivable without colour alone and announced to a screen reader; defects routed to `E09-Q04`.

## Performance notes
Record the elapsed time for both drills (lockout-to-recovery, disable-to-full-effect). These are operational latency figures the Owner needs for incident planning, and SR-029's "immediately" needs a measured number rather than an adjective.

## Observability
Confirm the detections the threat model demanded exist and fire: `cv_audit_chain_verified` (nightly verifier), `cv_network_binding_ok` (binding self-check), `cv_auth_lockouts_total`, `cv_authz_denied_total{permission}`, plus the alert routes for chain-verification failure, binding-check failure and break-glass use. A control that works but is undetectable when it fails is recorded as a finding.

title: Publish the auth/RBAC operator runbook and ADR-0010 implementation addendum
body:
## Context
E09 ends with several operational procedures that exist only as scattered knowledge: how to unlock a locked-out manager, how to reset a user's TOTP, what to do when the nightly audit-chain verification fails, what the binding self-check's read-only mode means and how to clear it, and how to read the RBAC matrix artefact when a permission question arises. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires the plan docs to reflect *shipped* behaviour rather than the original proposal, and ADR-0010 was written before implementation — several details (final Argon2id parameters, session cache invalidation strategy, the exact rotation points, the permission vocabulary's generation pipeline) were settled during the epic and are currently undocumented.

This chore closes both gaps so the next person — including the Owner at 2 a.m. during a lockout — has one place to look.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Operator runbook** `docs/ops/runbooks/auth-rbac.md`:
  - Unlock a locked account (SR-016), including the Owner's own account via recovery codes.
  - Reset a user's TOTP as Owner (US-ONB-010) and the step-up it requires.
  - Break-glass for total Owner lockout (SR-023) — the authoritative procedure, cross-linked from `E09-X04`'s corrected version, with its preconditions stated first.
  - Disable a user and what happens downstream (SR-029): sessions, sockets, pending actions, positions decision.
  - Audit-chain verification failure: how to confirm, how to preserve evidence, who to notify, what *not* to do (do not re-run migrations, do not delete rows).
  - Binding self-check failure: what read-only mode disables, how to diagnose the listener binding, how to clear it safely.
  - Reading the RBAC matrix artefact and answering "why was this denied?" using `cv_authz_denied_total` and the audit log.
  - Rotating the fixture/test credentials and the CI secrets used by the auth test suites.
- **ADR-0010 implementation addendum** (appended to `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0010-auth-and-rbac.md` as a dated "Implementation notes" section, not a rewrite of the decision): final Argon2id parameters and the reference host they were calibrated on; the session-cache design and its invalidation points; the enumerated rotation points as implemented; the permission-vocabulary generation pipeline (`tools/rbac/generate.py`) and the contract test that guards it; anything decided during implementation that a future reader would otherwise mistake for an accident.
- **Doc reconciliation**: confirm `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §4/§9.5, `21-database-schema.md` §3.1/§3.10 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1–15.2 match the shipped behaviour; file a ticket for any divergence too large to fix here.
- A changelog fragment for the R0 release notes covering the user-visible auth behaviour.

## Out of scope
- Writing new controls or tests.
- The security review document itself (`E09-X04`) and the QA sign-off (`E09-Q06`) — this chore consumes both.
- Admin screen documentation beyond `SCR-123` invite (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A runbook procedure is executable by someone unfamiliar with it
  Given an engineer who did not build E09 and a staging environment
  When they follow the unlock-a-locked-account procedure
  Then they complete it without asking the author a question
  And every command in the procedure is copy-pasteable and states its expected output

Scenario: The ADR reflects what shipped
  Given the implementation addendum
  When it is compared with the code
  Then the stated Argon2id parameters, rotation points and cache invalidation points match the implementation exactly
  And any decision that changed during the epic is recorded with its reason

Scenario: Failure case - a documented procedure that no longer works
  Given a procedure referencing a command or flag that has since changed
  When the docs check runs during the review
  Then the discrepancy is corrected or the procedure is removed
  And a stale procedure is never left in place as a best guess

Scenario: Edge case - audit-chain failure guidance is safe
  Given the audit-chain verification failure procedure
  When it is reviewed by the Security engineer
  Then it preserves evidence before any remediation step
  And it explicitly forbids destructive actions that would erase the tamper signal
```

## Technical notes / design
Write the runbook in the imperative, one procedure per heading, preconditions first, expected output after every command, and a "stop and escalate" line wherever the operator could make things worse. Break-glass in particular must open with its preconditions (filesystem access to the host plus the KEK) so nobody reads three paragraphs before discovering they cannot proceed.

Keep the ADR addendum additive: ADR-0010's decision stands and is not re-litigated. The addendum records implementation facts and is dated, so a future reader can tell decision from detail.

## Test plan
Documentation, verified by execution: at least the unlock, TOTP-reset and binding-check procedures are executed on staging by someone other than the author, and the run is recorded on the ticket. The break-glass procedure's execution evidence comes from `E09-X04`'s drill and is referenced rather than repeated.

## Security notes
The runbook must contain no secrets, no KEK material, no host addresses and no real credentials — only references to where they live and who may access them. Because it describes recovery paths, it lives in the private repo and is code-owned jointly by Security and Ops; the break-glass section is reviewed by the Security engineer before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — documentation. Where a procedure requires reading a UI state, it names the accessible name of the control rather than only its visual position, so it is followable with a screen reader.

## Performance notes
Record the expected elapsed time for each procedure (from `E09-X04`'s drill measurements) so an operator knows whether a run is going wrong rather than merely being slow.

## Observability
Each procedure names the metric or audit action that confirms it worked (`cv_auth_lockouts_total` dropping, `auth.mfa_reset` written, `cv_network_binding_ok` returning true), so the operator verifies from telemetry rather than from a hopeful click.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/ops/runbooks/auth-rbac.md` merged with all eight procedures.
- [ ] ADR-0010 implementation addendum merged, dated, and matching the code.
- [ ] Three procedures executed on staging by a non-author and recorded.
- [ ] Doc reconciliation completed against the OpenAPI, WS, DB-schema and internal-schema docs; divergences fixed or ticketed.
- [ ] Changelog fragment added for R0.
