title: Break-glass offline owner-recovery CLI (SR-023)
body:
## Context
SR-023 (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.3) requires a documented break-glass path for total Owner lockout: "an offline CLI, runnable only with filesystem access to the host and the KEK, that resets the Owner's TOTP; every use writes an audit event and is loudly surfaced in the UI afterwards". The E09 threat model rates the lockout as U10 and gives the break-glass path its own trust boundary (`docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md` §3.6.1).

The E09-X04 review (#300, PR #2104, finding R-6) found no implementation and no owning ticket. That blocks the R0 area-6 security gate and the E09-X04 break-glass drill (#2494). The owner approved this Story on #1778 (item AB, 2026-10-09).

Placement decision (orchestrator, 2026-10-09, on #2119): the flow lives in `candleviewer.admin`, which C-3.2 already allows to import `secrets`, so there is no new import-linter edge and no ADR (C-3.4). The work waited for the KEK loader from E27-T02 (#835), which is done.

This twin records the DoR package of 2026-10-15 on #2119 (DoR plan and decision record). Orchestrator items R1–R8 are accepted. Owner items O1, O2 and O4 are accepted on an interim basis, subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed): it lists #2119 O1, O2 and O4 among the interim decisions open to veto, and asks the owner for the O3 answer. **O3 stays open with the owner** (see "Live gating" below).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Entry point (R5).** `python -m candleviewer.breakglass`, a thin top-level composition module in the style of `health_wiring.py`. The flow stays in `candleviewer.admin.breakglass`; `secrets` and `audit` are reached only through a factory in `admin.wiring`. Nothing is mounted on cv-api: no HTTP route, WS topic or OpenAPI path reaches break-glass.
- **Preconditions.** All are checked before any change, and the CLI refuses unless every one holds:
  - KEK possession, proven by a new metadata-only `secrets.prove_kek_possession` that refuses `kek_not_enrolled` in every environment (O1). The flow never uses `verify_kek_possession`: that only reflects the state `SecretsService.start` left, and `start` runs `verify_kcv(must_exist=False)`, which enrols an unknown KEK when no rows exist.
  - Host filesystem access: the journal and run lock live at `<dir of CV_AUDIT_WAL_PATH>/breakglass/{journal.wal,instance.lock}`. The CLI refuses unless that directory is absolute, free of `..` and not a symlink (R2a). The check lives in `audit/journal.py`, not in the `settings.py` hotspot.
  - cv-api stopped: cv-api holds a shared flock on the run lock from `AuditService.start` to `stop` and refuses to boot while the CLI holds it (R2b). The CLI also refuses while another session of its database role is connected, probed through `pg_stat_activity` (R2c).
  - An interactive TTY, and a confirmation phrase that the operator retypes.
- **Reset only (O2).** One transaction revokes the named Owner's active MFA methods and sessions with `revoked_reason='break_glass'`, as `reset_totp` does, and inserts a critical, unresolved `system_events` row (`auth` / `break_glass_used`). It runs through a new one-transaction repository, `storage/repositories/break_glass_sqlalchemy.py`, behind an auth port (R4). No login, session or token is minted; the Owner re-enrols TOTP at the next sign-in.
- **Live gating (O3 caveat).** Slices 3 and 4 are built against the ratified rule (ADR-0009 Amendment 1; `docs/plan/spikes/e27-kek.md` §8 ★; KV-E08): in `live` the operator also supplies one unused Owner recovery code, verified offline against its hash and consumed. On top of that, `live` needs `--live` and a typed phrase that names the user and `live`. O3 asks the owner to replace the recovery-code requirement with `--live` and the phrase alone; that call is the owner's. If the owner approves O3 before slices 3 and 4 merge, they leave the recovery-code branch out. If the approval comes later, slice 7 also removes that branch and `test_code_consumed_once_concurrently`, so it ships as a code PR (`feat(auth-rbac)`) rather than `docs(auth-rbac)`. Either way slice 7 amends ADR-0009 Amendment 1, spike §8 and KV-E08.
- **Write-ahead audit (R2d, R3).** `auth.break_glass_attempt` is written before any check, then `auth.break_glass_refused` or `auth.break_glass_reset`. All three are critical, with actor `system:breakglass`. Records go to the host journal and are flushed to `audit_log` before the CLI exits. The boot fold-in carries only refusals journaled while Postgres was down, runs after the main WAL replay, and on corruption raises a critical event without blocking boot. Each action is registered in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits it.
- **Loud surfacing (O4).** While the `break_glass_used` event is unresolved, a client's first `/ws` authentication receives a role-neutral `system` notice (reason `auth.break_glass_used`) after `auth_ok`.
- **No secret output (C-12.6).** Nothing secret is printed, logged or written into audit details: KEK material, TOTP secrets, recovery codes, session tokens or their hashes.
- **Runbook (slice 7).** The break-glass procedure in `docs/ops/runbooks/auth-rbac.md` moves from BLOCKED to runnable. The image entrypoint `candleviewer.server` rejects extra arguments, so the procedure runs the image with `--entrypoint python`, and under compose it needs the durable audit volume from #2615 (R2e).
- **Design records (slice 7).** `docs/plan/spikes/e27-kek.md` §8 and `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md` §3.6.1 are brought in line with the decisions: the entry point is `python -m candleviewer.breakglass` (R5), KEK possession is proven by `prove_kek_possession` (O1), the CLI resets the Owner's MFA and mints no recovery path or login (O2), and it flushes its records to `audit_log` before it exits, so only refusals journaled while Postgres was down fold in at the next boot (R2d).
- **Flag (R7).** No runtime flag. The CLI is dark-launched until slice 5 and every run is audited (C-4.14).

Slice plan (from the DoR plan on #2119). PR titles use the form `feat(auth-rbac): <summary> (E09-S11 k/7)`; slice 7 is `docs(auth-rbac): …`.

| # | Summary | Branch | ~LOC | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | break-glass audit actions, host journal and run lock | `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-audit-journal` | 380 | R1–R3 |
| 2 | offline KEK possession proof without enrolment | `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-kek-proof` | 340 | O1 |
| 3 | single-transaction owner TOTP reset primitive | `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-reset-store` | 390 | R4, O2, O3 caveat |
| 4 | break-glass CLI flow with write-ahead audit and refusals | `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-cli-flow` | 400 | slices 1–3, R5 |
| 5 | break-glass entry point and offline composition | `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-entrypoint` | 330 | slice 4, #2295 (R6) |
| 6 | break-glass notice on the system topic | `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-notice` | 220 | slice 3, O4 |
| 7 | make the SR-023 break-glass runbook runnable | `chore/e09-s11-breakglass-runbook` | 130 | slices 5–6, #2295, #2615 |

Slice 3 ships as one PR, #2682 on `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-reset-store`. It folds the one-transaction reset store (3a) and the reset service with the live recovery-code rule (3b) together under main-orchestrator's PR-cap rule of 2026-10-15 21:53Z, which prefers one PR of up to 800 LOC with a "why this can't be split" note (C-4.8). The plan's branch `feat/e09-s11-breakglass-owner-reset` is superseded and gets no further commits.

## Out of scope
- Password reset, and minting any login, session or recovery token (O2).
- The UI banner that renders the notice: #306 (E10-S04) with CMP-092 and design sign-off (O4).
- The Owner route that resolves a break-glass event: a new Story, E09-S12 (O4; OpenAPI first, step-up, audited). It has no issue yet; filing it is item 2 of #2710.
- The break-glass gauge and its page rule: #2496 (R8). A later comment on #2119 and PR #2660 move them here instead; until main-orchestrator settles that (item 3 of #2710), R8 stands.
- A durable audit volume for the compose `api` service: #2615 (R2e).
- Moving the TOTP and recovery-code keys under the KEK (#2152), and the KEK custody host drill (#2151).
- The online recovery path for holders of recovery codes (#2344).
- The staging drill itself, which stays with E09-X04 (#300) and #2494.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: S1 Break-glass resets the Owner when every precondition holds
  Given cv-api is stopped, the audit dir is absolute, the KEK is enrolled and there is a TTY
  When python -m candleviewer.breakglass --owner <u> runs and the operator retypes the phrase
  Then one transaction revokes the Owner's MFA methods and sessions and writes the critical break_glass_used event
  And the attempt and reset records reach audit_log
  And the CLI exits 0 and prints nothing secret

Scenario (failure): S2 The KEK cannot be proven
  Given the KEK is missing, mismatched, retired or not enrolled
  When the CLI runs
  Then it refuses, writes attempt and refused records, and changes zero rows

Scenario (failure): S3 Host filesystem unavailable
  Given the audit dir is relative or unwritable
  When the CLI runs
  Then it refuses with host_fs_unavailable
  And its records go straight to audit_log if Postgres is up, otherwise the refusal is a documented pre-audit refusal

Scenario (failure): S4 cv-api is running
  Given cv-api is running
  When the CLI runs
  Then it refuses with api_running
  And cv-api does not boot while the CLI holds the run lock

Scenario (failure): S5 The target is not an active Owner
  Given the target user is unknown, disabled or not an Owner
  When the CLI runs
  Then it refuses with not_owner and no rows change

Scenario (failure): S6 Live without its extra gate
  Given the environment is live
  When the CLI runs without --live and the typed phrase, or, while the ratified rule stands (O3), without an unused Owner recovery code
  Then it refuses and nothing is consumed

Scenario (edge): S7 Postgres is down
  Given Postgres is down when the CLI refuses
  When cv-api next boots
  Then the refusal records land in audit_log exactly once and the audit chain verifies

Scenario: S8 No network path reaches break-glass
  Given the cv-api application
  When its HTTP routes, WS topics and OpenAPI paths are enumerated
  Then none of them reaches break-glass

Scenario: S9 The event is surfaced loudly
  Given an unresolved break_glass_used event
  When a client completes its first /ws authentication
  Then it receives the system notice with reason auth.break_glass_used after auth_ok
  And no notice is sent once the event is resolved

Scenario (failure): S10 Crash mid-reset
  Given the CLI crashes during the reset transaction
  Then zero rows change and a failure record is written
  And a re-run succeeds
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Why `prove_kek_possession` (O1).** `SecretsService.start` runs `verify_kcv(must_exist=False)`, which enrols an unknown KEK when no rows exist (`secrets/service.py`, `secrets/_rotation.py`). A break-glass proof must never enrol: it is metadata-only and refuses `kek_not_enrolled` in every environment.
- **Why reset only (O2).** SR-023 says the CLI "resets the Owner's TOTP". A minted login would be a bearer secret on the TTY (C-12.6). `set_mfa_required_reenroll` keeps the lost device's row and is not a `users` column, so it is not the primitive.
- **Why a new repository (R4).** Each existing repository call is its own transaction (`storage/repositories/relational_sqlalchemy.py`), so reusing them cannot put the revokes and the event insert in one unit of work.
- **Why a top-level entry point (R5).** `admin` may not import SQLAlchemy, even indirectly (`.importlinter`), and of the two modules allowed to import `secrets` only `admin` fits; a `candleviewer.auth.breakglass` module would break C-3.2. The 2026-10-09 placement decision holds and needs no ADR (C-3.4). This supersedes the entry-point line in spike §8 and this ticket's original text.
- **Why an anchored directory and a flock (R2).** `CV_AUDIT_WAL_PATH` is relative and created under the working directory (`settings.py`, `audit/wal.py`), and the compose container is `read_only` with only `/tmp` writable, so a `compose run` CLI would take its lock somewhere cv-api never looks. A probe on `application_name` misses idle connections because the name is set with `SET LOCAL`. The alternative to the `pg_stat_activity` probe is an API-held advisory lock (`storage/retention/locks.py`).
- **Re-enrolment (R6).** Login answers 501 for a user with no confirmed, unrevoked MFA method (`auth/login_service.py`), so a reset Owner cannot re-enrol until #2295 lands. Slices 1–4 are unreachable from cv-api and may merge before #2295; slice 5 and Done may not.
- **Order entry and notices (O4).** Order entry keys on reason codes, never on `critical`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 says so when slice 6 lands.
- No migration, OpenAPI change or statechart change (R3). The CLI never runs a statechart interpreter: cv-api is stopped while it runs.

## Security notes
- Threat model: U10 and §3.6.1 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`; KV-E08 in `docs/security/threat-models/E27-accounts.md`; ADR-0009 Amendment 1. Host plus KEK access already amounts to full compromise (§3.6.1, accepted residual risk). KEK possession is only a policy gate until #2152 moves the TOTP and recovery-code keys under the KEK.
- Data classes: TOTP secrets, recovery-code hashes and session hashes are SECRET. The KEK never leaves `secrets` (C-3.2). No secret appears in output, logs or audit details (C-12.6).
- Every run is audited write-ahead, refusals included (C-2.9). No option skips audit.
- Every slice gets a security-reviewer pass; slices that change C-10.2 paths carry the `security-review` label.
